children.text: Bhāskara: Bhagavadāśayānusaraṇabhāsya
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāskara</s>: <s>Bhagavadāśayānusaraṇabhāṣya</s> (Commentary Following the Intent of the Lord)

children.text: Additional Remark
children.translated_text: Additional Remark

children.text:
bhāskarabhāṣyasya prathamapṛṣṭhasya dve vākye
ānandajayatīrthakṛtagītāṭīkāyā uddhṛte /
tayoḥ sāhāyyena bhāskarakṛtagītābhāṣyasya
luptaprathamapṛṣṭhasya viṣayonumātuṃ śakyate /
te vākye
1. śāstraprayojanābhidhāne prastute 'vatāraprayojanābhidhānam asaṃgatam /
2. jñānakarmasamuccayasādhyatvān mokṣasya tatpratipādanāya gītārambhe na dharmādipratipādanārtham /
tadarthānāṃ manvādidharmaśāstrāṇāṃ sanakādiyogaśāstrāṇāṃ ca pratikālaṃ vidyamānatvāt /
jayatīrthaṭīkāyām yad āha bhāskara iti vākyād anantaram upalabhete ime vākye / tatra prathamaṃ vākyaṃ ṣaṣṭhe pṛṣṭhe dvitīyaṃ vākyaṃ navame pṛṣṭhe /
children.translated_text: Two sentences from the first page of <s>Bhāskara's</s> commentary are cited in the <s>Gītā</s> commentary composed by <s>Ānandajayatīrtha</s>. With their help, the subject matter of the lost first page of <s>Bhāskara's</s> <s>Gītā</s> commentary can be inferred. Those two sentences are: 1. When the statement of the purpose of the scripture is being introduced, stating the purpose of the <s>avatāra</s> (incarnation) is incongruent. 2. Since <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is to be accomplished through the combination of knowledge and action (<s>jñānakarmasamuccaya</s>), the <s>Gītā</s> is begun for the purpose of teaching that, not for teaching <s>dharma</s> and the like, since scriptures on <s>dharma</s> by <s>Manu</s> and others, and yoga scriptures by <s>Sanaka</s> and others, exist for each respective purpose in every age. In <s>Jayatīrtha's</s> commentary, these two sentences are found immediately after the words 'thus says <s>Bhāskara</s>.' Therein, the first sentence is on the sixth page, the second sentence on the ninth page.

children.text:
śrībhagavadgītāyā
bhagavadbhāskarakṛtabhagavadāśayānusaraṇābhidhānabhāṣyam /
children.translated_text: The commentary on the blessed <s>Bhagavadgītā</s> called <s>Bhagavadāśayānusaraṇa</s> (Following the Intent of the Lord), composed by the revered <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: (idaṃ hi triṣu lokeṣu mahajjñānaṃ) pratiṣṭitam1 /
children.translated_text: (This great knowledge indeed) is established in the three worlds.

children.text: vistaraiś ca samāsaiś ca dhāryate yad dvijātibhiḥ2 //
children.translated_text: It is maintained by the twice-born in both its extensive and concise forms.

children.text: yodhīte bhārata puṇyaṃ brāhmaṇo niyatavrataḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of steady vows who recites the holy <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: śrāvayec ca mahāpuṇyaṃ tasya dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
children.translated_text: and causes others to hear [this] greatly meritorious [text]—his is the eternal <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: taponiyamam āsthāya3 kṛtam etan maharṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: This was composed by the great sage, having resorted to austerity and discipline.

children.text: tasmān niyamasaṃyuktair adhyeyaṃ4 brāhmaṇair idam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this should be studied by <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are endowed with discipline.

children.text: kṛṣṇaproktam imāṃ5 puṇyāṃ bhāratīm uttamāṃ6 kathām /
children.translated_text: Those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who will cause others to hear this holy, supreme story of <s>Bhārata</s>, spoken by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: śrāvayiṣyanti ye7 viprā ye ca śroṣyanti mānavāḥ //
children.translated_text: and those human beings who will listen to it—

children.text:
ityevamādau8 śrāvayiṣyanti9 ityatra vipragrahaṇād
dvijātīnām evādhyayane10 śravaṇe cādhikāro darśitaḥ /
itareṣāṃ tu ye tu śrośyanti mānavā iti mānavagrahaṇāc chravaṇa
evādhikāraḥ śāstravirodhāc cādhyayane nādhikāraḥ11 /
children.translated_text: Thus, at the beginning, through the use of 'will cause to hear' and the mention of '<s>brāhmaṇas</s>' therein, the qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) for study and hearing has been shown to belong to the twice-born alone. For the others, through the mention of 'human beings' in 'and those human beings who will hear,' the qualification is for hearing only; and because of conflict with the scriptures, there is no qualification for study.

children.text: tathā coktaṃ śukotpattau12
children.translated_text: And thus it is said in the <s>Śukotpatti</s> (birth of <s>Śuka</s>):

children.text: sarvas taratu durgāṇi13 sarvo bhadrāṇi paśyatu14 /
children.translated_text: May all cross over difficulties, may all see auspicious things.

children.text: śrāvayec caturo varṇān kṛtvā brāhmaṇam agrataḥ //
children.translated_text: One should cause [the text] to be heard by [all] four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), placing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> at the head.

children.text:
iti cāturvarṇyamadhyapātinaḥ1 śūdrasya śravaṇamātraṃ
vidhīyate2 /
rāmāyaṇe hy ayam evārtho3 viśeṣeṇa pratipāditaḥ4
children.translated_text: Thus, for the <s>śūdra</s>, who falls within the four <s>varṇas</s>, only mere hearing is prescribed. In the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, this very meaning has been specifically established:

children.text: paṭhaṃ dvijo vāgṛṣabhatvam īyāt5
children.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who recites [it] would attain pre-eminence in speech;

children.text: syāt kṣatriyo6 bhūmipatitvam amīyāt /
children.translated_text: a <s>kṣatriya</s> would attain sovereignty over the earth;

children.text: vaiśyas tathā sarvadhanatvam īyāc
children.translated_text: a <s>vaiśya</s> would likewise attain mastery of all wealth;

children.text: chṛṇvan hi śūdropi7 mahattvam īyāt //
children.translated_text: and even a <s>śūdra</s>, by merely hearing, would attain greatness.

children.text:
ity atretihāsaśravaṇamātram eva śūdrāder nirṇītam8 /
tatrāpi cākhyāyikāmātraśravaṇe9 na tu
rahasyavedāntārthapratipādanapradeśeṣu
sanatsujātīyagītāmokṣadharmādiṣu10 tasya
vedādhyayanaśravaṇatadarthaparijñānatadanuṣṭānānāṃ11
pratiṣedhasmaraṇāt /
tathā ca manusmṛtau
children.translated_text: Thus, in this [passage], for the <s>śūdra</s> and others, only the mere hearing of the <s>itihāsa</s> (epic) has been determined. And even that, [the qualification is] only for hearing the narrative portion, not in passages dealing with the secret meaning of <s>Vedānta</s>—such as the <s>Sanatsujātīya</s>, the <s>Gītā</s>, the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>, and the like—because the prohibition is remembered regarding Vedic study, hearing, comprehension of its meaning, and its practice by him. And thus in the <s>Manusmṛti</s>:

children.text: na śūdrāya matiṃ dadyān nocciṣṭaṃ12 na haviṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: One should not give counsel to a <s>śūdra</s>, nor leftovers, nor the oblation-offering;

children.text: na cāsyopadiśed dharmaṃ na cāsya13 vratam ādiśet //
children.translated_text: one should not teach him <s>dharma</s>, nor prescribe a vow for him.

children.text:
iti cādṛṣṭārthamatidānadharmopadeśādiniṣedhāt14 /
na ca svamanīṣikayā brāhmaṇopadeśam anapekṣya pustakādes
tadvivaraṇād vā tadartham adhigamya karmānutiṣṭhataḥ15
phalāya tad bhavati16 pratyuta17 śāstraniṣiddhenānupanītena18
gṛhītaṃ (śāstrajñāna)m anarthotpādakam /
yato nyāyasmṛtyācārāvirodhī yaḥ padārthaḥ19 sa śāstrārthaḥ /
tatra nyāyaḥ
yathotkṛṣṭanikṛṣṭavarṇayor na (karma) tulya(tā) tathā na
sadṛśadharmatā yuktā / tad uktam
children.translated_text: And [this is] because of the prohibition against giving counsel regarding matters of unseen [spiritual] merit, teaching <s>dharma</s>, and so forth. And for one who, by his own devices, without depending on instruction from a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, comprehends the meaning from books or from commentaries thereon, and performs actions accordingly—it does not yield fruit for him; rather, knowledge of scripture grasped by one who is uninitiated and [acting] against scriptural prohibition produces harm. For that meaning which does not contradict reasoning, <s>smṛti</s> (traditional law), and established practice—that is the meaning of scripture. Regarding this, the reasoning is: just as there is no equality of <s>karma</s> between those of higher and lower <s>varṇa</s>, so equality of <s>dharma</s> is not appropriate. As it is said:

children.text:
apavarge 'dhikāras tu strīśūdrāṇāṃ bhaved yadi /
jātyutkarṣo dvijātīnām anarthāya1 tato bhavet2 // iti /
children.translated_text: If women and <s>śūdras</s> were to have qualification for liberation, then the superior birth of the twice-born would become purposeless.

children.text: smṛtir api
children.translated_text: And the <s>smṛti</s> (traditional law) also [says]:

children.text:
viduṣā brāhmaṇenedam adhyetavyaṃ3 prayatnataḥ /
śiṣyebhyaś ca pravaktavyaṃ4 samyaṅ nānyena kenacit // iti5 /
children.translated_text: This should be studied with effort by a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and it should be properly taught to disciples, by no one else.

children.text:
ācāraś cāryyadeśe jñānaśāstraśravaṇe tasyāpravṛttyaivāveditaḥ
yaḥ śāstravidhim utsṛjya ityādinā cehāpi pratyayasya
pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt / ata evoktam6
children.translated_text: through [the verse beginning with] 'He who, casting aside scriptural injunction...' Therefore it is said:

And the established practice in the noble land (<s>āryadeśa</s>) is known through the very non-engagement of [the <s>śūdra</s>] in hearing knowledge-scriptures. And here too, the means of valid cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) will be demonstrated

children.text: adhikāraṃ vinā yas tu gṛḥṇāti śāstram anyathā7 /
children.translated_text: One who, without qualification, grasps scripture improperly—

children.text: tat tyaktvā8 pāvanaṃ kṛtvā svadharmaṃ punar āśrayet //
children.translated_text: having abandoned that, and having performed expiation, should resort again to his own <s>dharma</s>.

children.text:
pāvanaṃ prāyaścittam /
manunā cādhyayanaśravaṇatadarthānuṣṭhānayuktasyaiva9
dvijāter jñānedhikāro darśitaḥ10
children.translated_text: 'Expiation' means <s>prāyaścitta</s> (penitential rite). And by <s>Manu</s>, the qualification for knowledge has been shown to belong only to the twice-born who is equipped with Vedic study, hearing, and the practice of its meaning:

children.text: adhītya vidhivad vedān putrān utpādya11 dharmataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having studied the <s>Vedas</s> according to rule, having produced sons in accordance with <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: iṣṭvā12 ca śaktito yajñair mano mokṣe niveśayet13 //
children.translated_text: and having offered sacrifices according to one's ability, one should set the mind on <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: tadrahitasya dvijāter api mokṣedhikāro14 noktaḥ
children.translated_text: Even for a twice-born lacking these, no qualification for liberation has been stated:

children.text: anadhītya dvijo vedam anutpādya tathā prajām15 /
children.translated_text: A twice-born who has not studied the <s>Vedas</s>, who has not produced offspring,

children.text: aniṣṭvā caiva16 yajñaiś ca mokṣam icchan vrajaty adhaḥ //
children.translated_text: and who has not offered sacrifices—desiring <s>mokṣa</s>, he goes downward.

children.text:
śūdrasya ca vasiṣṭamunināpy upanayanādibhir asaṃskāryatvaṃ17
pratipāditam /
children.translated_text: And the unsuitability of the <s>śūdra</s> for <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread ceremony) and other <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacramental rites) has been established by the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> as well.

children.text:
tathā ca tatroktam
gāyatryā brāhmaṇam asṛjata triṣṭubhā rājanyaṃ1
jagatyā2 vaiśyaṃ na kenacic chandasā3 śūdram ity asaṃskāryo4
vijñāyata iti /
kiṃ ca bhagavatā sākṣād dharmeṇāpi śāpavaśād
vidurākhyaśūdrajanmanātmajñānaviṣaye dhṛtarāṣṭrapṛṣṭena
śūdrayonisthatvād anadhikāritvaṃ5 manyamānena vedārthopadeśārthaṃ
sanatsujātam ānayatā6 tatrānadhikāro darśitaḥ7 /
tathā ca tenaiva tatroktam
children.translated_text: And thus it is stated there: 'By the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] He created the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, by the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> the <s>kṣatriya</s>, by the <s>Jagatī</s> the <s>vaiśya</s>, and by no meter [did He create] the <s>śūdra</s>'—thus, [the <s>śūdra</s>] is known to be unfit for <s>saṃskāra</s>. Moreover, even by the Blessed Lord <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Vidura</s>) himself—who, due to a curse, was born as a <s>śūdra</s> named <s>Vidura</s>—when asked by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> about self-knowledge, considering himself unqualified because of being situated in a <s>śūdra</s> birth, [<s>Vidura</s>] brought <s>Sanatsujāta</s> for the purpose of teaching the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>, thereby demonstrating the lack of qualification there. And thus he himself stated there:

children.text: śūdrayonāv ahaṃāto nāto 'nyad vaktum utsahe /
children.translated_text: 'Being born in a <s>śūdra</s> womb, I do not venture to speak more than this.

children.text: brāhmīṃ8 hi yonim āpannaḥ suguhyam api yo vadet9 //
children.translated_text: For one who has attained a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> birth may speak even the most secret [teaching].

children.text: na te(na) garhyo devānāṃ tasmād etad bravīmi10 te //
children.translated_text: He is not to be censured by the gods—therefore I tell this to you.'

children.text:
evaṃ ca brāhmaṇayonivyatiriktānyayonijo11 yadi guhyaṃ vedārthaṃ
vadati tadā devādibhir asau garhyate12 niṣiddhasevanena13
pāpayogān narakādau prakṣipyata ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, if one born in a womb other than that of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> speaks the secret meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>, then he is censured by the gods and others; due to the sin of engaging in what is prohibited, he is cast into hell and the like—this is the meaning.

children.text: kumārasya tu yā buddhir veda tāṃ14 śāśvatīm aham /
children.translated_text: 'But I know the eternal wisdom of <s>Kumāra</s> (the eternally youthful one).'

children.text:
kumārasyānujjhitabrahmacaryasya15 sanatsujātasya16 yā buddhir
yaj jñānam17 bodhanaṃ buddhiḥ tām ahaṃ veda /
niratiśayajñānayukto 'sāv iti jātis maratvāj jānāmi18 /
kiṃ tu nikṛṣṭajātisthatvenānadhikārād vaktuṃ na śaknomi19 /
children.translated_text: The wisdom of <s>Kumāra</s>—<s>Sanatsujāta</s>, who has not abandoned his <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship)—that wisdom, meaning knowledge, illumination—I know. He is endowed with unsurpassable knowledge, and due to his birth I know [this]. However, because of my lack of qualification due to being situated in a low birth, I am unable to speak [of it].

children.text: yas te guhyān prakāśāṃś ca sarvān hṛdayasaṃśrayān1 /
children.translated_text: '[<s>Sanatsujāta</s>], the best among all the wise, will speak to you, O great king, all [teachings]—both secret and manifest—that abide in the heart.'

children.text: pravakṣyati mahārāja sarvabuddhimatāṃ varaḥ //

kiṃ bahunā2 sāṅkhyādiśāstreṣv api brāhmaṇānām
evāsuriprabhṛtīnāṃ3 bhagavadbhiḥ4 kapilamunipramukhair mahātmabhir
jñānopadeśaḥ5 kṛto nānyasya /
ity ato 'pi6 na śūdrāder jñāne 'dhikāro 'sti7 /
tasmāt sakaletihāsapurāṇadharmaśāstrādipaurvāparyaparyālocanenāyam
eva8 vākyārtha iti sthitam /
śāstraikasamadhigamyā9 kilādhikāravyavasthā dharmādharmavyavasthāvan
na
pramāṇāntaragamyā /
ko hi nāma bhagavato dharmasya hetuto niścayam avadhārituṃ śaktaḥ10 /
hetutaś ca dharmavyavasthāyāṃ (kariṣyamāṇāyāṃ) hetvanavasthānād
dharmānavasthānam api prasajyeteti /
ataś ca
children.translated_text: In short, even in the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and other <s>śāstras</s>, the instruction of knowledge was given by the great souls, headed by the sage <s>Kapila</s>, only to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> such as <s>Āsuri</s> and others—not to anyone else. Therefore, from this too, the <s>śūdra</s> and others have no qualification for [spiritual] knowledge. Therefore, by considering the sequence of all the <s>itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>dharmaśāstras</s>, and other [texts], this alone is established as the meaning of the statement. For the determination of qualification, like the determination of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, is to be understood solely from scripture and cannot be known through any other means of valid knowledge. For who indeed is capable of ascertaining with certainty the cause of the Lord's <s>dharma</s>? And if the determination of <s>dharma</s> were to be made [merely] on the basis of [rational] causes, then due to the instability of causes, the instability of <s>dharma</s> too would absurdly follow. And therefore:

children.text: striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās te 'pi yānti parāṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: 'Women, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and also <s>śūdras</s>—even they attain the supreme goal.'

children.text: itīdam api liṅgam /
children.translated_text: This too is an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>).

children.text: kiṃ punar brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayas tathā /
children.translated_text: 'How much more so, then, holy <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and devoted royal sages?'

children.text:
ity api
kṛtabrāhmaṇarājarṣiviṣayakapravartakavidhiprarocanārthavādatvena11
draṣṭavyam12 na tu svārthapratipādanaparam /
liṃ gaṃ hi pramāṇāntarataḥ prāptasyaivārthasya13 dyotakaṃ bhavati
nāprāptasyāprāpakam14,15 te 'pi yānti ity
abhidhāyakavartamānakālavācipratyayāntaśabdanirdeśāt16
pūrvoktavidhisāpekṣatvena sākāṅkṣatvāc ca /
vāstavena17 rūpeṇānyaparaṃ yadvākyaṃ18 śabdena
cānyārthapratipādakaṃ
talliṃ gam /
children.translated_text: This too should be understood as an <s>arthavāda</s> (commendatory passage) whose purpose is to encourage the injunctions that pertain to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and royal sages, not as primarily establishing its own [literal] meaning. For an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) illuminates only a meaning already obtained from another means of valid knowledge; it does not bring about what has not been obtained. [This is understood] from the use of the present-tense suffix in the word 'attain' [suggesting an already-known fact], and from its syntactic expectancy dependent on the injunction stated earlier. A sentence that, in its actual form, is directed toward something else, and that, by its words too, conveys another meaning—that is an indicatory mark.

vidhiniṣedhaśeṣatayā tv arthavādānāṃ1 pravṛttiḥ
na tu svārthapratipādakatayā viṣabhakṣaṇādivākyavad2
arthavādavākyānāṃ parārthatvāt svārthe3 tātparyābhāvād4
anyaparatvād vidhivihitārthastāvakatayā5 niṣiddhārthaninditṛtayā6
ca pravṛtter iti7 /
etac ca8 nipuṇataram atraiva9 navame 'dhyāye vakṣyāmaḥ /
anyac ca
children.translated_text: However, <s>arthavāda</s> (commendatory) passages function as subordinate to injunctions and prohibitions, not as establishing their own [literal] meaning—like the statement 'eating poison' and such. Because <s>arthavāda</s> statements are directed toward another [purpose], because there is no primary intention regarding their own [literal] meaning, because they are directed elsewhere, and because they function as praising what is enjoined and censuring what is prohibited. And this we shall discuss more thoroughly in the ninth chapter here itself. Furthermore:

children.text: jñānaṃ vijñānam āstikyaṃ10 brāhmaṃ karma svabhāvajam11 /
children.translated_text: Knowledge, discriminative wisdom, faith—these constitute the <s>brāhmaṇa's</s> <s>karma</s> born of [his own] nature.

children.text:
iti brāhmaṇasyaiva bhagavān dharmaḥ12 śreyaḥsādhanam iti
darśayiṣyati13 /
yato 'dikṛtānām āryyāṇāṃ dvijātīnām eva
śrutivihitanityanaimittikakarmakṣapitakalmaṣamohabhayāyāsānām
upāsyamāna14 eṣa paramātmātigrahanaḥ saṃsāropaplavarahito
'nanto 'kṣayo 'nādir ajo 'manomayo15 nirvikalpo 'pāpaḥ
sarvalokeśa16 eka17 eva sarvaśarīrāvasthitaḥ sarvapadārthāvasthitaḥ
satatā(sā)ditavimalabhāvaḥ sarvaśaktiḥ
svaśaktivibhavajanitasakalādvaitasadrūpaḥ18 pra(tyakṣo) bhavati /
sādhanavīryāt teṣām eva19 hi
śrutismṛtyuktapraśastayamaniyamapramukhayogāṅgādisambhavād
upāsakatvena ca teṣām eva niyamāt ta eva ca20
tam ātmānaṃ paśyanti21 /
tathā cānukramaṇyādāv api22 bhagavatā vyāseno(ktam)
children.translated_text: Thus the Blessed Lord will demonstrate that <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) is the means to <s>śreyas</s> (the highest good) for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> alone. For this supreme <s>Ātman</s> (Self) — beyond the grasp [of ordinary means], free from the calamity of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), infinite, imperishable, beginningless, unborn, not composed of mind, free from conceptual construction, sinless, the one lord of all worlds, abiding in all bodies and all objects, of eternally pure nature, possessed of all powers, whose nature is identical with all non-dual reality produced by the splendor of his own power — becomes directly manifest to the qualified noble ones, the twice-born alone, whose impurities, delusions, fears, and fatigues have been exhausted through the permanent and occasional rites prescribed by <s>śruti</s> (scripture), and who worship him. Through the power of their spiritual practice, since the limbs of <s>yoga</s> (spiritual discipline) beginning with <s>yama</s> (restraints) and <s>niyama</s> (observances), which are praised in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, are possible for them alone, and since the qualification of being worshippers is restricted to them alone — they alone see that Self. And thus also at the beginning of the table of contents, it was stated by the Blessed <s>Vyāsa</s>:

children.text: yat tad yativarā23 muktā24 dhyānayogabalānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those best of ascetics, liberated, endowed with the power of meditation and <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: pratibimbam ivādarśe25 paśyanty ātmany avasthitam //
children.translated_text: see [the Self] established in the <s>Ātman</s>, like a reflection in a mirror.

children.text: yad akṣaraṃ vedavido1 vadanti (viśanti) yad yataro vītarāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>Veda</s> speak of the imperishable, which the dispassionate ascetics enter —

children.text:
ityādinā viśiṣṭajātīyāśramiviṣaye dhānenātmopalambhanam
upapannaṃ2 bhavatīti pradarśitam /
children.translated_text: thus it has been shown that through meditation, the attainment of the Self is appropriate specifically for those of distinguished birth and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life).

children.text: nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogam āyāsam āvṛtaḥ3 /
children.translated_text: 'I am not manifest to all; I am covered by <s>yogamāyā</s>' (Gītā 7.25) —

children.text:
iti bhagavān eva śūdrāder ātmadarśanābhāvaṃ4 pratipādayiṣyati5 /
dvaipāyano 'pi6
children.translated_text: thus the Blessed Lord himself will establish the absence of Self-realization for the <s>Śūdra</s> and others. <s>Dvaipāyana</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) also [says]:

children.text: śāntātmāno dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ7 prāpnuvanti tadakṣaram8 iti /
children.translated_text: 'The foremost among the twice-born, whose selves are at peace, attain that Imperishable.'

children.text:
ataḥ śūdrader dhyānādinā9 kriyamāṇenāpi na tatprāptir bhavati10
niyamavidher bhaṃ gabhayād akhilavidyāyā11 adhikṛtānuṣṭhitāyā12
(eva) phaladātṛtvāvagamāt /
avihitena tūtkṛṣṭajātīyakarmaṇā13 yogena jñānena14 ca
śūdrādir utkarṣa15 netuṃ na śakyate /
na hi kārṣṇāyasaṃ16 bhūyo 'py analasantāpanena suvarṇatvam
āpādayituṃ śakyam17 /
kriyā hi dravyaṃ vilāpayati18 nādravyam /
vedasmṛtiliṃ gebhyaḥ19 kila brāhmaṇasyaiva mukhyayā vṛttyā
mokṣādhikāro 'vagamyate na kṣatriyavaiśyayoḥ
yogābhyāsādhikāre saty api20 /
tad uktam
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though meditation and such practices are performed by the <s>Śūdra</s> and others, there is no attainment of that [Self] for them, because of the understanding, derived from the force of the restrictive injunction, that only knowledge performed by the qualified yields fruit. Through unauthorized performance of actions belonging to a higher caste, or through <s>yoga</s> and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), a <s>Śūdra</s> and others cannot be elevated to a higher state. For just as iron, no matter how much it is heated in fire, cannot be made into gold, so too action melts [only] a substance, not a non-substance. From the <s>Veda</s> and <s>smṛti</s> texts, it is understood that only the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has primary eligibility for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), not the <s>Kṣatriya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s>, even though they have eligibility for the practice of <s>yoga</s>. Thus it is said:

children.text: bandhamokṣavyavasthityāṃ pramāṇaṃ codanā svataḥ /
children.translated_text: In the determination of bondage and liberation, the injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is the self-sufficient authority;

children.text: vedasyānatiśaṅkyatvād anapekṣatayā tathā //
children.translated_text: because the <s>Veda</s> is beyond doubt and is independent.

children.text: vidhir niyuṅkte 'dhikṛtam uttamaṃ1 śreyase sadā /
children.translated_text: The injunction always directs the qualified, the highest, toward <s>śreyas</s> (the supreme good);

children.text: aśāstrīyāt phalāsaṃ gāt svayaṃ kāmī hi badhyate1 //
children.translated_text: one who acts on his own desire, without scriptural basis, is bound due to the absence of [legitimate] fruit.

children.text: apunarjanmasambandho yasmāc chabdaikagocaraḥ2 // iti /
children.translated_text: 'For the state of non-return is accessible only through scripture' — thus [it is said].

children.text:
yat tu rājarṣīṇāṃ janakaśvapatipravāhaṇaprabhṛtīnāṃ
mahābhā(ra)tādau mokṣaśravaṇaṃ tat kasyāñcid viśiṣṭāyām
avasthāyāṃ pravṛttayāgatvena yajamānānāṃ tu
mantrāptasambodhāvirbhāve3 sati na sarvadā /
yāgasthānāṃ hi teṣāṃ brāhmaṇatvaṃ śrūyate / tathā ca
śatapathaśrutiḥ
children.translated_text: As for the hearing of teachings about <s>mokṣa</s> by royal sages (<s>rājarṣis</s>) such as <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Śvapati</s>, <s>Pravāhaṇa</s>, and others in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and elsewhere — that occurred in a special circumstance, through the arrival of [exceptional] engagement, and for sacrificers, upon the manifestation of the awakening attained through <s>mantras</s>, but not always. For when they are in the position of performing sacrifice, they are spoken of [in <s>śruti</s>] as possessing <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> status. And thus the <s>Śatapatha</s> scripture [states]:

children.text: sā yāṃ4 kāñcana yajate5 brahmaiva bhūtvā yajata iti /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever performs sacrifice, sacrifices having become <s>Brahman</s> itself.'

children.text: tadvadhe ca smṛtau brahmahatyāprāyaścittam āmnātam6
children.translated_text: And regarding the killing of such a person [a Kṣatriya engaged in sacrifice], the <s>smṛti</s> prescribes the expiation for <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brāhmaṇa):

children.text: yāgasthakṣatriyaṃ hantā cared brahmahaṇivratam7 iti /
children.translated_text: 'One who kills a <s>Kṣatriya</s> while he is engaged in sacrifice should observe the vow for killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.'

children.text:
evaṃ ca kṣatriyavaiśyayor api na tathā brāhmaṇena tulyatayā
mokṣe 'dhikāraḥ tasmād dvijātīnām eva8 /
yogābhyāsena tu prayatamānānām apy anadhikṛtānāṃ
śūdrādīnāṃ vidyamāne hṛdayapuṇḍarīke 'pi9
(nādhikāraḥ) tiraścām iveti / kiṃ ca yathā saura āloko
divācarāṇāṃ
eva bhūtānām ākṣaṃ10 janayati na tu rātricaraṇāṃ kauśikādīnāṃ
tulye 'pi prakāśadātṛtve tadvat /
children.translated_text: Thus, even for the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s>, there is not equal eligibility for <s>mokṣa</s> as for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; therefore [eligibility belongs] to the twice-born alone. And for those who are not qualified — the <s>Śūdras</s> and others — even though they make effort through the practice of <s>yoga</s>, even though they possess the lotus of the heart, they have no eligibility, just as animals do not. Moreover, just as sunlight produces vision only for creatures that move by day, not for nocturnal creatures like owls and the like, even though the capacity to give light is the same — so it is.

children.text:
yad ayaṃ samudāyārthaḥ11 garbhādhānādisaṃskārasaṃskṛto yo
yathāvidhyupanīto12 yathāśakticīrṇavedavratādiko
'rthāvabodhaparyantavedādhyayanasaṃskṛto gṛhād vanaṃ
vanān maunam āśramāṇāṃ samuccayam
aṅgīkṛtya vikalpe vā brahmacaryād yathāruci śānto13

dāntaḥ1 śraddadhānaḥ so 'pavarge 'dhikārabhāk yataḥ sūtrakāraḥ
svadharmāṇāṃ vidhyarthatvaṃ na manyate3
children.translated_text: self-controlled, faithful — he is the one eligible for <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). Since the author of the <s>sūtras</s> does not consider the prescribed duties (<s>svadharmas</s>) to be merely means-to-an-end, [but rather says]:

children.text: karmaṇāṃ sahakāritvaṃ sahaiveti śruter matam /
children.translated_text: The auxiliary nature of actions is accepted from scripture as being 'together with' [knowledge];

children.text: na hy anāśramiṇo4 vedo yogyatvam iha manyate //
children.translated_text: for the <s>Veda</s> does not consider one who does not belong to any <s>āśrama</s> as eligible here.

children.text: devopakāraḥ kartavyo5 devān bhāvayateti ha /
children.translated_text: 'Service to the gods must be performed' — 'nourish the gods' — thus [it is said];

children.text: ataḥ
children.translated_text: therefore:

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ prakurvīta6 svakarmāṇi yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: 'One should perform one's own duties according to the prescribed rules throughout life;

children.text: saṃskurvīta svadharmaiś ca smṛtito 'vagataṃ7 tathā //
children.translated_text: and one should purify oneself through one's own <s>dharmas</s>, and also [follow] what is understood from <s>smṛti</s>.'

children.text:
mahāyajñaiś ca yajñaiś ca aṣṭāv ātmaguṇā8 iti
catvāriṃśat saṃskārā9 iti ca /
api (ca) saṃyatānām eva10 yajñādayaś ca śrūyate11 /
tattvaprakaraṇe12 kila
children.translated_text: 'Through the great sacrifices and [other] sacrifices, the eight qualities of the self' — thus [it is said]; 'the forty <s>saṃskāras</s>' — thus also [it is said]. Moreover, it is heard [in <s>śruti</s>] that sacrifices and the like are only for those who are self-controlled. Indeed, in the section on fundamental principles:

children.text: vidyayāśramiṇo yogo nānyasyeti śruter matam //
children.translated_text: 'The <s>yoga</s> of knowledge belongs to one in an <s>āśrama</s>, not to another — this is the view from scripture.'

children.text:
karmaṇā tasya vijñānaṃ13 tadbhāvam upanīyate14 /
paścād āpannatadbhāvo14 deham etaṃ vimuñcati16 // iti /
children.translated_text: 'Through <s>karma</s>, one's consciousness is led to that state; afterward, having attained that state, one abandons this body.' Thus [it is said].

children.text:
tathā cātra vājasaneyināṃ yajñasūtrakāraḥ
kātyāyano 'dhikāravivekam uktavān17
athāto 'dhikāraḥ (iti) /
athaśabda ānantaryārthaḥ / ataḥśabdo18 hetvarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'atha' (now) has the meaning of sequence. The word 'ataḥ' (therefore) has the meaning of reason.

children.text:
yato vedādhyayanaṃ pūrvavṛttam atas tadarthajñānāvasare
prathamam adhikāro nirūpyate
kasyātrādhikāra19 iti /
adhikāraśabdasyaiva tāvat
children.translated_text: Since Vedic study has preceded, at the occasion for understanding its meaning, eligibility is first determined — [the question being] 'Who has eligibility here?' Now, regarding the very meaning of the word 'eligibility' (<s>adhikāra</s>):
And here, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, the author of the ritual <s>sūtras</s> of the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, has stated the distinction regarding eligibility: 'Now, therefore, [we discuss] eligibility.'

children.text: ko 'rthaḥ1 ayam ucyate
children.translated_text: What is the meaning? This is said:

children.text:
abhyupagatāgamaprāmāṇyānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ śāstreṇa
yady asya kartavyatayā vidhīyate tatra
tasyāgamapāratantryeṇānuṣṭhānāṅgīkaraṇam2 /
tathā yac chāstreṇa3 niṣidhyate na kalañjaṃ bhakṣayet4
ityādi tatra pratiṣidhyamānakriyasya mukhyasyādhikāriṇo5
jighatsāprayuktarāganibandhanaḥ
kalañjabhakṣaṇapravṛttiniṣedhārthaḥ6
śāstrapāratantryeṇaiva7 /
akāraṇasaṅkalpa audāsīnyāśrayaṇaṃ8 cādhikāraḥ /
tad uktaṃ bhaṭṭena9
children.translated_text: For persons who have accepted the authoritativeness of scripture, when something is enjoined by the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) as something to be done, then, being subordinate to scripture, they accept its performance. Likewise, what is prohibited by scripture — 'one should not eat <s>kalañja</s> [garlic]' and so forth — there, the prohibition is addressed to the primary qualified person, one who is impelled by desire and appetite toward eating <s>kalañja</s>, with the purpose of prohibiting such activity, solely through subordination to scripture. And eligibility also [means] the adoption of an attitude of indifference, without purposeless volition. Thus it was stated by <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [<s>Kumārila</s>]:

children.text: vidhinā yujyate yatra na hanyān na pibed iti /
children.translated_text: 'Where one is enjoined by an injunction — "one should not kill," "one should not drink" —

children.text: tatraudāsīnyavastv eva pratipattāvalambane //
children.translated_text: there the object of comprehension is simply indifference [i.e., abstention].'

children.text:
audāsīnyaṃ pravṛttyuparamo10 vyāpārābhāvaḥ svāmitvena
yo vyāpārasyādhikāras tasyābhāva11 ity uktaḥ /
tenaitad uktaṃ bhavati ---
idam agnihotrādi karma matsambandhitayā12 vihitam ato mama kartavyam /
idaṃ ca parahiṃsādi tathaiva niṣiddham ato na kartavyam iti
brāhmaṇādir avagacchati13 /
eṣa adhikāraśabdārtha14 iti / tad uktam ---
children.translated_text: Indifference means cessation of activity, absence of engagement; it is called the absence of that mastery which is eligibility for action. Thus what is stated amounts to this: 'This <s>agnihotra</s> and other <s>karma</s> (ritual action) is prescribed as connected with me; therefore I must perform it. And this — violence toward others, etc. — is likewise prohibited; therefore I must not do it' — thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and others understand. This is the meaning of the word <s>adhikāra</s> (eligibility). Thus it is said:

children.text:
yatra yasyādhikāro 'sti15 nitye naimittike ca saḥ /
badhyate na hi sarvo hi16 śāstrātikramabandhanaiḥ // iti /
children.translated_text: 'Where one has eligibility — in the permanent and occasional [rites] — he is bound; for not everyone is bound by the bonds of transgressing scripture.'

children.text:
śāstradṛṣṭyādhikāro nirūpyata ity atra17 niyojyatvaṃ tāvad
āha18 brāhmaṇarājanyavaiśyānāṃ19 śrutiḥ20 /
tathā ca ---
children.translated_text: Eligibility is determined from the perspective of scripture — here, as for who is the one to be enjoined, <s>śruti</s> speaks of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Rājanyas</s> (Kṣatriyas), and <s>Vaiśyas</s>. And thus:

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: NOTES:

children.text:
1. kārthaḥ
2. pārataṃ jeṇānuṣṭānāṅgī^
3. yachāstreṇa
4. bhakṣayetyādi
5. ^kriyormukhasyādhikāraṇo
6. ^bhukṣaṇa ... ^dhārthaṃ
7. ^pārataṃśaiṇa^
8. saṅkalpaḍaukādāsīnyā^
9. bhaddena
10. pravṛnni upa^
11. vyāpārasyodhikāra^
12. satsambandhitayā
13. ^rivagacchatīti
14. rāṣodhi^
15. ^adhikaro^
16. ta rva nahi^
17. kātradiśyādhikāro nirūpyata ityatra
18. niyojyāstāvadā^
19. ^caiśyānāṃ
20. śruteḥ

children.text:
vasante1 brāhmaṇenādhyeyo2 grīṣmo rājanyena3 śaradi
vaiśyena iti śrutiḥ /
kiṃ ca aṅgahīnāśrotriyaṣaṇḍapatitaśūdravarjam4 ity
aṅgahīnānām andhamūkapaṅgvādīnām
ājyāvekṣaṇopasthānavacanaviṣṇukramaṇādiṣv
asāmarthyāt karmaṇi nādhikāraḥ5 /
aśrotriyasya sāṅgavedādhyayanavijñānarahitasya6
yathāvac chāstrānavabodhe mantrāṇāṃ devatādisatattvānagamād
anadhikāraḥ7 /
uktaṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: 'In spring, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should begin study; in summer, the <s>Rājanya</s>; in autumn, the <s>Vaiśya</s>' — thus says <s>śruti</s>. Furthermore, 'excluding those with deficient limbs, non-learned [in Veda], eunuchs, the fallen, and <s>Śūdras</s>' — for those with deficient limbs such as the blind, mute, lame, and so forth, there is no eligibility for ritual action due to their inability to perform the gazing at ghee, attending, reciting, the strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the like. For one who is not a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned in Veda) — one who lacks the study and knowledge of the <s>Veda</s> with its limbs — because of not properly understanding the scripture, and because of not grasping the true nature of the deities of the <s>mantras</s> and so forth, there is no eligibility. And it is said:

children.text:
vaidhe kṛtārthakaṃ śāstram avaidhaṃ nānuśāsti9 hi / iti /
ṣaṇḍasya10 klībasya pūrvajanmārjitaduṣṭakarmasūcakatvena11
duṣkṛtitvād anadhikāro dāyādivibhāgapratiṣedhāt tasya12
karmaṇāṃ13 ca dravyādisādhyatvād vibhavayuktasya14 putriṇa
ādhānādisaṃyogāt15 klībasyāputriṇo nādhikāraḥ16 /
tathā coktam
children.translated_text: 'Scripture that follows the prescribed [rules] is authoritative for the properly [performed]; what is not prescribed does not instruct.' For the eunuch — because his condition indicates evil <s>karma</s> accumulated in a previous birth, because he is a wrongdoer, because of the prohibition of his share in inheritance — and since <s>karmas</s> require material means and the like, and since the performance of <s>ādhāna</s> (setting up the sacred fires) and such requires a son, the eunuch, being without a son, has no eligibility. And thus it is said:

children.text:
patitavyādhiśūdrāṇāṃ17 yāvad vacanam iṣyate18 /
adhikāro na sarvasmin namuceḥ ṣaṇḍakasya19 ca // iti /
children.translated_text: 'For the fallen, the diseased, the <s>Śūdras</s>, up to [the extent of their] speech, eligibility is granted; but not in everything — nor for the impotent or the eunuch.'

children.text:
patito brahmahādiḥ20 / tasyānadhikāro mahāpātakitvāt /
śūdrasya cānadhikāraḥ21 / kuto 'thātaḥśabdābhyāṃ
vedādhyayanānantaryadyotakābhyāṃ22 yasya vedādhyayanaṃ
tasya karmaṇy adhikāra iti jñāpitatvāt /
karmādhikṛtasya ca jñāne 'dhikāro jñānena karmaṇaḥ
samuccayanāt /
tathā coktam23 ---
children.translated_text: The 'fallen' refers to one who has committed <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing of a Brāhmaṇa) and such [great sins]. His ineligibility is due to being a great sinner. And the <s>Śūdra</s> has no eligibility. Why? Because the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ,' indicating the sequence after Vedic study, convey that one who has studied the <s>Veda</s> has eligibility for ritual action. And one who has eligibility for <s>karma</s> has eligibility for <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) as well, since <s>jñāna</s> is to be combined with <s>karma</s>. And thus it is said:

children.text: niḥśreyasāyādhikṛtān1 vidyā karma vyabodhayat2 /
children.translated_text: Knowledge and action instructed those entitled to the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>);

children.text: ... ... karmaśrutir evānuśāsti3 tān // iti
children.translated_text: ... the injunction of [ritual] action itself instructs them. Thus.

children.text:
tasmāc chūdro yajñe 'navakḷpta iti4 tasya karmaparyudāsād5
mūrkhatvāc ca / mūrkhatvaṃ ca
tasyopanayanavedādhyayanatadarthādhigamapratiṣedhāt6 /
tathā ca gautamaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>śūdra</s> is not ordained for the sacrifice — because of the exclusion of [ritual] action for him and because of his ignorance. And his ignorance is due to the prohibition against his <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), study of the <s>Veda</s>, and comprehension of its meaning. And thus <s>Gautama</s> [states]:

children.text: śūdraś caturtho varṇa ekajātir na ca saṃskāram arhati / (iti)
children.translated_text: 'The <s>śūdra</s> is the fourth <s>varṇa</s> (class), once-born, and does not merit the <s>saṃskāra</s> (sacramental rite).'

children.text:
tathā
athāsya7 vedam upaśṛṇvatas trapujatubhyāṃ8 śrotrapratipūraṇam
udāharaṇe jihvocchedo9 dhāraṇe hi śarīrabheda10 iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'And for him who listens to the <s>Veda</s> — his ears are to be filled with molten tin and lac; if he recites it, his tongue is to be cut out; if he memorizes it, his body is to be split.'

children.text: vaśiṣṭo 'py āha11
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> too says:

children.text:
padyur vā eṣa śmaśānaṃ yac chūdras tasmāc chūdrasamīpe
nādhyetavyam12 iti /
children.translated_text: 'This one may defile even the cremation ground who is a <s>śūdra</s>; therefore one should not study in the vicinity of a <s>śūdra</s>.'

children.text:
na cānadhikṛtena13 kṛtaṃ karma śāstrapratyayaṃ phalaṃ
sampādayitum arhati śāstralakṣaṇatvāt
phalasambandhasyotkarṣāpakarṣayoś
ca /
uktaṃ ca
children.translated_text: And action performed by one who is not entitled does not merit the production of a fruit warranted by scripture, because the connection with the fruit has the nature of scriptural [entitlement], and because of degrees of superiority and inferiority. And it is said:

children.text: avaidhatvād anagnitvān nādhikāro 'sti14 karmasu /
children.translated_text: Because of not being scripturally ordained and not maintaining the sacred fires, there is no entitlement to [ritual] actions;

children.text: śrauteṣv avaidhatāpy asya15 vedādhyayanavarjanāt //
children.translated_text: and his lack of scriptural ordination in <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) rites is due to the prohibition of Vedic study.

children.text: yaḥ svādhyāyam adhīyīta kuryāt karma16 sa e(va) tat /
children.translated_text: He alone who studies the sacred recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>) and performs the ritual action — he [is entitled to] that;

children.text: avaiduṣyād ataḥ śūdraḥ17 karmaṇaḥ18 paryudasyate //
children.translated_text: because of lack of learning, therefore the <s>śūdra</s> is excluded from [ritual] action.

children.text: kiṃ sarvebhyaḥ na /
children.translated_text: Is [the exclusion] from all [rites] or not?

children.text: smārtaṃ1 ca pitṛyajñādiṃ śūdraḥ kuryād yathāśrutam2 /
children.translated_text: The <s>śūdra</s> may perform <s>smārta</s> (rites based on <s>smṛti</s>) such as the <s>pitṛyajña</s> (ancestor-worship) and such, as heard [in tradition];

children.text: tad vidvattām avāptyaiva3 kathañcid dvijasaṃśrayāt //
children.translated_text: having somehow attained some learning through association with the twice-born.

children.text: śrautād adhikṛtānāṃ tu4 yāvadvihitasevanāt /
children.translated_text: But for those entitled to <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) rites, through the observance of what is enjoined,

children.text: niṣiddhavarjanāc cāpi pāramparyeṇa sadgatiḥ5 //
children.translated_text: and through the avoidance of what is prohibited — through successive [births], a good destination [is attained].

children.text: hīnād dhīnāc chubhaṃ6 janma pāramparyeṇa yad abhavet7 /
children.translated_text: From a lower and still lower [birth], the good birth that may come about through succession —

children.text: anugrahaḥ sa eṣo 'sya8 puṃsaḥ śrutikṛto9 mataḥ //
children.translated_text: that is considered as the favor bestowed upon the person by scripture.

children.text:
tasmāc chūdrādīnāṃ10 karmaṇy anadhikārād asmin śāstre
etatpratipādite ca yogābhyāse nāsty adhikāra11 iti /
kiṃ ca
children.translated_text: Therefore, because <s>śūdras</s> and others have no entitlement to [ritual] action, in the practice of <s>yoga</s> taught in this scripture, there is no entitlement [for them]. Moreover:

children.text: ātmābhyāso 'pi nāsyāsti12 vipraseveti hi smṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: Self-contemplation too is not available to him, because of the <s>smṛti</s> injunction 'service to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>';

children.text: teṣām evānukampeti dvijāter adhikāritā //
children.translated_text: it is out of compassion toward them [that the teaching exists] — therefore the entitlement belongs to the twice-born (<s>dvijāti</s>).

children.text: teṣām evetiśabdena13 brāhmaṇasya stutiḥ kṛtā14 /
children.translated_text: By the word 'eva' (alone) in 'of them alone,' praise of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is made;

children.text: śūdrayonāv ahaṃāta ityādi bahu dṛśyate //
children.translated_text: much is seen [in scripture] such as 'I was born in a <s>śūdra</s> womb' and so forth.

children.text:
evamādi bahuvākyajātaṃ15 bhārate tatra tatra dṛśyate
granthagauravabhayāt tu na likhyata16 iti /
uktaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Such a large body of passages is seen here and there in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, but is not written [here] out of fear of prolixity. And it is said:

children.text: adhikāry eva śāstrārthaṃ17 śaktaḥ sādhayituṃ yataḥ /
tatsiddhāv aprabhutvaṃ hi jñātātrānadhikāritā // iti18 /
children.translated_text: for the inability to accomplish that is recognized as the non-entitlement. Thus.
Only the entitled person is capable of accomplishing the purpose of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture);

itthaṃ śūdrāder mokṣābhāvād dharmārthakāmalakṣaṇe1 trivarge
ca puruṣārthe sati hīnādhikārād gītāśāstrādes tenādhyayanādi2
na kartavyam / yasmād yo yatrānadhikṛtaḥ sa tadiṣṭabuddhyāpi3
children.translated_text: should not be undertaken. Because whoever is not entitled to something,

children.text:
(anutiṣṭhan) na kevalaṃ tatphalaṃ na prāpnoti yāvad apareṇa
pratyavāyenāpi yujyate /
yathā rājādinā yaḥ kutracid apy aniyuktaḥ puruṣaḥ sa
tadīyagrāmādau svātantryeṇa4 grāmavyāpārādi kurvaṃs tasmād
rājādeḥ5 śarīradhanadaṇḍādilakṣaṇaṃ6 pratyavāyaṃ7 prāpnoti
tathā śāstre 'pi yo yatrānadhikṛtas tadiṣṭārtham api8 kurvan
pratyavaiti / yathā ca ślaiṣmikahitam auṣadhaṃ bhakṣayann
ārogyārthaṃ
paittiko nairujyaṃ na labhate pratyuta9 rogaprakopeṇa pīḍyate
evam ihāpi boddhavyam10 /
uktaṃ ca
children.translated_text: even performing that with the intention of desiring its result — not only does he not obtain that fruit, but he is also afflicted with a counter-result (<s>pratyavāya</s>). Just as a person who has not been appointed by a king or such to any [office], acting independently in village affairs and such in the king's village — he receives from that king a counter-result in the form of punishment to the body and property. Likewise, in scripture too, whoever performs something for which he is not entitled, even though he desires its result — he suffers a counter-result. And just as a person of <s>pitta</s> (bilious) constitution, eating medicine beneficial for a <s>kapha</s> (phlegmatic) constitution for the sake of health, does not obtain freedom from disease but rather is afflicted by the aggravation of his illness — so too should it be understood here. And it is said:

Thus, since liberation is not available to the <s>śūdra</s> and others, and since in the group of three human aims (<s>trivarga</s>) characterized by <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, they have inferior entitlement — from the <s>Gītā</s> scripture and such, study and the like by them

children.text: paryudasto hi yo yasmāc chāstrīyād api karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who is excluded from even a scriptural action,

children.text: sa tatrānadhikārī11 syād dānādau dīkṣito yathā12 //
children.translated_text: he would be non-entitled to that — like one who has undergone <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) with respect to gifts and such.

children.text:
evaṃ cādhikṛtenānuṣṭhitaṃ13 karma phalasādhakaṃ na
svabuddhyaivānadhikṛteneti14 śāstraniyamaḥ /
etac ca bhagavān eva vakṣyati
children.translated_text: Thus, action performed by the entitled person produces fruit, not [action performed] by the non-entitled person by his own understanding alone — this is the rule of scripture. And the Blessed Lord himself will say:

children.text: yaḥ śāstravidhim utsṛjya15 vartate kāmakārataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who, abandoning the injunction of scripture, acts according to his own desire —

children.text: na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ16 gatim //
children.translated_text: he attains neither perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.'

[Page 15]

children.text: yataḥ
children.translated_text: Because:

children.text:
pratiṣedham atikramya pratyaveyāt kṛtān naraḥ1
tasmāt tasyānatikrāntau nityaṃ2 yuktataro bhavet // iti /
children.translated_text: 'A person who, transgressing the prohibition, would suffer a counter-result — therefore, in not transgressing it, he would always be more proper.' Thus.

children.text:
yataḥ kila sarveṇa
puruṣeṇāvihitānuṣṭhānapratiṣiddhasevananimittajanitapāpahetukavividhanarakarauravāsipatravanakrakacacchedanaśvaśṛgālādikṛmikīṭabhakṣaṇavedanāpūyaśoṇitakardamamajjanādiyāmyayātanāśatādyanarthasaṅkaṭādisantrāsāc
charaṇaiṣiṇā3
sthāvarakīṭapataṅgādiyonisahasrāvartabhramaṇasadyomaraṇajarāvyādhikṣutpipāsābandhanāṅgacchedādiduḥkhabhayocchedakāri4
śāstrīyaṃ karmānuṣṭhīyate5 /
tat punar utkṛṣṭaṃ karma niṣiddhatvād viruddhaṃ6
sadgatānugatikatvenādṛṣṭabuddhyānuṣṭhīyamānam
apy avihitatvenāśāstrīyatvān na7 kevalaṃ
niṣphalaṃ bhavati yāvat pratyutānadhikṛtatvena8 pratyavāyakaratvāt
paraloke9 bahuvidhanarakapātādyupadravavṛndotpādakam iti10
jñātvā śūdrādinā naivātra nityam ātmā11 kṣapaṇīyaḥ /
tathā cehaiva12 vakṣyati
children.translated_text: Since indeed every person, out of terror of the dire calamities — the hundreds of torments of <s>Yama</s>'s punishments such as immersion in mud of pus and blood, the pains of being devoured by dogs, jackals, worms, and insects, the cutting by saws in the forests of sword-leaves (<s>asipatra</s>), the terrible and frightful hells (<s>raurava</s>) and such, caused by sins generated from performing what is not enjoined and resorting to what is prohibited — seeking refuge, performs scriptural action to cut off the fear of sufferings such as death and birth, old age and disease, hunger and thirst, bondage and dismemberment and such, [involved in] revolving through thousands of births in the species of plants, insects, moths, and so on; that superior action, being prohibited [for the non-entitled] and thus contrary, even when performed with invisible [meritorious] intent following the conduct of the virtuous, being not enjoined and therefore non-scriptural — not only is it fruitless, but rather, because of the counter-result arising from non-entitlement, it produces a multitude of misfortunes in the next world such as falling into various hells — knowing this, the <s>śūdra</s> and others should never torment themselves here. And [the Lord] will say here in this very [text]:

children.text: varaṃ svadharmo viguṇaḥ13 paradharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt /
children.translated_text: 'Better is one's own <s>dharma</s>, though imperfect, than another's <s>dharma</s> well performed;

children.text: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhyāvahaḥ14 //
children.translated_text: death in one's own <s>dharma</s> is better; another's <s>dharma</s> is fraught with danger.'

children.text: varaṃ śreyan / darśayati ca manur api
children.translated_text: 'Better' means 'preferable.' And <s>Manu</s> too demonstrates:

children.text: paradharmeṇa jīvan hi sadyaḥ patati jātitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who lives by another's <s>dharma</s> immediately falls from his caste.'

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text: śūdrajātito 'pi bhraṣṭas tiryagādijātiṃ prāpnotīti vākyārthaḥ1 /
children.translated_text: Even from the <s>śūdra</s> caste, one who has fallen attains rebirth in the animal and other species — this is the meaning of the statement.

children.text: vede mantreṣu gṛhyeṣu2 śrutismṛtiniṣedhataḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Veda</s>, in the <s>mantras</s>, in the <s>gṛhya</s> [sūtras] — because of the prohibition by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>,

children.text: nādhikāro 'sti śūdrasya purāṇādiṣu3 bhārata //
children.translated_text: the <s>śūdra</s> has no entitlement to the <s>Purāṇas</s> and such, O <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text:
brāhmaṇaṃ tu puraskṛtya4 śṛṇvataḥ phalam īritam /
striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrāḥ śuddhāḥ sukham avapnuyuḥ5 // iti /
children.translated_text: But with a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> placed at the head, the fruit for one who listens has been declared: women, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>, if purified, may attain happiness. Thus.

children.text: yataḥ
children.translated_text: Because:

children.text: tiryagbhyaḥ6 puruṣāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ7 kāryākāryavivekataḥ8 /
children.translated_text: Humans are superior to animals because of the discrimination between what should and should not be done;

children.text: tantrādhikārāt tebhyo 'pi9 dvijā vedādhikārataḥ //
children.translated_text: the twice-born are [superior] even to them because of entitlement to the <s>śāstra</s> (systematic treatises), because of entitlement to the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text:
adhikā(rā)t pravacane tebhyaḥ śreṣṭhā dvijottamāḥ /
śrutyā smṛtyādhikārārthaṃ śraiṣṭyam eṣāṃ prakāśate10 // iti /
children.translated_text: Because of entitlement to authoritative teaching, superior to them are the best among the twice-born (<s>dvijottamāḥ</s>); the superiority of these [<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>] is manifested by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> for the purpose of [establishing] entitlement. Thus.

children.text: tathā ca manuḥ
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Manu</s> [states]:

children.text: brāhmaṇo jāyamāno hi pṛthivyām adhijāyate /
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, by his very birth, is born supreme upon the earth,

children.text: īśvaraḥ11 sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmako(śa)sya guptaye //
children.translated_text: the lord of all beings, for the protection of the treasury of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text:
tad evam uktasambandhābhidheyaprayojanaṃ12
pratipāditādhikāraviśeṣam
etacchāstraṃ vyākhyātuṃ13 śrotuṃ ca14 yogyam iti /
ato 'sya vyākhyānam ārabhyate15 /
children.translated_text: Thus, having the connection (<s>sambandha</s>), subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), and purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) as stated, and having the specific entitlement (<s>adhikāra</s>) established — this scripture is fit to be expounded and heard. Therefore, the exposition of it begins.

children.text:
anekaiś ca vyākhyātṛbhiḥ svapakṣanikṣiptadṛṣṭibhir
itas tataḥ16 kṛṣyamāṇam anavasthām āpadyamānaṃ gītāśāstram
apavargaprāptyupadeśamahāprayojanam17 /
(ataḥ) bhagavato 'bhiprete sanmārge sthāpayitum ayaṃ yatnaḥ kriyate18 /
children.translated_text: And this <s>Gītā</s> scripture — which has the great purpose of teaching the attainment of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), but which has been dragged here and there by many commentators with vision confined to their own positions, and has thus fallen into an unsettled state — effort is now made to establish it in the correct path intended by the Blessed Lord.

children.text:
nanv itihāsapurāṇānāṃ pauruṣeyatvād apavargaprāptilakṣaṇe
'tīndriyārthe1 na svataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ sambhavati /
satyam etat /
kiṃ tu mantrārthavādās teṣāṃ2 mūlam iti nyāyavidbhiḥ sthāpitam3 /
atas tetra4 mūlaṃ syuḥ
children.translated_text: Now, since the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> are of human authorship (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), regarding the supra-sensory matter (<s>atīndriyārtha</s>) characterized by the attainment of liberation, they cannot possess intrinsic validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>). This is true. However, it has been established by those versed in logic (<s>nyāya</s>) that <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages) are their source. Therefore, those [<s>smṛtis</s>] have their source there —

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ5 viprakīrṇānāṃ vedajñātṛprayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: The compilation of <s>dharmas</s> scattered about, through the effort of those who know the <s>Veda</s>,

children.text: kṛtaṃ saṃharaṇaṃ6 sākṣād dharmāvagatihetukam //
children.translated_text: was made — directly being the cause for the understanding of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: vaidikānāṃ (hi) śabdānāṃ prasthānāt tu vilakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: But distinct from the system of Vedic words,

children.text: smṛtīnāṃ racaneyaṃ7 hi puṃpraṇītā vilakṣaṇā8 //
children.translated_text: is this composition of the <s>smṛtis</s>, for it is distinct, being composed by [human] persons.

children.text:
bhagavadvyāsādismaraṇaṃ9 ca svataḥ prāmaṇam eva /
te hi sākṣātkṛtadharmatvāt karatalagatāmalakavat sakalaṃ vedārthaṃ
pratyakṣeṇaiva paśyanti10 /
tad uktam sākṣātkṛtadharmāṇa ṛṣayo babhūvur iti /
na hy asmadādivad vyāsādayo 'tīndriyam arthaṃ na paśyantīti vaktuṃ
śa(kyam11) /
vidhūta(ka)lmaṣatvād īśvarānugrahād vedārthasya12 vopanibandhanāc ca
sambhavaty evatīndriyārthadarśanaṃ13 teṣām ity adoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the recollection of the Blessed <s>Vyāsa</s> and others is itself a valid means of knowledge. For they, having directly realized <s>dharma</s>, perceive the entire meaning of the <s>Veda</s> by direct perception alone, as clearly as a myrobalan fruit in the palm of the hand. As it is said: 'The <s>ṛṣis</s> were those who had directly realized <s>dharma</s>.' For it cannot be said that <s>Vyāsa</s> and others, like ourselves, do not perceive supersensible objects — since due to the destruction of their impurities, by the grace of the Lord, and because of their exposition of the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, the perception of supersensible objects is indeed possible for them. Hence there is no fault.

children.text:
itthaṃ sthite 'rjunasya jñānakarmopadeśaprasaṅgam avatārayituṃ
prastutakathāsamāptau kāryāntaraṃ jijñāsur dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ14
punaḥ sañjayaṃ pṛcchaṃs tāvad āha15
children.translated_text: This being so, in order to introduce the occasion for the teaching of knowledge and action to <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, wishing to know further developments at the conclusion of the current narrative, again asking <s>Sañjaya</s>, first says:

children.text: dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre sarvakṣtrasamāgame /
children.translated_text: On the field of <s>dharma</s>, on <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, when all the warriors had assembled,

children.text: māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvata sañjaya // BhG_1.1 //
children.translated_text: what did my [sons] and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> do, O <s>Sañjaya</s>? (BhG 1.1)

children.text: he sañjaya kurukṣetrākhye deśe dharmaprasavahetutvād dharmasya
children.translated_text: O <s>Sañjaya</s>, in the region called <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, [which is] the field of <s>dharma</s> because it is the cause of the production of <s>dharma</s>,

kṣetre sthāne sarvakṣatrasamāgame sannidhāne sati
matsanbandhinas tanayāḥ pāṇḍuputrāś ca kim akurvata kim
anuṣṭhitavanta
iti /
pūrvaṃ1 rājaṛṣiṇā tapasyatā tatra dharmaḥ kilopta iti
kurukṣetrasya dharmakṣetratvam2 / atra kurutāto dharmaṃ3 kṣipraṃ
trāṇo bhaviṣyatīti kurukṣetrasya kurukṣetratvam ity āhuḥ
paurāṇikāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (those learned in the <s>Purāṇas</s>). (1)

in that field, that place, when all the warriors had gathered together — what did those connected with me, i.e. my sons, and the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> do, what did they perform? Thus [the question is asked]. It is said that formerly, a royal sage, while performing austerities there, planted <s>dharma</s> — hence <s>Kurukṣetra</s>'s designation as the 'field of <s>dharma</s>.' Also, 'practice <s>dharma</s> here and you will quickly be protected' — thus <s>Kurukṣetra</s> has its designation as <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, say

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sañjaya4 uvāca
children.translated_text: Thus questioned, <s>Sañjaya</s> said:

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ5 duryodhanas tadā /
children.translated_text: Seeing the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> arrayed, <s>Duryodhana</s> then,

children.text: ācāryam upasaṅgamya rājā vacanam abravīt // BhG_1.2 //
children.translated_text: approaching the teacher (<s>Ācārya</s>), the king spoke these words: (BhG 1.2)

children.text:
pāṇḍavasainyaṃ vyūḍhaṃ śāstradṛṣṭyā kṛtavinyāsaviśeṣaṃ6
dṛṣṭvaiva7 tasmiṃ kāle duryodhano droṇam upasaṅgamya gauravāt
tatsamīpaṃ8 prāpya vakṣyamāṇaṃ9
children.translated_text: having reached his proximity, [spoke] what is about to be stated —

children.text: viśiṣṭapadakriyāparikalpitarūpaṃ10
children.translated_text: a sentence of a form constructed with distinguished words —

children.text: vākyam uktavān // 2 //
children.translated_text: he spoke the following statement. (2)

Having seen the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army arrayed — arranged in a special formation as prescribed by the science [of warfare] — at that very time, <s>Duryodhana</s>, approaching <s>Droṇa</s>, out of respect,

children.text: tadāha
children.translated_text: Then he said:

children.text: paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇām ācārya mahatīṃ11 camūm /
children.translated_text: Behold this great army of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, O teacher,

children.text: vyūḍhāṃ12 drapadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā // BhG_1.3 //
children.translated_text: arrayed by the son of <s>Drupada</s>, your wise disciple. (BhG 1.3)

children.text:
he ācārya pāṇḍuputrasambandhinīṃ13 camūṃ mahatīṃ14
senām aṅgabāhulyād vistīrṇāṃ15 dhṛṣṭadyumnena
vyūhavidhānakuśalena16 ca vyūḍhāṃ kṛtacaranāviśeṣāṃ
(paśya) /
yo hi bhavacchiṣyo buddhimāṃś ca so 'vaśyam17
children.translated_text: O teacher, behold the army belonging to the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> — a great force, extensive due to its many divisions — arrayed by <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, who is skilled in the arrangement of formations, and arranged in a special battle order. For he who is your disciple and intelligent will inevitably

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. pūrva
2. kurukṣatrasya dharmakṣatratvam
3. ataś ca kurutātra dharma
4. pṛṣṭaṃ ssañjaya^
5. vyuḍaṃ
6. ^sainye vyuvaṃ śāstradṛkṣmākṛta^
7. dṛṣṭaiva
8. gauravātnatsamīpa
9. vakṣyamāṇa
10. ^rupaṃ
11. pāṃḍatrāṇāṃ ........ mahatī
12. vyūḍhān
13. ^sambandhinī
14. mahantī
15. byahulyā hi stīrṇāṃ
16. byūha^

vyūharavanāṃ karotyataḥ

children.text: apratimāṃ vyūharacanāṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: compose a matchless arrangement of formations.

children.text: ataḥ pratividhānaparo1 bhavetyāśayaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the intention is: you should be occupied with counter-measures. (3)

children.text: kiṃ ca
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi /
children.translated_text: Here are heroes, great archers, equal to <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> in battle —

children.text: yuyudhāno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ2 // BhG_1.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yuyudhāna</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, and <s>Drupada</s>, the great chariot-warrior. (BhG 1.4)

children.text:
atra asyāṃ senāyām amī3 śūrā bhayaviṣādān abhijāḥ4 /
tathā maheṣvāsāḥ5 /
iṣavaḥ śarā asyante kṣipyante6 yais ta iṣvāsāḥ koḍaṇḍāḥ7
mahānto bṛhantaḥ sudṛḍhāḥ parair abhedyā
iṣvāsā dhanūṃṣi yeṣāṃ te maheṣvāsāḥ /
atha vā yuddha iṣūn asyantītīṣvāsā dhānuṣkāḥ
(yuddha)karmaparāḥ8 /
ta eva ca divyāḥ prabhāvattvād dhanur vedakṛtābhiyogatvād
anekasaṅgrāmalabdhavijayatvāc ca9 /
mahānta uttamāḥ praśastāḥ /
tathā yudhi yuddhe bhīmārjunābhyāṃ yoddhṛtvena10 samās tulyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Also, equal to <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> in prowess in battle.

children.text: ke ta ity āha yuyudhānaḥ sātyakiḥ virāṭo11 drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who are they? He says: <s>Yuyudhāna</s>, i.e. <s>Sātyaki</s>; <s>Virāṭa</s>; and <s>Drupada</s>, the great chariot-warrior.

children.text: mahān preraṇāvaraṇayuddhāpasāraṇāvakāśādidharmayogāt12
children.translated_text: A great [warrior], praiseworthy by virtue of possessing the qualities of driving forward, blocking, fighting, retreating, making room, and the like —

children.text: praśasto ratho yasyāsau mahārathaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: whose chariot is such is a <s>mahāratha</s> (great chariot-warrior). (4)

Here, in this army, these are heroes — those born without fear or dejection. Also, great archers: arrows (<s>iṣu</s>) are shafts that are thrown, those [weapons] from which they are thrown are <s>iṣvāsa</s> (bows); great, large, very firm, unbreakable by enemies are the bows of those who are <s>maheṣvāsa</s> (great bowmen). Alternatively, those who shoot arrows in battle are <s>iṣvāsa</s> (archers), devoted to the art of battle. They are also divine, because of their power, because of their training in the science of archery, and because of victories won in many battles — great means excellent, praiseworthy.

children.text: kiṃ ca
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: dhṛṣṭaketuś cekitānaḥ13 kāśirājaś ca vīryavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, <s>Cekitāna</s>, and the valorous king of <s>Kāśī</s>,

children.text: purujit kuntibhojaś ca14 śaibyaś ca narapuṅgavaḥ // BhG_1.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Purujit</s>, <s>Kuntibhoja</s>, and <s>Śaibya</s>, the bull among men. (BhG 1.5)

children.text:
1. ^vicāna^
2. mahārarthaḥ
3. senāyāsamī^
4. mayaviṣāda^
5. maheṣāsāḥ
6. arayante kṣipyate
7. ṣaiste draghāsāḥ kodaṃḍāḥ
8. mahānto vṛhantaḥ sudavāḥ paraisamedhā^ dhanuṣi .... te tathā
yuddhādraṣṭūnasyantītīṣvāsā dhānukāḥ karmaraparā
9. prabhāvatvā .... dekasaṃ^
10. yoddhatvena
11. yuyudhānastātyakirvirāṭo^
12. mahānpraraṇāvaraṇā yuddhāpasārāvakāśādidharmayogāt
13. cekitān
14. kuntibhojaiśca
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
iha sañjñāmātrapradhānā amī śabdā nigadavyākhyā(tāḥ)1 /
(tāḥ) ato na vyākhyāyogyāḥ /
yeṣāṃ tv arthānugame viśeṣa upalabhyate te leśato vyākhyāyante2 /
kāśīnāṃ rājā (vīryavān) utsāhaśaktyupetaḥ6 /
puru bahu jayatīti purujit / kuntayo janapadāḥ teṣāṃ vāsī4
children.translated_text: He who conquers (<s>jayati</s>) much (<s>puru</s>) is <s>Purujit</s>. The <s>Kuntis</s> are a people; [the king] who resides among them

children.text: (kuntibhojaḥ) / śivayo janapadās teṣāṃ rājā5 (śaibyaḥ) /
children.translated_text: is <s>Kuntibhoja</s>. The <s>Śibis</s> are a people; their king is <s>Śaibya</s>.

children.text: sa ca śauryādyuttamaguṇayogān narapuṅgavaḥ puruṣaśreṣṭhaḥ6 // 5 //
children.translated_text: And he [is called] <s>narapuṅgava</s> (bull among men), i.e. the best among men, because of possessing excellent qualities such as valor and the like. (5)

Here, these words, being primarily mere proper names, are explained by simple glossing. Therefore they do not require [detailed] explanation. However, those where a particular [meaning] is perceived in understanding the sense are briefly explained. The king of the <s>Kāśīs</s> [is] valorous — endowed with the power of effort.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Also:

children.text: yudhāmanyuś ca7 vikrānta uttamaujāś ca vīryavān /
children.translated_text: <s>Yudhāmanyu</s>, the valiant, and <s>Uttamaujas</s>, the powerful,

children.text: saubhadro draupadeyāś ca sarva eva mahārathāḥ // BhG_1.6 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Subhadrā</s>, and the sons of <s>Draupadī</s> — all of them great chariot-warriors. (BhG 1.6)

children.text: vikrānto vīryavān subhadrāsūnur abhimanyuḥ8 // 6 //9
children.translated_text: The valiant, powerful one; the son of <s>Subhadrā</s> is <s>Abhimanyu</s>. (6)

children.text:
evaṃ pāṇḍavānīke pradhānanāyakanirddeśaṃ10 kṛtvā svānīke
pradhānanāyakān darśayann āha11
children.translated_text: Having thus indicated the chief leaders of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army, now showing the chief leaders of his own army, he says:

children.text: asmākaṃ tu12 viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha13 dvijottama /
children.translated_text: But know those who are distinguished among us, O best of the twice-born,

children.text: nāyakān mama sainyasya14 sañjñāarthaṃ tān bravīmi te15 // BhG_1.7 //
children.translated_text: the leaders of my army — I name them to you for identification. (BhG 1.7)

children.text:
asmākaṃ ye viśiṣṭāḥ kulaśauryādibhiḥ16 pradhānās tān
sañjñārthaṃ bravīmi17 /
sañjñānaṃ sañjñā / tuśabdaḥ18 pūrvebhyo
children.translated_text: Identification (<s>sañjñāna</s>) is <s>sañjñā</s>. The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) indicates a distinction from the

children.text: viśeṣāvadyotanaḥ19 /
children.translated_text: preceding [warriors].

children.text: yuyudhānādayo varākā yuṣmākaṃ purato 'kiñcitkarā20 ity arthaḥ // 7
children.translated_text: The meaning is: <s>Yuyudhāna</s> and the others are wretches, insignificant before you. (7)
Those who are distinguished among us — pre-eminent by lineage, valor, and the like — I name them for the purpose of identification.

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. śabdā .... vyakhya
2. eṣāṃ tvārhānunamaḥ kaścidulabhyate .... vyākhyāyate
3. utsāhaśatsupetaḥ
4. janapadastamājas vāmī
5. janapadaistasya rājā
6. sauryadu ... yogānnapugava puruṣaśreṣṭhaḥ
7. vudhānyuśca
8. ^sūnubhimanyuḥ
9. aṅkoyam darśayannāha asmātparaḥ vidyate
10. ^nideśaṃ
11. svākhāneke pradhānāndarśayannāha
12. lu
13. nivodha
14. maṃ daunyasya
15. sañjñārthaṃ tān
16. cauryādibhiḥ
17. bravimi
18. sañjñā na sañjñā tu śabdaḥ
19. viśeṣāvaṣvotnā
20. kiṃ titkarā ity arthaḥ
21. aṅkoyaṃ parigaṇayannāha asmātparosti
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: tāś ca parigaṇayann āha
children.translated_text: And enumerating those, he says:

children.text: bhavān1 bhīṣmaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaḥ śalyo jayadrathaḥ3 /
children.translated_text: Your lordship, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Śalya</s>, <s>Jayadratha</s>,

children.text: aśvatthāmā4 vikarṇaś ca saumadattiś ca5 vīryavān // BhG_1.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, <s>Vikarṇa</s>, and the valorous son of <s>Somadatta</s>. (BhG 1.8)

children.text: na kevalam ete yāvat
children.translated_text: Not only these, but also:

children.text: anye 'pi bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ6 /
children.translated_text: And many other heroes who have abandoned their lives for my sake,

children.text: nānāśastrapraharaṇā nānāyuddhaviśāradāḥ7 // BhG_1.9 //
children.translated_text: wielding various weapons, skilled in various forms of combat. (BhG 1.9)

children.text:
nānāprakārāṇi cakrāsimuśalagadāprabhṛtīni (śastrāṇi)
praha(ra)ṇāni yeṣāṃ te tathā /
nānāvidhagajarathāśvādiyuddhakriyāsu paṇḍitā matkārye ca
tyaktajīvitā. santy evānye // 9 //8
children.translated_text: Those whose striking weapons are various kinds — discs, swords, pestles, maces, and so forth — they are such. And those who are learned in various kinds of battle-craft involving elephants, chariots, horses, and the like, and who have abandoned their lives for my cause — there are indeed many others. (9)

children.text:
evam ubhayasainyanāyakanirdeśaṃ kṛtvā sārāsāratāṃ
nirūpayann āha
children.translated_text: Having thus indicated the leaders of both armies, now assessing the relative strength and weakness, he says:

children.text: aparyāptaṃ tad asmākaṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam /
children.translated_text: That strength of ours, protected by <s>Bhīma</s>, is insufficient;

children.text: paryāptaṃ tv idam eteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam // BhG_1.10 //
children.translated_text: but this strength of theirs, protected by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, is sufficient. (BhG 1.10)

children.text:
asmākaṃ yathānirdiṣṭasaṃhatānāṃ10 tatpāṇḍavabalam
aparyāptam asamartham abhibhavitum yato bhīmābhirakṣitam
bhīmasenena pradhānabhūtena guptam /
sa ca (bhīmo) bhīṣmāpekṣayā kiñcin nyūnatara ity abhiprāyaḥ11 /
idaṃ tv asmākaṃ balam eteṣāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ paryāptam
abhibhavāya vināśane samartham ity arthaḥ12 yato bhīṣmābhirakṣitam13
/
bhīṣmas tv anekaśastrāstrapārago nirjitānekamahāsamara ityāśayaḥ14
//
children.translated_text: That army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> is insufficient — unable to overcome us who are united as described — because it is protected by <s>Bhīmasena</s>, who is the chief [protector]. And that <s>Bhīma</s> is somewhat inferior compared to <s>Bhīṣma</s> — this is the purport. But this army of ours is sufficient — capable of overcoming, i.e. destroying, these <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> — because it is protected by <s>Bhīṣma</s>. And <s>Bhīṣma</s> is one who has mastered many weapons and <s>astras</s>, who has won numerous great battles — this is the intent.

children.text:
1. mavān
2. kaṇaśca
3. jayadrathaḥ
4. aśvasyāmā
5. saumardanniśca
6. śūrādarthe tyaktā jīvitāḥ
7. viśāradāḥ
8. aṅkoyam nirūpayannāha asmāt parosti
9. valaṃ
10. ^sahitānāṃ
11. kiñcintyūnatara iti ābhiprāyaḥ
12. pāṇḍavāmāṃ paryāsamābhibhavāya vināśane sarmarthamity arthaḥ
13. ^rakṣitaṃ
14. bhīṣmosvanekaśāstrāśsrapāragonekanirjitamahāsamara ityāśayaḥ
15. aṅkoyam āha asmāt parosti
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: pradhānanirdeśaparyojanam āha
children.translated_text: He states the purpose of indicating the chief [warriors]:

children.text: anyeṣu tu sarveṣu yathābhāgam avasthitā(ḥ) /
children.translated_text: Therefore, stationed in your respective positions in all the divisions,

children.text: bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi // BhG_1.11 //
children.translated_text: all of you must protect <s>Bhīṣma</s> alone. (BhG 1.11)

children.text:
hi yasmād evambhūtena bhīṣmeṇābhirakṣitam asmākaṃ balaṃ
pāṇḍavānāṃ parābhave paryāptam /
tato 'yaneṣu sarveṣu rathamārgarathyāsu sarvāsu
yathābhāgam /
yo yo bhāgo yathābhāgam /
yo yasyātmīyo bhago 'ṃśaḥ (sa tena) rakṣyaḥ1 /
tatra avasthitāḥ santo bhavanto bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantv2 iti
tasmin nāyake3 sarvato gupte balaṃ parabalapraṇāśane4 kṣamaṃ
bhavatītyāśayaḥ / yady asminn iti5 (?) ayanaṃ kakṣyādi // 11 //
children.translated_text: Since (<s>hi</s>) the army of ours, protected by <s>Bhīṣma</s> of such stature, is sufficient for the defeat of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, therefore, in all the other divisions — in all the chariot-paths and roads — [stationed] in your respective positions — whichever position is one's own share, that should be guarded by him. Being thus stationed, all of you should protect <s>Bhīṣma</s> alone — the intent is that when that leader is guarded from all sides, the army becomes capable of destroying the enemy's force. 'Divisions' [means] the flanks and so forth. (11)

children.text: idānīṃ6 kāryāntaram upakṣipati sañjayaḥ7
children.translated_text: Now <s>Sañjaya</s> introduces a further development:

children.text: tasya sañjanayan harṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Generating joy in him, the grandfather, the eldest of the <s>Kurus</s>,

children.text: siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ8 dadhmau pratāpavān // BhG_1.12 //
children.translated_text: roaring a lion's roar loudly, blew his conch — that illustrious one. (BhG 1.12)

children.text:
tasya prakrāntasya balasya duryodhanasya vā9 harṣam utpādayan
bhīṣmaḥ kurūṇāṃ tatkālajānāṃ pūrvavayāḥ
siṃhanādam ucchair vinadya10 tataḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau /
siṃhasya iva nādaḥ siṃhanādaḥ taṃ vinadya /
sāmānyanader viśeṣanadiḥ11 karma / siṃhanādaṃ kṛtvety arthaḥ // 12
//
children.translated_text: Generating joy in that advancing army, or in <s>Duryodhana</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s> — the eldest among the <s>Kurus</s> born at that time — having roared a lion's roar loudly, then blew his conch. A roar like that of a lion is a lion's roar; having sounded that — the specific roar is the object of the general sounding. The meaning is: having made a lion's roar. (12)

children.text: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ12 /
children.translated_text: Then conches, kettledrums, tabors, drums, and cow-horns

children.text: sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat // BhG_1.13 //
children.translated_text: were sounded all at once, and that sound was tumultuous. (BhG 1.13)

children.text:
anantaraṃ śaṅkhādayaḥ sahasaivāvicāritaniyantraṇam eva
abhyahanyanta13 tāḍitāḥ /
sa ca vāditrasaṅghātajaḥ śabdas tumulo mahān
children.translated_text: Immediately thereafter, the conches and the rest were sounded all at once, struck without deliberation or restraint. And that sound, born from the aggregate of instruments, was tumultuous, great,

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. yasyātmīyoṃso bhāgo rakṣyaḥ
2. bhoṣmame^
3. ttasminnāyake
4. ^praddarśane
5. yatyasmimniti
6. idānnī
7. kāryātaramupāṅkṣipati saṃyayaḥ
8. vinadyoścaiḥ saṅkhān
9. calasya duryodhanasyā vā
10. kuruṇāṃ .... siṃhanādasuścaurvitaghaṃ
11. samānya^
12. paṇavānaka^
13. śaṅkhāyāḥ sahasaivādhicāritaṃ niryatraṇamevābhyahanyata
children.translated_text: [Variant readings:] 1. Whose own portion is to be protected. 2-13. [Manuscript variants for preceding text.]

children.text:
avibhāvyamānāvayavavivekaḥ
śrotṛhṛdayadāraṇo 'bhavat1 / bheryaḥ kātvāḥ (?)
ānakastamisvā (?) gomukho 'nalambakaḥ2 (?) // 13 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The sound, whose component parts could not be distinguished, was heart-rending to the listeners. [Instruments:] drums, kettledrums, <s>ānakas</s>, <s>gomukhas</s>, and <s>analambakas</s>. // 13 //

children.text: tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau /
children.translated_text: Then, standing in the great chariot yoked with white horses,

children.text: mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś caiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ // BhG_1.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s> and the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> blew their divine conch-shells. // BhG 1.14 //

children.text:
mādhavapāṇdavau divyaikarathārūḍhāvacintyaprabhāvau
śaṅkhāvatyarthaṃ5 dhmātavantau // 14 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Mādhava</s> and the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, of inconceivable power, mounted on a single divine chariot, blew their conch-shells with great force. // 14 //

children.text: atha pradhānaśaṅkhanāmanirddeśam āha6
children.translated_text: Now he states the names of the principal conch-shells:

children.text: pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> blew <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s> blew <s>Devadatta</s>.

children.text: pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ7 // BhG_1.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛkodara</s> (Bhīma), the doer of fearsome deeds, blew the great conch <s>Pauṇḍra</s>. // BhG 1.15 //

children.text: anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro8 yudhiṣṭhiraḥ /
children.translated_text: King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the son of <s>Kuntī</s>, blew <s>Anantavijaya</s>.

children.text: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau // BhG_1.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s> blew <s>Sughoṣa</s> and <s>Maṇipuṣpaka</s>. // BhG 1.16 //

children.text:
pauṇḍraṃ (puṇḍra)deśajaṃ vipulaṃ vṛkodaro dīptāgnyudaro9
bhīmakarmā bakahiḍimbādirākṣasavidāraṇādīni bhīṣaṇāni
karmāṇi yasya (saḥ) / kuntīputragrahaṇaṃ praśaṃsārtham /
pitur asaṃvijñāne mātrā vyavadeśo yady api kutsā10 rādhāsutasyeva
children.translated_text: When the father is unknown, designation by the mother, though sometimes a reproach — as in the case of the 'son of <s>Rādhā</s>' —

children.text: tasya punaḥ saṃvijñāne praśaṃsaiva11 dharmaputratvād
children.translated_text: in his case, when the father is known, it is indeed praise, because

children.text: yudhiṣṭhirasya12 //13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> is the son of <s>Dharma</s> (Righteousness). // 15-16 //

[Commentary:] <s>Pauṇḍra</s> — produced in the <s>Puṇḍra</s> region, large. <s>Vṛkodara</s> — one whose belly has blazing fire. 'Doer of fearsome deeds' — one whose deeds are fearsome, such as the destruction of the <s>rākṣasas</s> <s>Baka</s>, <s>Hiḍimba</s>, and others. The use of 'son of <s>Kuntī</s>' is for the purpose of praise.

children.text: kiṃ ca tathā
children.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: kāśyaś ca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Kāśī</s>, a supreme archer, <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, a great warrior,

children.text: dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ // BhG_1.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, and the unconquered <s>Sātyaki</s>, // BhG 1.17 //

children.text:
1. mahānavibhāvyamāmāvayavavivekaḥ śrottrtṛdayāruṇobhavat
2. gomukhonalavaṅkaḥ
3. śveteha^
4. pāṃḍavāścaiva
5. diyyaikaratharuṭāvacintyaprabhāvau śaṃvyau^
6. ^nāmunirdeśa^
7. karmārvṛkodaraḥ
8. kutīputra
9. dīptāgyadaraḥ
10. yatyukutsā
11. savijñāne praśaṃseva
12. dharmaputrātvāghradhiṣṭirasya
children.translated_text: [Variant readings for preceding text.]

children.text:
pāñcālaś ca1 maheṣvāso draupadeyāś ca pañca ye /
saubhadraś ca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak (pṛthak) // BhG_1.18
children.translated_text: The prince of <s>Pāñcāla</s>, a great archer, and the five sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, and <s>Saubhadra</s> (Abhimanyu), the mighty-armed — all blew their conch-shells separately. // BhG 1.18

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Sātyaki</s>, unconquered in battles — this should be understood. // 18 //
