children.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ3 hṛdayāni vyadārayat4 /
children.translated_text: That tumultuous sound pierced the hearts of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>'s sons,

children.text: nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ5 caiva tumulo vyanunādayat // BhG_1.19 //
children.translated_text: and made both heaven and earth resound. // BhG 1.19 //

children.text: yathoktaśaṅkhaghoṣas tumulo6 duryodhanādīnāṃ hṛdayāny abhinad7
bhinnavān / yato nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ caiva8 sakalam iva
children.translated_text: It split them. Because it made heaven and earth, as if the entire universe,

children.text:
vyanunādayat pratiśabddayuktam akārayat vyanunadanaṃ prayuktavān /
vyanunādayad ity atra vyatyaye 'nāḍabhāvaḥ9 /
ihasthānam apadānāṃ10 nirvacanaṃ granthagauravabhayān na11 kṛtam /
yeṣāṃ ca śabdānām iha lakṣaṇānugamo na dṛśyate teṣāṃ virodho
nodbhāvanīyaḥ /
yataḥ paramarṣiṇā dvaipāyanenaivoktam alaṅkṛtaṃ śubhaiḥ śabdair
children.translated_text: resound with echo — it produced resounding. The irregular form 'vyanunādayat' here follows the rule of substitution. The etymological analysis of words in this passage has not been given, out of concern for the weightiness of the text. And for those words whose forms here do not follow standard grammatical rules, no contradiction should be raised, since the supreme sage <s>Dvaipāyana</s> (Vyāsa) himself has said: 'Adorned with auspicious words.'

children.text: iti / atas tad āgamād evāvagamyate śubhaśabdatve12 vyākaraṇānāṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, from that very authority it is understood that the words are auspicious. And given the multiplicity of grammars, how is it proper to raise a contradiction based on <s>Pāṇini</s>'s grammar alone?

children.text:
bahutve ca kathaṃ pāṇinīyena kevalena virodha udbhāvayituṃ yuktaḥ13 /
itihāsādīnāṃ vaidikārthapratipādanāc chandastulyatvam14 /
tathā cānenaivoktam15 idaṃ hi devasammitam16 pavitram idam uttamam iti
kārṣṇavedam idaṃ puṇyam iti17 / tathā anyatrāpi coktam
children.translated_text: Since the <s>Itihāsas</s> and other texts teach Vedic meaning, they are equal to the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedas). And thus he himself has said: 'This is equal to the gods,' 'This is supremely sacred,' 'This is the <s>Kṛṣṇa-Veda</s>, this is meritorious.' And elsewhere too it is said:
[Commentary:] The tumultuous sound of the conch-shells described above shattered the hearts of <s>Duryodhana</s> and others.

atha śaṅkhaghoṣād anantaram arjuno duryodhanādīn5
(vyavasthitān) vividhenākāreṇa6 yathāvibhavam avasthitān
dṛṣṭvā śastrāṇāṃ sampāte pravṛtte dhanur utkṣipya
sāvadhāno hṛṣīkeśam idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ vākyam āha /
hṛṣīka(m) itīndriyagrāmākhyā tadīśaṃ7 hṛṣīkeśam iti /
he mahīpata iti dhṛtarāṣṭrodbodhanaṃ sañjayena8 // 20 //9
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Then, after the sound of the conch-shells, <s>Arjuna</s>, seeing <s>Duryodhana</s> and others arrayed — stationed in various formations according to their rank — when the clash of weapons had begun, raising his bow, attentively spoke to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> the words that will be stated. <s>Hṛṣīka</s> means the aggregate of senses; their lord is <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>. 'O lord of the earth' — this is <s>Sañjaya</s>'s address to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>. // 20 //

children.text: kiṃ tad vākyam ity āha
children.translated_text: What were those words? He says:

children.text: ubhayoḥ senayor madhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me 'cyuta // BhG_1.21 //
children.translated_text: Place my chariot between the two armies, O <s>Acyuta</s>. // BhG 1.21 //

yāvad etān nirīkṣe 'haṃ10 yoddhukāmān avasthitān11 /
kair mayā12 saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇasamudyame13 // BhG_1.22 //
children.translated_text: So that I may observe these warriors arrayed and eager to fight — with whom must I fight in this battle engagement? // BhG 1.22 //

madhye rathasthāpanād yuyutsāsaṃśayo 'numīyate14 pārthasya /
taṃ ca prakaṭayiṣyati / kimarthaṃ (senayor madhye) rathasthāpanam iti
ced ata āha yāvad i(ti) / yāvad ity anena kāryaśeṣaṃ sūcayati15
children.translated_text: to that he says 'yāvad' (so that). By 'yāvad' he indicates a remaining purpose.

[Commentary:] From the request to place the chariot in the middle, <s>Pārtha</s>'s doubt about his desire to fight is inferred. And he will make this manifest. If asked why the chariot should be placed between the two armies,

kim uvācety āha he pārtha /
paśyaitān ekatra samavāyaṃ gatān kurūn iti13 /
children.translated_text: And facing all the kings. What did he say? He says: 'O <s>Pārtha</s>, behold these <s>Kurus</s> assembled in one place.'

children.text: bhīṣmadroṇābhimukhe14 rathasthāpanābhiprāyaṃ bhagavān āha

children.text: yata15 pitāmahagurūn16 prati kadācid asyāyuyutsā syāt tad enaṃ

children.text: jñānopadeśena17 pravartayiṣyāmīti18 // 24 //
children.translated_text: direct him through the teaching of knowledge. // 24 //

[Commentary:] <s>Guḍākā</s> means sleep; its lord — the conqueror of sleep — is <s>Arjuna</s>. Thus addressed by him, the Blessed Lord, having placed the chariot in the middle of the two armies, spoke. How did he place it? He says: 'In front of <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>' —

children.text: tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝn atha19 pitāmahān /

children.text: śvaśurān suhṛdaś caiva senayor ubhayor api22 /
children.translated_text: as well as fathers-in-law and companions in both armies. //

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Seeing all those kinsmen and reflecting — 'There is no stranger here; all are my own people' — and wondering 'How are these to be killed?' — he was overcome by intense compassion. Therefore, despairing — falling into depression, abandoning the effort for battle — he spoke thus. The <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) here is used by interchange. // 27 //

children.translated_text: Moreover, through the slackening of effort due to compassion, I am unable to maintain my composure. And due to the excess of suffering, my mind whirls as if mounted on a wheel,

children.text: anavasthitatvād bhramatīvety uktam12 // 29 //
children.translated_text: unstable — hence 'whirls as if' is said. // 29 //

[Commentary:] and <s>romaharṣa</s> means the rising of body hair. The <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> slips — falls down. The skin — the body's surface — burns with the fire of grief. Being in such a state through compassion upon seeing those about to die — here, the difference of agent-subjects should not be objected to, by the previously stated principle. Or, <s>Arjuna</s> is the agent of the act of seeing, and in the failing of limbs and so forth, <s>Arjuna</s> himself is the real agent, for there are no limbs etc. separate from <s>Arjuna</s>. The particle 'iva' (as if), though having the sense of comparison, generates a cognition of difference.

na ca sukhāni kāṅkṣe /
kasmād ity āha --- he govinda (rā)jyena bhogaiḥ sukhādibhir vā
kiṃ naḥ6 kṛtyam / sarvaṃ vā rājyabhogādikaṃ yaj jīvitopakaraṇaṃ7
children.translated_text: Nor do I desire pleasures. Why? he says: O <s>Govinda</s>, what need have we of kingdom, enjoyments, pleasures, and the like? Or, all that is the means of life — kingdom, enjoyments, and so forth —

children.text: tenāpi kiṃ prayojanam iti // 31 //
children.translated_text: what purpose does even that serve? (31)
Since the kinsmen are about to die right now, therefore I do not desire — I do not wish for — even victory. Now if it is said that upon victory, a kingdom is obtained — that is not so.

children.text: na tv eṣa puruṣārthāṃ yad ātmambharitvam /
kiṃ tarhi / sarvaṃ8 (hi) jīvitaṃ rājyādi (vā) gurupitrādyartham
children.translated_text: What then? All life, kingdom, and the like are desired for the sake of teachers, fathers, and others —

children.text:
iṣyata
ity āha9 ---
children.translated_text: thus he says:
But this is not true, that the goal of human life is mere self-sustenance.

children.text: yeṣāṃ arthe kāṅkṣitaṃ10 no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca /
children.translated_text: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures —

children.text: ta eveme sthitā yoddhuṃ prāṇāṃs tyaktvā sudustyajān // BhG_1.32 //
children.translated_text: they themselves are standing here ready to fight, having abandoned their most-difficult-to-renounce lives. (BhG 1.32)

children.text:
yeṣāṃ gurvādīnāṃ kṛte rājyādy asmābhiḥ kāṅkṣitaṃ ta eva
me gurvādayaḥ sudustyajān12 prāṇāṃs tyaktvā13 no 'smākaṃ
purato yoddhuṃ14 sthitāḥ / tat ko nāma buddhipūrvakārī
niṣprayojanaṃ
rājyādi priyaṃ kuryān na gurvādīn15 // 32 //
children.translated_text: Those teachers and others, for whose sake kingdom and the rest were desired by us — those very teachers and others, having abandoned their most-difficult-to-renounce lives, are standing before us ready to fight. So what person, acting deliberately, would desire a purposeless kingdom and the like rather than the teachers and others? (32)

children.text: tān eva darśayati
children.translated_text: He points them out:

children.text: ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ /
children.translated_text: Teachers, fathers, sons, and likewise grandfathers,

children.text: bhātulāḥ (śva)śurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ16 sambandhinas tathā // BhG_1.33 //
children.translated_text: maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and kinsmen. (BhG 1.33)

children.translated_text: Now, overcome with compassion, he says:

children.translated_text: I do not wish to kill these, even though they seek to kill [us], O <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

necchāmi / ghnato hy avaśyaṃ hanyate6 lābhārthaṃ yadi (te) hanyeran /
children.translated_text: I do not wish [to kill them]. For one who seeks to kill will certainly be killed [in return]. Even if they were to be killed for the sake of gain,

children.text: tatra trailokyarājyasyāpi hetor na hantum icchāmi7 kiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: I do not wish to kill even for the sake of sovereignty over the three worlds — how much less

children.text: pṛthivyā arthe // 34 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of the earth! (34)
These teachers and others — even though they seek to kill, even though they desire to harm —

children.text: pāpaśaṅkāyām āha8 ---
children.translated_text: Regarding the apprehension of sin, he says:

children.text: nihatya9 dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana10 /
children.translated_text: What pleasure would be ours, O <s>Janārdana</s>, by killing the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>?

children.text: pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ // BhG_1.35 //
children.translated_text: Sin alone would take hold of us by killing these aggressors. (BhG 1.35)

children.text:
he janārdana etān11 hatvā asmākaṃ ko 'bhyudayo bhavet12 /
kasya hi bandhumaraṇāt prītir utpadyate13 /
prītir iti yady api kṛdabhihito bhāvo dravyavad bhavati14 tathāpi
bhāvarūpatāṃ na jahāti15 nāsti bhinnakartṛkatā /
hananaprītyor hy ekakartṛkatā16 /
yata ātatāyinaḥ kilaite kathan naḥ prītiḥ syād ity āha17 ---
pāpam eveti / etān hatvā pratyuta pāpam eva asmān āśrayet /
yata ātatāyitve 'pi bhrātrādayaḥ sambhajanīyā vardhanīyā
lāḍanoyā na tu
children.translated_text: O <s>Janārdana</s>, having killed these, what prosperity would there be for us? For whose joy arises from the death of kinsmen? As for 'pleasure' (<s>prīti</s>) — although the word, formed by a <s>kṛt</s>-suffix, denotes a state (quality), it [also] functions like a substance; yet it does not abandon its nature as a state, [so] there is no separate agency. For killing and pleasure have [only] one agent. [Objection:] Since these are aggressors, how can there be pleasure for us? — to this he says: 'Sin alone' — having killed these, on the contrary, sin alone would take hold of us. Because even when they are aggressors, they are brothers and the like, who should be honored, nurtured, and

children.translated_text: cherished, not killed. For how would unrighteousness not befall us from killing brothers and the like? Therefore, 'having killed them, sin would take hold.' Here too, the word 'api' [indicates that] in logic

children.translated_text: And so, whoever kills — the sin is done by that very person; thus there is one agent. (35)
there may be separate agency, but in reality there is not.

tadabhiprāyāviṣkaraṇāyāha4 ---
children.translated_text: Having thus described [<s>Arjuna</s> as] distressed with the apprehension of killing brothers and the like, in order to reveal his intent, [<s>Arjuna</s>] says:

children.text: tasmān nārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ5 dhārtarāṣṭrān svabandhavān6 /
children.translated_text: Therefore, we are not justified in killing the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, our own kinsmen.

children.text: svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava // BhG_1.36 //
children.translated_text: For how could we become happy by killing our own people, O <s>Mādhava</s>? (BhG 1.36)

children.text: yasmād dhārtarāṣṭrahananāt prītir nāsti pratyutādharmaḥ7
children.translated_text: Since there is no pleasure from killing the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, but on the contrary there is <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness),

children.text: tasmāt tān svajanavargān hantuṃ vayaṃ nārhāḥ8 /
children.translated_text: therefore we are not justified in killing those kinsmen.

children.text: svajanaṃ hi hatvā kathaṃ sukhino bhavema /
children.translated_text: For having killed our own people, how could we be happy?

children.text: dharmabahiṣkṛtānām etadācāraṇam ityabhyiprāyaḥ9 // 36 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: such conduct [as killing kinsmen] belongs to those who are outside <s>dharma</s>. (36)

children.text: kiṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ10 /
children.translated_text: Even if these, whose minds are overcome by greed, do not see

children.text: kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam // BhG_1.37 //
children.translated_text: the wrong caused by the destruction of the family, or the sin in treachery toward friends, (BhG 1.37)

kathaṃ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum11 /
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhir janārdana12 // BhG_1.38 //
children.translated_text: how should we not know to turn back from this sin, O <s>Janārdana</s>, we who see the wrong caused by the destruction of the family? (BhG 1.38)

druhyatīti
mitradhruk tasmin mitradruhi puruṣe yat pātakam
children.translated_text: The destruction of the family is indeed imminent, already at hand. And the fault caused by that is, as will be described, everything [evil]. And these — <s>Droṇa</s> and others — are friends, since they maintain friendship toward us. The sin involved in treachery toward them — in the desire to kill them — or, friends betray, thus one is a betrayer of friends (<s>mitradhruk</s>); the sin in that person who is a betrayer of friends —

children.translated_text: — that is the connection. These sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, whose minds are afflicted by the greed for obtaining the earth, even though they do not see — do not consider — both of these [evils], still, how should we not know to turn back from such sin as described? We must certainly know — this is the meaning. What kind of 'us'? Those who perceive the fault caused by the destruction of the family. (38)

children.text: tam eva doṣaṃ darśayati8
children.translated_text: He shows that very fault:

children.text: kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the family is destroyed, the eternal family <s>dharmas</s> perish;

children.text: dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta9 // BhG_1.39 //
children.translated_text: when <s>dharma</s> is destroyed, <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) overwhelms the entire family. (BhG 1.39)

children.text:
kulakṣaye sati ye dharmā nityanaimittikā yāgādayo
gotrasamācārāḥ srtīrakṣaṇādayaś cānādikālīnās te
puruṣāṇām anuṣṭhātṝṇām abhāvāt praṇaśyanti10 /
yatra ca dharmasya hānis tatrāvaśyam adharmaḥ prabhavati parasparaṃ
pratyanīkatvāt tayoḥ / tadabhibhūtaś ca11 prāṇino 'kāryeṣu
children.translated_text: because the two are mutually opposed. And [beings] overcome by that [<s>adharma</s>], creatures engage in improper actions —

children.text: pravartanta ity āha12 --- dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam iti /
children.translated_text: thus he says: 'When <s>dharma</s> is destroyed, the entire family...'

children.text: ubhayalokahitavan nistryādikam adharma ākramya tiṣṭhatīty arthaḥ14 /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: <s>adharma</s>, detrimental to both worlds, transgressing [the duties toward] women and the like, takes hold and persists.

children.text: utāvaśyam iti // 39 //
children.translated_text: 'Uta' [means] certainly. (39)

When the family is destroyed, the <s>dharmas</s> — the permanent and occasional rites such as sacrifices, the practices of the clan, the protection of women, and the like, which have existed from time immemorial — perish due to the absence of persons to perform them. And wherever there is a loss of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s> inevitably prevails,

children.text: kiṃ ca
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇā praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the prevalence of <s>adharma</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the women of the family become corrupted;

children.text: strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ // BhG_1.40 //
children.translated_text: when women are corrupted, O descendant of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> (intermixture of castes) arises. (BhG 1.40)

children.text:
adharmābhibhavād hetoḥ kulastriyaḥ caritrahīnā15 bhavanti /
tāsu duṣṭāsu varṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ /
varṇaś cāsau saṅkaraś ceti / aśuddho varṇa ity arthaḥ // 40 //
children.translated_text: From the prevalence of <s>adharma</s>, as the cause, the women of the family become devoid of good character. When they are corrupted, O descendant of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> arises. <s>Varṇa</s> (caste) that is also <s>saṅkara</s> (mixture) — meaning: impure caste. (40)

children.text: saṅkaro narakāyaiva kuladhnānāṃ kulasya ca1 /
children.translated_text: Intermixture [of castes leads] to hell alone for the destroyers of the family and for the family itself;

children.translated_text: for their ancestors fall, deprived of the rites of <s>piṇḍa</s> (food-offering) and water-offering. (BhG 1.41)

sa varṇasaṅkaraḥ kulasya narakapatanāya kalpate /
yataḥ --- santatiḥ śuddhavaṃśyā tu patareha ca śarmaṇe /
viparītā tu narakāya ity āgamaḥ2 /
kuladhnānāṃ ca narakāya / yato varṇasaṅkarotpattau3

children.text:
kuladhnāḥ kāraṇabhāvaṃ pratipadyante4 / kasmāt saṅkaro narakāya5 /
yasmād eṣām ubhayasainyāśritakulānāṃ pitaraḥ dharmyasantānābhāval
luptapiṇḍodakakriyā6 bhavanti / piṇḍaś ca udakaṃ ca piṇḍodake
tayoḥ kriyāḥ tā luptā yeṣāṃ te śrāddhādivicchede7 sati patanti //
children.translated_text: the family-destroyers become causes [of that sin]. Why does intermixture lead to hell? Because the ancestors of these — belonging to the families of both armies — being deprived of the rites of <s>piṇḍa</s> (food-offering) and water-offering due to the absence of righteous offspring, fall [from their heavenly state] when the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) and other [ceremonies] are interrupted.

That <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> (intermixture of castes) serves as the cause for the family's fall into hell. Because [scripture says]: 'Offspring of pure lineage is for welfare here and hereafter; the opposite leads to hell' — thus is the tradition.

children.text: punar api śokasaṃvignatvāt8 saṅkṣepeṇa tad evālocayann āha9 ---
children.translated_text: Furthermore, being agitated by grief, surveying that very [consequence] in brief, he says:

children.text: doṣair etaiḥ kuladhnānāṃ10 varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ /

children.text: utsādyate11 jātir dharmaḥ kuladharmaś ca śāśvataḥ // BhG_1.42 //

kuladhnānāṃ sambandhibhiḥ etaiḥ yathoktaiḥ
kuladharmanāśādharmābhibhavakulastrīdūṣaṇair varṇasaṅkarakārakair
hetubhiḥ12 doṣaiḥ kulābhāvād jātidharmo 'nādikālīnaḥ13
kṣātraḥ14

children.translated_text: and the family <s>dharma</s>, such as Vedic study, devotion, water-offering, and the like, are destroyed — uprooted

children.text: vilopyata ity arthaḥ // 42 //
children.translated_text: from the very root — this is the meaning. (42)

By these above-described faults — the destruction of family <s>dharma</s>, the prevalence of <s>adharma</s>, the corruption of the women of the family — which are causes of <s>varṇasaṅkara</s>, belonging to the kinsmen of the family-destroyers: from the absence of the family, the <s>dharma</s> of caste (<s>jātidharma</s>), which has existed from time immemorial —

children.text: tataś ca ---
children.translated_text: And therefore:

children.text: utasannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana /
children.translated_text: For those whose family <s>dharmas</s> have been destroyed, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.translated_text: a dwelling in hell is certain — so we have heard. (BhG 1.43)

children.translated_text: When the family <s>dharma</s> has been destroyed, this is another fault — that through family <s>dharmas</s>

evaṃ saṃśayāviṣṭacetā3 narakapratyavāyadarśanāt sañjātasaṃvega
āha4 ---
children.translated_text: Thus, with a mind beset by doubt, having seen the evil consequences leading to hell, filled with alarm, he says:

children.text: aho bata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ5 vyavasitā vayam /
children.translated_text: Alas! We have resolved to commit a great sin,

children.text: yad rājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ6 svajanam udyatāḥ // BhG_1.44 //
children.translated_text: in that, out of greed for the pleasures of sovereignty, we are prepared to slay our own kinsmen. (BhG 1.44)

children.text:
aho vismaye / bata viṣāde / yad rājyasukhalobhena vismayakāriṇā7
sārabhūtaṃ durlabhaṃ svajanaṃ hantuṃ vayam udyatāḥ tat mahatpāpaṃ
kartuṃ vyavasitā ity ato 'sya viṣādaḥ8 /
tathā rājyasukhaṃ nāma paśya kīdṛśaṃ yena vayam adya pāpāḥ
sambhāvyamānasvajanavadhāya pravartāmaha9 iti10 vismayaḥ /
yad vā11 aho dainye / bata khedānukampayoḥ /
rājyena yat sukhaṃ tallobhāt svajanavadhapāpavyavasāye pravartāmahe12
/
trayo 'py ete kleśā rājyārtham asya prādur abhavann iti13 kṛtvā
nivartitum icchatīti14 // 44 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Aho</s>' [expresses] amazement. '<s>Bata</s>' [expresses] sorrow. That, out of greed for the pleasures of sovereignty—which is cause for amazement—we are prepared to slay our own kinsmen, who are essential and rare, means we have resolved to commit a great sin—hence his sorrow. Also: 'See what the pleasure of sovereignty is like, by which we sinful ones are now engaged in the slaughter of our anticipated kinsmen'—thus is the amazement. Or else: '<s>aho</s>' [expresses] wretchedness; '<s>bata</s>' [expresses] distress and compassion. Out of greed for the happiness that comes from sovereignty, we are engaged in the sinful resolve of slaying our kinsmen. All three afflictions arose in him on account of sovereignty—considering this, he wishes to desist. (44)

children.text: saṃvegākulaḥ punar api pralapann āha15 ---
children.translated_text: Agitated with alarm, lamenting again, he says:

children.text: yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṃ16 śastraprāṇayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, weapons in hand, were to slay me in battle, unarmed and unresisting,

children.text: dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṃ bhavet // BhG_1.45 //
children.translated_text: that would be more beneficial for me. (BhG 1.45)

children.text:
yadi dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ santaḥ mām aśastram
anudyatāyudham apratīkāram17 akṛtapratividhānam udāsīnāvasthaṃ
hanyus tan me
children.translated_text: If the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, with weapons in hand, were to slay me—unarmed, with no weapon raised, unresisting, having made no counter-measures, remaining in a state of indifference—that would be

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. dharmaiḥ pretānāṃ parasvargādabhyu^ yogaḥ satadvicchedānna bhavati pratyata
2. ^kule^ ... patanamityervaveda^
3. eva śayāviṣṭacetā
4. āha 43
5. kartu
6. hantu
7. vismāreṇa
8. ciṣādaḥ
9. vayamadhyasambhāvyamānapāpāstvajanavadhayāye pra^
10. hati
11. yuddhā
12. pravatīmade
13. kleśāṃyārthasya prā^
14. ^micchatīti
15. ^āha 44
16. ^bratīkāra^
17. tāyadhamaṃ^

children.translated_text: more beneficial, more fitting for me.

children.text: paro manorathaḥ (siddhaḥ) syāt pāp(ā)karaṇād ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The highest wish (would be) fulfilled, by not committing sin—this is the meaning.

children.text: saśastraṃ1 sapratīkāraṃ māṃ hantuṃ na kecana kṣamāḥ syur
children.translated_text: No one would be capable of slaying me if I were armed and resisting—

children.text: ity ubhayor upādānam // 45 //
children.translated_text: the mention of both [unarmed and unresisting] [is for this reason]. (45)

children.text:
idānīṃ sañjayo dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ2 praty arjunakathāprastāvaṃ
samāpayann i(da)m āha ---
children.translated_text: Now <s>Sañjaya</s>, concluding the narrative of <s>Arjuna</s> addressed to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, says this:

children.text: evam uktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye3 rathopastha upāviśat /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Arjuna</s> sat down on the chariot-seat in the midst of battle,

children.text: utsṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ // BhG_1.46 //
children.translated_text: casting aside his bow along with its arrows, his mind overcome by grief. (BhG 1.46)

children.text:
tān samīkṣya ...... sīdamāno 'bravīd idam ity ataḥ prabhṛti
evaṃ yathoktam uktvā arjunaḥ4 saṅkhye yuddhabhūmau
dhanur utsṛjya5 rathasyopary upāviśat / kiṃ kāraṇam /
yataḥ svajanahananajanitaśokākula6 iti // 46 //
children.translated_text: From 'seeing them...... sinking down, he spoke this' onwards, having spoken as described above, <s>Arjuna</s>, on the battlefield, having cast aside his bow, sat upon the chariot. For what reason? Because he was agitated by grief born from [the prospect of] slaying his own kinsmen. (46)

children.text: atra saṅgrahaślokāḥ ---
children.translated_text: Here are the summary verses:

children.text: śūrasaṅkhyā paravyūhe svabale śūrasaṅgrahaḥ7 /
children.translated_text: The enumeration of warriors in the enemy's formation, the gathering of warriors in one's own army,

children.text: tadviveko bhīṣmarakṣā8 śaṅkhavāditraniḥsvanāḥ //
children.translated_text: their distinction, the protection of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, the sounding of conches and instruments,

children.text: didṛkṣā sainyayor jñātigurumitrānudarśanam9 /
children.translated_text: the desire to see both armies, the sight of kinsmen, elders, and friends,

children.text: tajjānukampā pārthasya paridevaparibhramau //
children.translated_text: the compassion born thereof of <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), his lamentation and confusion,

children.text: yuddhatyāgaś ca śokaś ca10 padārthāḥ sārasaṅgrahaḥ11 //
children.translated_text: the abandonment of battle and grief—these are the topics [and] the summary of essentials.

children.text: iti śrīmadbhagavadgītāsu bhagavadbhāskarakṛte
children.translated_text: Thus, in the blessed <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>, in the commentary composed by the revered <s>Bhāskara</s>

children.text: bhagavadāśayānusaraṇābhidhāne bhāṣye 'rjunaviṣādo12 nāma
children.translated_text: called '<s>Bhagavadāśayānusaraṇa</s>' (Following the Intent of the Lord), [the chapter entitled] '<s>Arjunaviṣāda</s>' (The Despondency of <s>Arjuna</s>),

children.text: prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: the first chapter. (1)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. maśastraṃ
2. dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ
3. ^muktā sekhye
4. yathoktamuttkārjunaḥ
5. dhanuḥnsṛjya
6. yata sṛvajanahanana^
7. ślokā'paravyūhe śūrasaṅkhyāsva^
8. ^rakṣāṃ
9. didṛśā sainyayojñāti^
10. yuddhatyāgo daśaikaśca
11. saṅgrahaḥ / 46
12. bhāṣe^
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: atha dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the second chapter.

children.text:
ittham antakavaktrakuharābhimukhaṃ janaṃ mitrabandhuvargaṃ
prati jātaghṛṇaṃ arjunaṃ1 pṛthivībhārāvataraṇasampipādayiṣayā
bhagavān svadharmasahitasamyagdarśanopadeśena yuyodhayiṣatīti
pratipādayituṃ dvitīyādhyāyagranthārambhaḥ2 /
taṃ sañjayo dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ prati vivṛṇvann āha3 ---
children.translated_text: With the intention of motivating <s>Arjuna</s>—who had become compassionate toward his group of friends and relatives, [that group being] headed toward the jaws of death—to fight, through the teaching of right knowledge combined with one's own <s>dharma</s> (<s>svadharma</s>), for the purpose of relieving the earth of its burden, the composition of the second chapter begins. <s>Sañjaya</s>, narrating this to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, says:

children.text: taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam4 /
children.translated_text: To him, thus overcome with compassion, his eyes filled and troubled with tears,

children.text: sīdamānam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ // BhG_2.1 //
children.translated_text: despondent, <s>Madhusūdana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) spoke these words. (BhG 2.1)

children.text:
tam arjunaṃ tena prakāreṇa prathamādhyāyoktena
gātrāvasādamukhaśoṣaromaharṣādilakṣaṇam avasīdantaṃ5
kāruṇyaparavaśam ata evāśrupūravyākulatvāl lohitekṣaṇam
avasīdantaṃ6 vyuparatayuddhodyamaṃ bhagavān vakṣyamāṇaṃ
children.translated_text: to him, sinking down, having ceased from the effort of battle, the Blessed Lord spoke the words

children.text: vākyam uvāca /
children.translated_text: that are about to be stated.

children.text: taṃ vākyam uvāceti dvikarmakatā // 1 //
children.translated_text: 'Spoke him the words'—[this has] a double-object construction. (1)

To that <s>Arjuna</s>, in the manner described in the first chapter—sinking down, characterized by bodily weakness, dryness of mouth, horripilation, and the like, overcome by compassion, and hence with reddened eyes due to being overwhelmed by tears—

children.text: kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ7 viṣame samupasthitam8 /
children.translated_text: Whence has this faint-heartedness come upon you at this difficult time,

children.text: anāryajuṣṭam asvargyam akīrtikaram arjuna // BhG_2.2 //
children.translated_text: which is unworthy of a noble person, which does not lead to heaven, which brings disrepute, O <s>Arjuna</s>? (BhG 2.2)

children.text:
kuta iti saṃśayānaḥ pṛcchati9 / kasmād idaṃ mohalakṣaṇaṃ
pāpaṃ kartṛ tvām upagatam āga(ta)m / asmin viṣame saṅkaṭe
trailokyasambhāvitapauruṣaṃ tvām asambhāvyamāno mohaḥ
kutaḥ samprāpta iti mahān saṃśayaḥ / kīdṛśaṃ10 kaśmalam /
children.translated_text: [asks] whence has it come? This is a great doubt. What kind of faint-heartedness?

children.text: kulaśīlavidyārahitaiḥ sevitam ataś cākīrtikaraṃ tata eva
children.translated_text: That which is practiced by those devoid of good family, character, and learning, and hence brings disrepute; and for that very reason

children.text: cāsvargya narakādiprāpakaṃ tasmāt // 2 //
children.translated_text: does not lead to heaven, being that which leads to hell and the like. Therefore: (2)

'Whence'—being in doubt, [the Lord] asks: From where has this sinful delusion-like [faint-heartedness] come upon you, the doer? In this crisis, this difficult situation, [the Lord], considering it inconceivable that you—whose valor is renowned in the three worlds—should be overcome by delusion,

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. ^kuharābhimukhajanamitravundhuvargaṃ prati tāta^
2. ^granthāraṃmaḥ
3. prativṛṇvannaha
4. ^mastrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam
5. tamarjuna tena prakāraṇa prathamādhyoṅktena gātrāvasādamubhāṃśoṣa^
6. kuruṇva ... evāludū^
7. kaśprala^
8. samapasthitam
9. pūchati
10. kīvṛśaṃ
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: mā klaivyaṃ gaccha kaunteya naitat tvayy upapadyate1 /
children.translated_text: Do not yield to unmanliness, O <s>Kaunteya</s>! This does not befit you.

children.text: kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha2 parantapa // BhG_2.3 //
children.translated_text: Cast off this base faint-heartedness and arise, O scorcher of foes! (BhG 2.3)

children.text:
klaibyam amanuṣyatvaṃ dīnabhāvaṃ mohān mā gaccha3 mā āśraya
yatas tvayi4 khāṇḍavānalatarpaṇena saṅgrāmārādhitatryambakatayā
nivātakavacavadhaparitoṣitapurandaratvādibhir upādānair deveṣv api5
prakhyātapauruṣe naitad upapadyate na sambhāvyate6 /
atas tvaṃ hṛdayasyālpasāratvaṃ7 kṣudram alpavastubhūtaṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, [cast off] this faint-heartedness of the heart—this base, trifling thing,

children.text: nyūnahṛdayatvaṃ8 kāpuruṣasevitaṃ tyaktvā rathopasthād uttiṣṭha /
children.translated_text: this inferiority of heart, practiced by cowards—cast it off and rise from the chariot-seat!

children.text: utthāya ca yuddhāya sajjo bhavety āśayaḥ9 /
children.translated_text: And having risen, be ready for battle—this is the intent.

children.text: parantapety anenārjunaṃ protsāhayati // 3 //
children.translated_text: By [the epithet] '<s>Parantapa</s>' (scorcher of foes), he encourages <s>Arjuna</s>. (3)

Unmanliness—non-manliness, a state of wretchedness—do not, out of delusion, yield to it, do not resort to it. Because in you—whose valor is celebrated even among the gods through such accomplishments as satisfying the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> fire, gratifying <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) in battle, and pleasing <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) by slaying the <s>Nivātakavacas</s> and the like—this is not fitting, it is not to be expected.

children.text: evaṃ bhagavatokte 'rjuna uvāca10 ---
children.translated_text: When the Blessed Lord has thus spoken, <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṅkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana /
children.translated_text: How shall I fight in battle against <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi11 pūjārhāv arisūdana // BhG_2.4 //
children.translated_text: with arrows, [against those] who are worthy of worship, O destroyer of enemies? (BhG 2.4)

children.text:
kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa kayā yuktyā12 bhīṣmādīn mānanīyān ahaṃ
pratiyotsyāmi11 / madhusūdanārisūdaneti bhaktaḥ punaḥ punar āsthāṃ
karoti samakrameṇa // 4 //
children.translated_text: step by step. (4)

How—by what means, by what method, by what reasoning—shall I fight against <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others who are worthy of respect? By [addressing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as] '<s>Madhusūdana</s>' and '<s>Arisūdana</s>' (destroyer of enemies), the devotee repeatedly expresses his trust,

children.text: kim iti13 na ca pratiyotsyāmīty āha14 ---
children.translated_text: 'Why will I not fight back?'—[to explain this] he says:

children.text: gurūn ahatvā15 hi mahānubhāvān śreyaś cartuṃ bhaiṣkyam apīha16 loke /
children.translated_text: It would be better to live in this world even by begging, rather than to slay these great-souled elders.

children.text: na tv arthakāmas tu gurūn nihatya bhuñjīya bhogān rudhir apradigdhān17 // BhG_2.5 //
children.translated_text: But having slain these elders who desire wealth, I would enjoy blood-stained pleasures in this very world. (BhG 2.5)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. gaccha kauṇtaveya naitatvasyupapadyate
2. taṅktontiṣṭa
3. gacha
4. tvaṣi
5. ^bhirapādānaira^
6. naitadrupapadyata nā sābhāvyate
7. ata sata hṛdayasya^
8. ^mūtānyūnahṛdaya^
9. tyattkā rathopasthāḥ uttiṣṭa / usyāya ca pukṛya sajjayā bhavetyāśayaḥ
10. uvāca 3
11. pratiyotsāmi
12. yuktā
13. ^nāriyūdaneti bhaktāpunaḥ punarāchānā karoti / samatrameṇa
kimiti
14. ca na pratiyotsyāma ityāha 4
15. ^hatva
16. śreyaścabhunttubhaikṣamapīha
17. patigghān
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
hi yataḥ kāraṇāt1 / yasmād (iha loke deśe) gurūn bhīṣmādīn
prati yuddhavarjanena ahatvā rakṣitvā bhaikṣyam api cartuṃ2 śreyaḥ /
na tu dhanābhilāṣī san gurūn nihatya bhogān rājyādīn3
śoṇitalepabahulān bhuñjīyeti kutsā /
naiva bhuñjīyety arthaḥ / iha loka iha kṣaṇike jīvaloka ity arthaḥ /
tuśabdo guruhananavyāvṛttisū(ca)nārthaḥ / punas tugrahaṇād
bhaikṣyam api praśasyataram4 / na tv evaṃvidho viṣayopabhoga iti // 5 //
children.translated_text: 'For' (<s>hi</s>)—because of the following reason: Since, by refraining from battle against elders such as <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others in this world, having not slain but protected them, even begging is better. But it would be contemptible to slay the elders while desiring wealth, and enjoy the royal pleasures and such that are steeped in blood. One should never enjoy [them]—this is the meaning. 'In this world' means 'in this fleeting world of the living.' The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) serves to indicate the distinction from slaying one's elders. From the second use of '<s>tu</s>', even begging is more praiseworthy; but such an enjoyment of sense pleasures [is not]. (5)

children.text: etaddaśāyām idam iva tāvad vicāryatām5 ---
children.translated_text: In this situation, let at least this much be considered:

children.text: na caitad vidmaḥ6 kataran no garīyo yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ /
children.translated_text: And we do not know which would be better for us—whether we should conquer or they should conquer us.

children.text: yān eva7 hatvā na jijīviṣāmas8 tena sthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ9 // BhG_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Those very ones, having slain whom we would not wish to live—the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> stand before us. (BhG 2.6)

children.text:
caśabdaḥ pūrvāpekṣayādhikābhyudayayuktidyotanārthaḥ10 /
etad iti vakṣyamāṇāvamarśinā sarvanāmnā ---
yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ ---
ity etadvakṣyamāṇavākyadvayābhidheyo 'rthaḥ pratyavamṛśyate11 /
na ty ātmīyaparavargāv ekīkṛtya12 nirdeśaḥ /
sa dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām asmākam ity artho vivakṣitaḥ13 /
katarad ity anena sāmānyavādinā tadvākyadvayābhidheyayor balayor
ekataraṃ garīyastvena vikalpato nirṇīyate14 /
children.translated_text: The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), with reference to the preceding, serves to indicate a reasoning of greater force. 'This' (<s>etat</s>)—by this pronoun which reflects on what is about to be said—the meaning expressed by the two statements about to be said, 'whether we should conquer or they should conquer us,' is reconsidered. The reference is not made by combining one's own party and the other into one, but the intended meaning is: 'of the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s>' and 'of us.' By '<s>katarat</s>' (which [of the two]), a general term, one of the two parties denoted by those two statements is determined in terms of superiority, as an alternative.

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. hiḥ kāraṇāyadeśe
2. cartu
3. śabdādīn
4. ^rthaḥ / agrahaṇātnmaikṣyamapi praśaṃsya^
5. etadāssābhidameva tāvadvicāryatām 5
6. viḍmaḥ
7. vāneva
8. jijoviṣāmaste^
9. pramusto dhartarāṣṭrāḥ
10. ^pekṣayābhyupayuktidyotanārthaḥ
11. ^vamaśinā sarvanāmnā padya jayema yadi vā no nayeyurityetadvākyatvayābhidheyorthaḥ pratyavamṛṣyate
12. ^svargāvakīkṛtya
13. ^maspākamityartho vivakṣataḥ
14. tadvākyadvatyābhidheyayorvalayo^
15. niṇormate
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
yadyadiśabdau vitarke vikalpe vā /
tad ayaṃ vākyārthaḥ1 --- na caitad vayaṃ jayaparājayayor aniyamāj
jānīmaḥ2 katarad balam asmākaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ
madhyād garīyo3 gurutaraṃ balavattaram iti /
yad vā vayaṃ tān jayemābhibhavema4 yadi vā te no 'smān jayeyur
abhibhaveyur iti5 / kiṃ ca6 yān eva dhārtarāṣṭrān hatvā jīvituṃ
necchāmaḥ7 kṛpālutayā ta evāsmākaṃ pramukhe sammukhe sthitā iti /
children.translated_text: out of compassion—those very ones stand before us, facing us.

children.text: etac cārjunasya sambhramaparidevanaṃ hastādyabhinayena // 6 //
children.translated_text: And this [expression of] <s>Arjuna's</s> confusion and lamentation [is conveyed] through gestures of the hands and so forth. (6)

The words '<s>yat</s>' and '<s>yadi</s>' [are used] in the sense of deliberation or alternative. The meaning of the passage is thus: We do not know, because of the uncertainty of victory and defeat, which army—ours or the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s>'—is the superior, the greater, the more powerful. 'Whether we should conquer them, i.e. overcome them, or they should conquer us, i.e. overcome us.' Moreover, those very <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s>, having slain whom we would not wish to live,

children.text: evaṃ sakāraṇaṃ svaparidevanaṃ punar api8 bhagavantam arjuna āha9 ---
children.translated_text: Thus, again stating his lamentation with its cause to the Blessed Lord, <s>Arjuna</s> says:

children.text: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi10 tvāṃ dharmasammūḍhacetāḥ11 /
children.translated_text: 'My nature is overcome by the defect of wretchedness; my mind is confused about <s>dharma</s> — I ask you.',

children.text: yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṃ brūhi tan me śiṣyas te 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam12 // BhG_2.7 //
children.translated_text: 'Tell me decisively what would be better; I am your disciple — instruct me, who have sought refuge in you.' // BhG 2.7 //

children.text:
evam ahaṃ gurubandhumitrasvajanān mṛtyunā dhṛtān dṛṣṭvā13
kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ14 kārpaṇyam aucityapratipakṣabhūtaṃ
dainyam15 tad eva doṣas tenopahato dūṣitaḥ sattvadhairyātmakaḥ16
svabhāvo yasya sa tathoktaḥ / tathā dharme sammūḍham apratipattiṃ
gataṃ ceto yasya so 'haṃ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ parameśvaram /
yan me śreyaḥ syāt tan me niścitam asandigdhaṃ brūhīti17 /
dharmaviṣayadainyadoṣopahatacitto 'ham ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, having seen my teachers, kinsmen, friends, and relatives seized by death — my nature is overcome by the defect of wretchedness (<s>kārpaṇyadoṣa</s>). 'Wretchedness' (<s>kārpaṇya</s>) is dejection, which stands as the opposite of propriety; that itself is the defect; one whose nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — whose [inner] character consisting of goodness and fortitude — is overcome and corrupted by it, is so described. Likewise, one whose mind has become confused and reached a state of indecision regarding <s>dharma</s> — I, being such, ask you, the Supreme Lord. Tell me that which would be better for me, decisively, without doubt — [this is the meaning]. The sense is: I am one whose mind is overcome by the defect of dejection concerning [my] duty.

children.text: senayor ubhayor madhye12 sīdamānam idaṃ vacaḥ // BhG_2.10 //

prati tyktotsāhaṃ hṛṣīkeśo14 hasann idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ vākyam

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There, because of the firm resolve of <s>Arjuna</s>, who said 'I shall not fight' under the influence of false self-knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) regarding the self, and since the cessation of that [delusion] was impossible without the teaching of self-knowledge (<s>ātmajñāna</s>) — in order to introduce the occasion for that teaching, the Blessed Lord said:

children.translated_text: seized by compassion upon seeing your kinsmen who have approached the mouth of death.' // BhG 2.11 //

children.translated_text: — this is appropriate. // 11 //

[Commentary:] You — your mind made impure by a tendency common to the human species. And for this very reason, seeing your kinsmen who have begun to approach the mouth of death face-on, overcome by compassion, bereft of consciousness (<s>visañjña</s>) — meaning one whose divine knowledge is obstructed — through the seizure by grief and delusion common to the human species, you have become thus.

children.text: kasmād visañjño 'sīty āha9 ---
children.translated_text: 'Why are you bereft of consciousness?' — to that he says:

children.text: aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ10 prajñāvādāṃś ca bhāṣase /
children.translated_text: 'You have grieved for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words of wisdom;

children.text: gatāsūnagatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ // BhG_2.12 //
children.translated_text: the wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.' // BhG 2.12 //

bhāvino 'rthasya13 ca nityatvād aśocyatvam /
api ca prajñāvādāṃś ca bhāṣase ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] You have grieved for those who should not be grieved for — <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others. For they are not worthy of grief because they are engaged in the performance of their own <s>dharma</s>, because there is [thereby] the non-failure of the three aims of life (<s>trivarga</s>), and because the reality to come is eternal. Moreover, you speak words of wisdom [such as]:

children.text:
pāpam evāśrayed asmān14 śreyaś cartuṃ bhaikṣyam apīha15 loke ---
iti16 /
tad etad ubhayaṃ tava (na) śobhate /

pariniṣṭhitatattvajñānāḥ18

tātparyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For them, grief does not exist because they see the indestructibility of the <s>ātman</s>. Likewise, you should attain that [knowledge of] indestructibility and abandon delusion and grief — this is the purport.

/
agnivisphuliṅgavan mahākāśaghaṭākāśavaj
jīvaparayor bhedābhedau15 /

/
anādisiddhāś ca jīvāḥ sanātanā iti vacanān na teṣāṃ
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And [the Lord] will say: 'An eternal portion of Myself becomes the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) in the world of living beings.' Just as sparks [relate to] fire, just as pot-space [relates to] the great space — so between the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>Paramātman</s> there is both identity and difference. Therein, the identity is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>), while the difference is due to limiting adjuncts (<s>aupādhika</s>) — this is the established position. Thus, hereafter, sometimes the designation will be through non-difference and sometimes through difference. And the <s>jīvas</s> are beginninglessly established and eternal (<s>sanātana</s>) — as stated; therefore there is neither their origination at the beginning of creation

children.text: sargādāv utpādaḥ pralayo vānte / (ta)thā ca yājñavalkyaḥ18 ---
children.translated_text: nor their dissolution at its end. And thus [says] <s>Yājñavalkya</s>:

[Commentary:] The word 'tu' (indeed) functions in the sense of 'at any time.' I was never at any time non-existent; rather, I existed indeed. You were not non-existent; rather, you existed — this is the meaning. These — <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others — were not non-existent; rather, they existed indeed. 'Nor shall we not be' — after [departure from] this body, in another body we shall indeed exist. By this, existence in all three times is declared. The designation of difference [among <s>jīvas</s>] is due to the difference of <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field) in each body.

And it is not reasonable that the <s>Paramātman</s> is a transmigrant, because of its association with knowledge, and because [the Upaniṣad declares:] 'consciousness, bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' — and because of its nature as eternal space-like bliss. then whose is that body? Since there is no distinction in the relationship of all [selves to bodies], and if it be said that the arrangement is due to intention and the like — since there is equality among intentions, etc., in a single mind, the volitions and the like of all [selves] would be co-inherent in one [mind]; the action preceded by that [volition] and the body caused by that [karma] — since all would be common to all, no cause of particularity can ever be shown by anyone. Since beginninglessness is common even to our position, the individual selves (<s>jīva</s>) are accepted as atomic in size. Why? children.translated_text: as the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> say. This is not so — the individual self, though stationed in the inner organ, does not [itself] perceive [pleasure and pain]. Just as form and the rest stationed in pots and the like [do not belong to the pots themselves]. And it will be said that this is not a property of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>: 'desire, hatred, pleasure, pain...' [BhG 13.6]. Although pleasure and pain co-inhere with the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, there is no modification of its essential nature — like the nature of a jewel. It is only the blue, yellow, and other [colors] that co-inhere with the jewel that undergo modification through mutual opposition. For modification means destruction, dissolution. So too of the self — there is no non-being, no destruction, of the existent self — because of the recognition 'I am he,' because eternality is established, and because there is no cause of non-eternality. As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'This self is indeed indestructible' [Bṛhadāraṇyaka]. Of both — the existent and the non-existent — the conclusion, the ascertainment, the boundary, the final state, has been seen. children.translated_text: The meaning is: by those who know the true nature of things. But others — the <s>Māyāvādins</s> (proponents of the doctrine of illusion) — interpret differently. [They say:] and from this [verse too], setting aside grief and delusion, of cold, heat, and the like there is being — existence. From what? From the fact of being a modification. And a modification, when examined by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) such as perception and the rest, arrives at non-existence. Just as a pot and the like, not being perceived apart from its material cause, is non-existent — so all modifications [are non-existent]. Now, if everything is thus non-existent, then the doctrine of the void (<s>śūnyavāda</s>) would follow. This is not a fault. For all sentient beings are known to have two types of cognition: the cognition of the qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>) and the cognition of the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>). [For example:] 'the pot exists,' 'the cloth exists.' Therein, the cognition directed toward the qualified — directed toward the pot and such — is a false cognition, because it deviates when applied to cloth and the like. But the cognition directed toward the qualifier — the cognition of 'being' (<s>sat</s>) — since it operates everywhere, is not false. Therefore, that alone is ultimately real. For they hold that all proliferation — pots, bodies, and the like — is mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion), unreal.
By whom was this determination made? He says: by the seers of truth (<s>tattvadarśin</s>).

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Nor does unreality follow merely from deviation. Just as the cognition of a pot, through deviating in the case of cloth, would be unreal, so too the cognition of Being, through deviating in the case of a hare's horn, would also be unreal — this consequence follows. The cognition of existence turns away from non-existence, since existence and non-existence are mutually contradictory. Now, just as the cognition of Being reveals existence, so too the cognition of pots and such — since there is no difference in being produced by the senses, and since they are apprehended through the cognition of continuity and exclusion — all intermediate universals such as pot-ness, cow-ness, and so forth must be accepted. And thus the individual is related to the universal, being its property. The universal is twofold — higher and lower. The higher is characterized by Being (<s>sattā</s>). The lower is characterized by cow-ness and such. For the existence of the substrate (the qualified entity) does not establish the reality of the universal dependent on it. For <s>sattā</s> (being) is the existence of what exists. It is not independent and pure, apprehended by any eye that is free from defect and not dependent on a substrate like a pot. When substances such as earth and others are being apprehended, <s>sattā</s> too is apprehended as inherent in them and inseparable from them. Therefore <s>sattā</s>, being a property of substance, is not the <s>ātman</s>. Thus what some have said — that <s>sattā</s> alone is the <s>ātman</s> — is thereby refuted. Therefore what was said by someone — 'perception is not to be censured by the wise, because of its fourfold nature' — intending that perception grasps <s>sattā</s> alone — that too is refuted.

For when the capacity of the object, sense organ, light, and mental impressions is present, the cognition of a pot never fails to arise for anyone. Moreover, being an effect, the cognition of pot-ness requires a cause. The pot alone is the cause of pot-knowledge, nothing else. Just as the sprout of a seed requires the seed as its cause, and smoke requires fire, so too elsewhere. Therefore deviation is not a false reason — this is a wrong teaching. children.translated_text: the modification of existence is negated. How is this? 'Having once come to be, this [<s>Ātman</s>] will not cease to be' — 'again' means once more. What then? It will certainly continue to be. The meaning is: even in the future time, it will not abandon existence. And by the word 'vā,' the [modification of] coming into being from non-being is negated. 'This does not come to be from non-being' — what then? Having [always] existed, it will continue to exist. The meaning is: it never lost its existence even in the past. But that which, having not existed, comes into being, and having existed, ceases to be — that is subject to birth and destruction, like a pot and the like. The existence [of the <s>Ātman</s>] is not conceived as preceded by birth, like that of a pot. Its existence is without limit — this is how it differs from pots and the like. He concludes: 'Unborn, eternal.' By the negation of birth and destruction alone, the intermediate modifications of existence are also negated. Even so, for the sake of assisting those of dull intellect, he negates them with specific words. By 'eternal' (<s>śāśvata</s>), decay is negated — there is no diminution of its limbs or of its means. Just as [one says] a king is thin, or diminished in elephants and horses, and so forth. By 'primeval' (<s>purāṇa</s>), the modification of existence characterized by aging is negated. This [<s>Ātman</s>] does not wane in phases like the moon. 'It is not killed when the body is killed' — thereby transformation is negated. Transformation means the transition to another state, as [for example] the state of flesh in [the case of] a hare.
[Commentary:] 'It is not born' — thereby the modification of existence characterized by birth is negated.

For the context, as stated — 'the drying up of the senses' — from its reading, [this verse] is directed toward removing that [grief]. The words 'it is not born' and so forth are aimed at negating the six modifications of existence. 'Indicatory mark' means capacity [of words]. And the capacity of the words concludes only in that much [i.e., negating modifications].

'This has not come to be' — thereby the state of being a material cause, like a lump of clay, is negated. 'Nor will it come to be' — thereby the state of being a product, like a pot and the like, is negated. The cause-effect relationship in <s>Brahman</s> is superimposed through limiting adjuncts, not ultimately real —

Therefore [the indicatory mark] does not introduce [the topic of] meditation. For now, it is only ignorance that needs to be removed. Why is meditation on <s>Brahman</s> being hastily construed? And the creation of an alternative reading is mere intellectual bravado. For the status of <s>Brahman</s> as the cause of the world is established by scripture — 'O dear one, this [world] was Being alone [in the beginning]' (Chāndogya Upaniṣad). How is the description of the nature of the <s>Ātman</s> here made for the purpose of engaging in battle? From the very beginning, if the abandonment of all action alone were intended, this verse would not need to be spoken to <s>Arjuna</s>. And the Blessed Lord has stated that the <s>Ātman</s> is free from the six modifications of existence. If, for the knower, action is impossible, then let it be so — for him too, the same [argument] would apply, and there would simply be inaction. children.translated_text: Why? Because birth and death, being adventitious [i.e., pertaining to the <s>upādhis</s>], are unavoidable. He states this:

children.text: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca /
children.translated_text: For, certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead.

children.text: tasmād aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi // BhG_2.28 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, regarding what is unavoidable, you should not grieve. (BhG 2.28)

[Commentary:] The unmanifest is <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the subtle state of the five elements. Those beings whose beginning is that [unmanifest]—they are said to have 'the unmanifest as their beginning.' The manifest—the gross state—is their middle; those whose middle is manifest are 'manifest in the middle.' The manifest state is called the gross state, because of operating in the effect. Those whose dissolution, destruction, and reabsorption is in the unmanifest—they are 'having the unmanifest as their dissolution,' dissolved into their own cause,

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [They say] the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> 'The <s>ātman</s> is indeed to be seen, to be heard' is being restated here. But this explanation is fitting only among those learned in the <s>Vedas</s>. For the recognition of that meaning is not found here. In that [<s>śruti</s>], an injunctive suffix is heard, whereas this [verse] is a descriptive statement. Nor is the meaning there 'it is to be seen as a wonder.' And merely from a superficial resemblance of syllables, a meaning found in another passage cannot be imposed [here]. Nor does this interpretation serve the contextual meaning. Moreover:

children.text: avācyavādāṃś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ11 /
children.translated_text: Your enemies will speak many unspeakable words, disparaging your ability.

children.text: nindantas tava12 sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim // BhG_2.37 //
children.translated_text: What could be more painful than that? (BhG 2.37)

children.text: ahitāḥ śatravaḥ / tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim / nv iti vitarke /
tato nānyad duḥkhataram astīty arthaḥ // 37 //
children.translated_text: There is nothing more painful than that—this is the meaning. (37)
[Commentary:] 'Enemies' means foes. 'What could be more painful than that?'—'<s>nu</s>' is [used] in the sense of deliberation.

children.text: yuddhe tu kriyamāṇe guṇā evobhayatrety āha13 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But if battle is undertaken, there is merit in either outcome—so he says:

children.text: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm14 /
children.translated_text: Either being slain you will attain heaven, or conquering you will enjoy the earth.

children.text: tasmād uttiṣṭha15 kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ // BhG_2.38 //
children.translated_text: Therefore arise, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, resolved for battle. (BhG 2.38)

children.text: mohaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha17 / yad vā (ma)yāvaśyaṃ kartavyaṃ hi
yuddham ity evaṃ kṛtaniścayaḥ // 38 //
children.translated_text: meaning 'battle'—thus having made a firm resolve. (38)
[Commentary:] Abandon delusion and arise! Or: 'I must certainly undertake this',

children.text: tatra ca yuddhapravṛttasya buddhisāmyam upadeṣṭum āha1 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And for one thus engaged in battle, to teach equanimity of mind (<s>buddhisāmya</s>), he says:

children.text: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau /
children.translated_text: Treating alike pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat,

children.text: tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpam avāpsyasi // BhG_2.39 //
children.translated_text: then engage in battle—thus you will not incur sin. (BhG 2.39)

children.text:
sukhe harṣo duḥkhe viṣādaḥ2 / tāv akṛtvā /
tayoḥ kinnimittam ity āha3 ---
lābhālābhau (samau kṛtvā) lābhe sukham alābhe
duḥkham utpadyate / tayoḥ punaḥ ko hetur ity āha4 ---
children.translated_text: suffering in loss. [He then asks] what is the cause of these:

children.text:
jayājayau / jaye lābho viparya(ye) alābha iti /
(i)dam uktaṃ kurvan na pāpaṃ5 pratyavāyam avāpsyasīsi /
tad evopasaṃhṛtam6 / anyathā papaśaṅkānupapatter iha svadharmaṃ7
kurvato yat pāpaṃ8 bhavati tan niṣidhyate9 /
atha vā pāpam iti saṃsāravyasanam / tan naivam avāpsyasi /
jñānakarmasamuccayānuṣṭhānam evam iti10 vyapadiśyate
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Victory and defeat'—in victory there is gain, in the opposite there is loss. What is stated is: acting thus, you will not incur the sin of adverse consequence. This has been concluded. Otherwise, since the apprehension of sin while performing one's own <s>dharma</s> would be untenable, the sin that might arise is here prohibited. Or alternatively, 'sin' means the affliction of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)—'thus you will not incur it.' The practice of the combination of knowledge and action (<s>jñānakarmasamuccaya</s>) is denoted by the word 'thus,'

children.text: sāmyaparyantam // 39 //
children.translated_text: [extending] up to equanimity. (39)
[Commentary:] Joy arises in pleasure, despondency in pain—without giving rise to these. [He then asks] what is their cause: 'Gain and loss'—[treating them equally:] happiness arises in gain,

children.text:
idānīṃ jñānaprakaraṇam upasaṃharati karmaṇy upāyaviśeṣo
vaktavya iti vibhāgajñāpanāya11 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he concludes the section on knowledge. [The purport is that] a specific means within action is to be stated—to indicate this division:

children.text: eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: This understanding has been declared to you with reference to <s>Sāṅkhya</s>; but hear now this [understanding] with reference to <s>Yoga</s>.

children.text: buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ12 prahāsyasi // BhG_2.40 //
children.translated_text: Endowed with which understanding, O <s>Pārtha</s>, you shall cast off the bondage of <s>karma</s>. (BhG 2.40)

children.text:
yady api sāṅkhyaśabdaḥ kāpilatantre rūḍhaḥ13
guṇapuruṣavivekajñānaṃ14 yatropadiśyate
tathāpi tad iha na gṛhyate /
na tatsādṛśyād ātmayāthātmyavivekaḥ15 sāṅkhyaśabdenātra
vyapadiśyate16 / tadviṣayā buddhir uktety arthaḥ /
yogaḥ karmānuṣṭhānopāyaḥ / phalasaṅkalparahitatvaṃ17
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> is the means of performing action — [characterized by] freedom from attachment to results,

children.text:
samatvam /
kṛtasya kriyamāṇasya vā (karmaṇaḥ) īśvarārpaṇam iti /
tvam imāṃ buddhiṃ18 śṛṇu /
tāṃ viśinaṣṭi śrotuś cittasamādhānāya19 /
children.translated_text: equanimity, and the offering of actions being done or already done to the Lord. Hear this understanding. He specifies it, for the purpose of concentrating the listener's mind.

Although the word <s>Sāṅkhya</s> is conventionally established in the <s>Kāpila</s> system, where the discriminative knowledge between <s>guṇa</s> (constituents of nature) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit) is taught, still that [meaning] is not intended here. Rather, by analogy with that, the discrimination of the true nature of the self is designated here by the word <s>Sāṅkhya</s>. The meaning is: the understanding relating to that [self-knowledge] has been stated.

karmānekajanmasañcitaṃ prahāsyasi tyakṣyasi /
children.translated_text: Endowed with which understanding, you shall cast off the bondage of <s>karma</s> — <s>karma</s> itself is bondage; the <s>karma</s> accumulated over many births — you shall abandon.

children.text:
kecid atra sāṅkhyaśabdenodgīthādyupāsanānām atimokṣasya
sampadaś ca vidhāyakaṃ2 śāstram etat sarvaṃ vyapadiśyata iti bruvate /
children.translated_text: Some say that by the word <s>Sāṅkhya</s> here, the entire scripture that enjoins the meditations on <s>udgītha</s> and the like, <s>atimokṣa</s> (transcendent liberation), and the [divine] attributes is designated.

children.text:
atrocyate / tad etad aprastutam anupayogyam ākasmikam upanyastam iti
naḥ pratibhāti / kutaḥ3 / puruṣaviśeṣaviṣayās tūpāsanāsampado
'timokṣaś ca4 / na ca tā ātmopāsanāḥ /
atra ca śokamohākulitacetasas
tadapanayanāyātmayāthātmyavarṇanārthaṃ5 prakaraṇam /
evaṃ ca kvodgīthādayaḥ kvedaṃ6 prakaraṇam /
na ca sāṅkhyaśabdaḥ paribhāṣayā vinātimokṣādiṣu varteta /
tasmāt paurvāparyaparyālocanayā7 sambandhyamāno
yo 'rthaḥ sa sāṅkhyaśabdayogyo8 vyākhyeyaḥ /
sa cāsmābhir ukta iti /
children.translated_text: To this we say: this appears to us as irrelevant, inapplicable, and arbitrarily introduced. Why? Because the meditations, attributes, and <s>atimokṣa</s> pertain to a specific [higher] person. And those are not meditations on the self. But the present context is for the purpose of describing the true nature of the self, in order to remove the grief and delusion of one whose mind is agitated. How then [can it pertain to] the <s>udgītha</s> meditations and the like, and how to this context? Nor does the word <s>Sāṅkhya</s> apply to <s>atimokṣa</s> and the like without a conventional designation. Therefore, the meaning that, when connected through consideration of the preceding and succeeding [passages], is appropriate to the word <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, is what should be explained. And that is what we have stated.

children.text: yogaśabdo 'py atra --- samatvaṃ yoga ucyate ---
children.translated_text: The word <s>Yoga</s> too, here — [as in] 'equanimity is called <s>Yoga</s>' —

children.translated_text: from this concluding statement,

children.translated_text: denotes the means of practice and should not be construed otherwise. (40)

children.text: buddhiyuktasya11 karmaṇo guṇāntaram ucyate12 ---
children.translated_text: Another merit of action performed with understanding is stated:

children.text: nehātikramanāśo 'sti13 pratyavāyo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: In this, there is no loss of effort and no adverse consequence;

children.text: svalpam apy asya14 dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt // BhG_2.41 //
children.translated_text: even a little of this <s>dharma</s> protects from great fear. (BhG 2.41)

children.text: atikrāmati saṃsāraduḥkhaṃ yena buddhiyuktena15 karmaṇā
so 'tikramaḥ / abhikrama iti kecit paṭhanti16 /
children.translated_text: that is the transcendence (<s>atikrama</s>). Some read <s>abhikrama</s> ('commencement').

children.text: arthas tu sa eva /
children.translated_text: But the meaning is the same.
That by which one transcends the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — the action endowed with understanding —

children.translated_text: connected [with benefit] — it protects, it guards the practitioner

is never fruitless — unlike the uncertain results of agriculture and the like. Nor is there any adverse consequence, as with the improper application of a physician's prescribed treatment. On the contrary, even a little

children.text:
ātmaviṣayā karmaviṣayā buddhir ekaivaikaphalatvād iti
darśayitum āha4 ---
children.translated_text: To show that the understanding relating to the self and that relating to action are one and the same, being directed toward a single fruit, he says:

children.text: vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekaiva kurunandana /
children.translated_text: The resolute understanding is one alone, O <s>Kurunandana</s> (joy of the <s>Kurus</s>);

children.text: bahuśākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām // BhG_2.42 //
children.translated_text: but the understandings of the irresolute are many-branched and endless. (BhG 2.42)

children.text:
samuccitābhyāṃ6 jñānakarmabhyām apavargo 'vāpyate
yathāgneyādibhir
itaretaraṃ yuktair yāgaiḥ svargaḥ7 /
sā ceyaṃ vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekā /
avyavasāyināṃ tu kevalakarmiṇāṃ kevalajñānavādināṃ
ca karmākaraṇe prayatamānānāṃ bahuśākhā8
children.translated_text: those who strive for the non-performance of action — the understandings are many-branched,

children.text: bahuprabhedā asaṅkhyeyāś
children.translated_text: of many divisions, and innumerable.

children.text: ca buddhayo bhavanti // 42 //

children.translated_text: Through the combination of knowledge and action, <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) is attained — just as heaven is [attained] through <s>Āgneya</s> and other rites properly combined with each other. And this resolute understanding is one. But for the irresolute — those who adhere to action alone or advocate knowledge alone,

children.text: tatra kevalakarmiṇo 'dhikṛtyāha9 ---
children.translated_text: Now, addressing the mere ritualists, he says:

children.text: yām imāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The unwise declare this flowery speech,

children.text: vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ // BhG_2.43 //
children.translated_text: delighting in the words of the <s>Veda</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, saying 'there is nothing else.' (BhG 2.43)

children.text:

agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ -- ityādiṣu ratāḥ
karmaṇā niratiśayasukhaṃ
children.translated_text: This speech that is about to be described — flowery, i.e. bearing fruit — the speech characterized by sentences — the unwise, those who do not know the self, delighting in the Vedic statements such as 'One desiring heaven should perform the <s>agnihotra</s>' and the like — [they say that] through action, unsurpassed happiness

tato 'nyad apavargākhyaṃ sukhaṃ nāstīti2
children.translated_text: 'There is no other happiness called <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) beyond that' —

children.text: vādino vadanaśīlāś

children.text: ca (pravadanti) // 43 //

denoted by the word 'heaven' is attained.

children.text: itaḥ ---

children.text: kāmātmānaḥ3 svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām /

children.text: kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati // BhG_2.44 //
children.translated_text: which is abundant in specialized rituals, aimed at enjoyment, lordship, and [rebirth in a particular] station — (BhG 2.44)

children.text:
aprāptasya prāptīcchā kāmaḥ /
tadanuraktacetasa ity arthaḥ4 /
svargaḥ paraḥ puruṣārtho yeṣāṃ te
svargaparāḥ svargapradhānāḥ / janmakarmaphalapradām /
karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ karmaphalaṃ /
janmayuktaṃ karmaphalaṃ pradadātīti janmakarmaphalapradām /
vācam ity adhikriyate / punar api kiṃviśiṣṭām /
kriyāviśeṣabahulām / kriyāṇāṃ viśeṣā (a)tibahulā
bahuprakārā yasyāṃ vāci tām /
kiṃ5 prati pravṛttām ity āha ---
bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati /
bhogaś caiśvaryaṃ ca6 tayor gatiḥ prāptis tām
uddiśya7 / bhogaḥ sukhavedanā / (aha)m eṣāṃ patiḥ svāmīti
yatrābhimāno jāyate tadāiśvaryam / athavā gater evobhayaṃ8 viśeṣaṇam
children.translated_text: arises, that is lordship. Alternatively, both are qualifiers of 'station' itself.

children.text: kīdṛśagatiṃ9 prati /
children.translated_text: Toward what kind of station?

children.text: janmakarmaphalapradāṃ kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Toward [the speech] that grants the fruit of birth and action, that is abundant in specialized rituals.

children.text: puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ (pra)tīty arthaḥ // 44 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: toward the flowery speech. (44)

Desire (<s>kāma</s>) is the wish for the attainment of what is not yet obtained — the meaning is: those whose minds are attached to that. Those for whom heaven is the highest human goal — they are <s>svargapara</s> (having heaven as supreme). 'Granting the fruit of birth and action': the fruit of action is <s>karmaphala</s>; that which gives a <s>karmaphala</s> accompanied by birth — that is 'granting the fruit of birth and action.' The word 'speech' is supplied from the previous verse. And what further characterizes it? 'Abundant in specialized rituals' — in which the specializations of rituals are exceedingly many, of many kinds — such a speech. Directed toward what? He says: 'toward enjoyment, lordship, and station.' Enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>) — their attainment is the 'station' — with reference to that. Enjoyment is the experience of pleasure. Where the sense of 'I am the master and lord of these' —

children.text: teṣāṃ caivaṃ vadatām10 ---
children.translated_text: And for those who speak thus:

children.text: bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām11 /

cittam iti1 samādhir ātmā / tasminn ātmani na vidhīyate na
sambhavatīty arthaḥ /
athavā samādhānaṃ samādhis tadviṣayā buddhiḥ /
apare punar yuktaṃ vyākhyānam ananusarantas
tatpratimānaṃ kalpayanto vadanti /
sarveṣāṃ kila karmakāṇḍagatānāṃ vākyānāṃ hi
(dvi)vidhaṃ phalam anvayanibandhanaṃ tātparyasamadhigamyaṃ ca2 /
tatrānvayikaṃ svargabrahmavarcasādiphalam anvayanibandhanam /
śamadamādihetutayānuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ vyavasāyātmikāyāṃ buddhau
yogyatāpādanaṃ tatrānvayaphalam eva svargādi
ye vadanty avipaścitas te
tātparyaphalam ajānanta iti yojayanti3 /
children.translated_text: the mind is concentrated — thus <s>samādhi</s> is the self. In that self, [the understanding] is not established — the meaning is: it does not arise. Alternatively, <s>samādhāna</s> (concentration) is <s>samādhi</s>, and the understanding relating to that [concentration]. Others, however, not following the proper interpretation and fabricating what they consider the standard [reading], say: indeed, all the statements of the <s>karma-kāṇḍa</s> (ritual section) have two kinds of fruit — one ascertained through syntactical connection and one ascertained through purport. Therein, the result connected through syntactic relation is fruits such as heaven, <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance), and the like. Those who say that the directly connected fruit such as heaven is the only fruit, through producing fitness for resolute understanding in practitioners through the development of tranquility, restraint, and the like as [their] cause — those [speakers] are the unwise, not knowing the purport-fruit — thus [the opponents] construe [the verse].

children.text:
atrābhidhīyate / tad etacchabdapramāṇabāhyaṃ
puruṣabuddhiprabhavaṃ
nyāyavidbhyo4 nātirocate /
na hi svargakāmo yajeta --- ity asya vākyasya dvāv arthau5 ---
tatra yāgena svargaṃ prāpnuyād ity ayam evaiko 'rtho vidhīyate6 /
padārthasaṃsargo hi vākyārthaḥ /
na punar yāgānuṣṭhānena7 jñānayogyatāṃ kuryād iti8
kasyacit padasya tātparyo dṛśyate9 /
padārthapūrvakaś ca vākyārtho jñāne nimittam iti sthitiḥ /
na ca puruṣecchāvaśād10 vākyasya nārthāntaram ākṣipati /
ye hi śrūyamāṇam artham anādṛtya12 vākyasyārthāntaraṃ kalpayanti13
ta eva sutarām avipaścito na mīmāṃsakā14
ye śabdapramāṇavṛttaṃ15
bruvate śamadamādayo yāgānuṣṭhānasādhyā iti16 /
kiṃ tarhi / śānto dānta uparataḥ17
children.translated_text: What then? [They are to be accomplished through:] 'One who is tranquil, self-restrained, withdrawn' —

To this we say: this [interpretation], being outside the authority of the word-[meaning], born of human imagination, does not particularly appeal to those who know proper reasoning. For the statement 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice' does not have two meanings. Among those, the one meaning that is enjoined is: 'By sacrifice one would attain heaven.' For the meaning of a sentence is the connection of word-meanings. But 'By performing sacrifice one would produce fitness for knowledge' — this purpose is not seen in any word. And the meaning of a sentence, being preceded by word-meanings, is the basis for knowledge — this is the settled position. Nor does the sentence, by the wish of a person, imply some other meaning. For those who, disregarding the meaning as heard, fabricate another meaning for the sentence — they are all the more unwise, not <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, who [claim to] state the operation of the word as a valid means of knowledge. [It is incorrect to say that] tranquility, restraint, and the like are to be accomplished through the performance of sacrifice.

sādhanāgranthagauravabhayād uparamyate1 /

āhopuruṣikāṃ loke prathayanti /

children.translated_text: and such statements, [which indicate that these qualities are] to be known through seeing the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, [leading to] the cessation of mental activity, [and that practitioners] desist out of fear of the weightiness of the texts on the means [of liberation]. And thus, various other commentators, imagining a meaning different from what precedes, propagate their self-aggrandizement in the world. Let the learned determine here what has been stated in accordance with valid authority.

ātmajñānena tu nityakarmaṇāṃ samuccayo4 vacanāntareṇa ---
tam evaṃ vedānuvaca(ne)na ---
iti niyatasya tu sannyāsaḥ karmaṇo5

children.text: nopapadyate --- iti ca tyāgapratiṣedhāt teṣām
children.translated_text: is not tenable — and because there is a prohibition of abandonment of those very

children.text: evātmanām6 // 45 //
children.translated_text: actions. (45)
But the combination of self-knowledge with regular obligatory actions (<s>nityakarma</s>) is [established] by another statement — 'Knowing him thus through the teaching of the <s>Veda</s>' —

children.text: traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> deal with the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature); be free from the three <s>guṇas</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: nirdvandvo nityasattvastho7 niryogakṣema ātmavān // BhG_2.46 //
children.translated_text: free from dualities, ever established in <s>sattva</s>, without [concern for] acquisition and preservation, self-possessed. (BhG 2.46)

trayāṇāṃ sattvarajastamasāṃ guṇānāṃ karma
ta(t) traiguṇyam /
sa viṣayaḥ prakāśayitavyo8 yeṣāṃ
vedānāṃ te traiguṇyaviṣayāḥ /
guṇānāṃ ca saṃsārapravartanaṃ karma /
tadviṣayā vedāḥ / tatra sattvam upasarjanam /

ihāmutraphaleṣu
karmasu pravartamānaḥ saṃsāracakraṃ nātivartata iti
tātparyārthaḥ10 /
tvaṃ tu11 nistraiguṇyo bhava /
traiguṇyam ativartasva / katham /
nirdvandvaḥ nityasattvasthaḥ12 /
kāmakrodhau13 rāgadveṣau sukhaduḥkhe śītoṣṇe14
iti dvandvāni15 tāni sahasvety arthaḥ /
sattvaguṇastho bhūtvā dhairyam
avalambya / niryogakṣemaś ca /
aprāptasya svīkaraṇaṃ yogaḥ
prāptasya pari(rakṣaṇaṃ) kṣemaḥ /
tayor yatamānasya16 na
children.translated_text: For one striving for those two, there is no

children.text: vyavasāyātmikā17 buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: resolute intellect.

children.text: ātmavān apramatta ity arthaḥ18 // 46 //
children.translated_text: Self-possessed and vigilant — that is the meaning. // 46 //

[Commentary:] The action of the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — is <s>traiguṇya</s> (the threefold quality). The <s>Vedas</s> whose subject matter is to illumine that are called 'having <s>traiguṇya</s> as their subject.' And the action of the <s>guṇas</s> is the impelling of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). The <s>Vedas</s> deal with that. Therein, <s>sattva</s> is subordinate. <s>Rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, however, are predominant. Overpowered by these two, a person engaging in actions aimed at fruits here and hereafter does not transcend the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the purport. But you — be beyond the three <s>guṇas</s>. Transcend the <s>traiguṇya</s>. How? By being free from pairs of opposites and ever established in <s>sattva</s>. Desire and anger, attraction and aversion, pleasure and pain, cold and heat — these are the pairs of opposites; endure them — that is the meaning. Being established in the <s>sattva guṇa</s>, taking hold of steadfastness. And free from <s>yoga-kṣema</s> (acquisition and preservation). <s>Yoga</s> is the acquisition of what is not yet obtained; <s>kṣema</s> is the preservation of what is obtained.
