na ca traiguṇyaviṣayeṣu vedeṣv
adhyayanaśravaṇavyākhyānādipareṇa
tvayā kṛtsnam āyuḥ paryupayoktavyam1 /
kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And you should not spend your entire life occupied with study, hearing, and expounding of the <s>Vedas</s> that have the <s>traiguṇya</s> as their subject. Why? He says:

children.text: yāvad artha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake /
children.translated_text: Whatever purpose is served by a well when there is water flooding everywhere,

children.text: tāvān sarveṣu vede(ṣu) brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ // BhG_2.47 //
children.translated_text: that much purpose is served in all the <s>Vedas</s> for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows. // BhG 2.47 //

children.text:
kūpataḍāgādau yāvān arthaḥ snānapānādiḥ2
puruṣasya tāvān arthaḥ
salilapūrṇe deśe prāvṛṭsamaye3 nādhiko vidyate /
yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntas tathā4 jñānakarmasamuccayapratipādanapare
vedabhāge5 yāvān arthas tāvān ekāhāhīnasatrapratipādake6
kṛtsnavede / ataḥ kāmyakarmābhiyogaṃ7 vihāya
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning the pursuit of desire-motivated actions,

children.text:
jñānakarmanityakarmapratipādanaparabhoge
'bhiyogavatā bhavitavyam iti /
children.translated_text: one should be devoted to the portion directed at teaching knowledge, action, and obligatory rites.

[Commentary:] Whatever purpose a person has in a well, pond, or reservoir — such as bathing and drinking — that much purpose exists in a land filled with water during the rainy season, no more. Just as this example illustrates, so in the portion of the <s>Veda</s> directed at teaching the combination of knowledge and action, whatever purpose exists, the same exists in the entire <s>Veda</s> that teaches <s>ekāha</s>, <s>ahīna</s>, and <s>sattra</s> sacrifices.

children.text:
apareṣāṃ vyākhyā --- yāvān arthaḥ sarvataḥ saṃplutodake
tāvān udapāne tatkārye tatraivāntarbhavatīty arthaḥ /
tathā vijānataḥ sannyāsino jñāne sarvataḥ
saṃplutodakasthānīye(ṣu9)
sarveṣu vedeṣu tāvān arthaḥ /
tatraiva samastakarmaprayojanam
antarbhavatīty arthaḥ10 iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The interpretation of others — 'Whatever purpose exists in water flooding everywhere, that much in a well, being included therein' — that is the meaning. Similarly, for the knower, the <s>sannyāsin</s>, in knowledge — which stands in the place of water flooding everywhere — all the <s>Vedas</s> have that much purpose. The purpose of all actions is included therein — that is the meaning.

tad asmin vyākhyāne11 yadi jñānam āhātmyaṃ tadānīm

vihāya tatsamparkād

raso 'pi tāmrasamparkāt puruṣārthasādhanam15 /
evam anyonyasamuccitam apavargārtham ity uktam16 /
tathā ca vasiṣṭhenoktam17 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In this interpretation, if the greatness of knowledge is asserted, then this greatness of knowledge is being acknowledged: that <s>karma</s> which, for those who are desire-natured, becomes a cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, abandoning its own nature and through association with knowledge, attains the status of a cause for elevation. Just as copper touched by the philosopher's stone attains the state of gold. And the philosopher's stone too, through association with copper, becomes a means to human goals. Thus, the two combined serve the purpose of liberation — so it is stated. And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> has said:

children.translated_text: 'Just as food combined with honey, and honey combined with food — so too <s>tapas</s> (austerity) and <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) combined are a great medicine.'

athaitad vyākhyāne2 karma niṣprayojanaṃ vaktavyaṃ3 /
jñānād eva kevalād apavargaṃ ity abhiprāyeṇa /
tad asad ity ucyate4 /

vakṣyate / brāhmaṇasyeti ca sāmānyaśravaṇaṃ na sanyāsina iti
viśiṣṭam /
tasmāt sarvāśramāṇāṃ sarvadvijānāṃ ca muktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore liberation belongs to all <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) and all twice-born.

children.text: tathā ca janakādayaḥ smaryante /
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Janaka</s> and others are remembered as examples.

children.text: tasmād vyavasāyātmikāyāṃ6 buddho sthātavyam iti sthitam // 47 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that one should remain established in resolute intellect. // 47 //

[Commentary:] But in the other interpretation, <s>karma</s> would have to be declared purposeless — with the intent that liberation comes from knowledge alone. That is wrong, it is said — because this meaning is outside the authority of verbal testimony. This has been stated elsewhere and will be stated more precisely. And the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' is a general term, not the specific term '<s>sannyāsin</s>'.

children.text: tatra yad uktam --- yoge tv imām --- iti ko 'sau yoga ity āha7 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Regarding what was said — 'In this <s>yoga</s>' — what is this <s>yoga</s>? He says:

children.text: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana /
children.translated_text: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits.

children.text: mā karmaphalahetur bhūrmā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi // BhG_2.48 //
children.translated_text: Do not be the cause of the fruit of action; nor let your attachment be to inaction. // BhG 2.48 //

children.text: svāśramavihiteṣu karmasv adhikāraḥ / phaleṣu cānadhikāraḥ8 /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] You have the right to actions prescribed for your own <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life). And no right to the fruits.

children.text: meti(śabdaḥ) pratiṣedhavācī / nāsty adhikāraḥ9 /
children.translated_text: The word 'mā' means prohibition. There is no right to fruits.

karmaṇy evety evakāraḥ phalavyavacchedārtho na
jñānavyavacchedārthaḥ10 /
tasya --- eṣā te 'bhihitā -- ityādyupadiṣṭatvāt11 /

children.text: nanu karmaṇy e(va)kāraḥ phalaṃ hi kriyāsādhyam /
children.translated_text: Now, the particle 'eva' applies to action — for fruit is accomplished through action.

children.text: na tatrāpi prasakto 'sau yena pratiṣidhyeta ity āśaṅkyāha14 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One is not attached to that either, such that it should be prohibited — anticipating this objection, he says:

children.text: mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi // 48 //
children.translated_text: Let there be no attachment to inaction for you. // 48 //
[Commentary:] The particle 'eva' in 'karmaṇy eva' (to action alone) is for excluding fruits, not for excluding knowledge.

Since this is so, therefore seek refuge in the intellect — take the intellect as your shelter, that is the meaning. At the time of engaging in action, those whose cause of action is merely the fruit of action are pitiable (<s>kṛpaṇāḥ</s>). // 50 //

tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What fruit does one who acts while endowed with intellect obtain? That is stated:

children.text: buddhiyukto jahātīme ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte /
children.translated_text: Endowed with the <s>yoga</s> of intellect, the wise abandon here both merit and sin.

children.text: tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam // BhG_2.51 //
children.translated_text: Therefore devote yourself to <s>yoga</s>. <s>Yoga</s> is skill in actions. // BhG 2.51 //

children.text:
īśvarārādhanārthaṃ1 karmety anayā buddhyā
yuktaḥ karma kurvan parityajaty anārabdhaphale
janmāntarakṛte2 śubhāśubhakarmaṇī /
ye tv ārabdhaphale tayor bhogenaiva kṣayaḥ3 /
asmin śarīre tayor bhogarūpeṇa4 pariṇatatvāt /
tathā ca śrutiḥ ---
tasya tāvad eva ciraṃ yāva(d asmāc charīrā)n na
vimokṣye 'tha sampatsya iti /
yāvad asmāc charīrān na vimokṣyate5
tāvad asya viduṣaś ciram ity avadhikaraṇāt /
tasmāt samatvayogāya6 yujyasva /
kaḥ punar yogaḥ / (yogaḥ) karmasu kauśalam /
idaṃ tāvad brahmaṇi7 samarpaṇaṃ karmaṇaḥ
phalasaṅkalparahitatā ca // 51 //
children.translated_text: and freedom from the desire for fruits. // 51 //

[Commentary:] Endowed with the understanding that action is for the worship of <s>Īśvara</s>, one who performs action thereby abandons good and bad <s>karma</s> whose fruits have not yet begun to manifest, performed in other births. As for those whose fruits have already begun to manifest, they are exhausted through experience alone — because they have already matured into the form of experience in this body. And thus the <s>śruti</s> says: 'His delay is only as long as he is not freed from this body — then he will attain.' Since the word 'as long as' sets a limit — meaning the delay of such a wise person is only that long. Therefore devote yourself to the <s>yoga</s> of equanimity. What then is <s>yoga</s>? <s>Yoga</s> is skill in actions. This means the offering of actions to <s>Brahman</s>

children.text: kiṃ punar evaṃ kṛte syāt8 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What happens when one does thus?

children.text: karmajaṃ9 buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ10 /
children.translated_text: The wise, endowed with the <s>yoga</s> of intellect, having abandoned the fruit born of action,

children.text: janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ11 padaṃ gacchanty anāpayam12 // BhG_2.52 //
children.translated_text: freed from the bondage of birth, go to the state beyond affliction. // BhG 2.52 //

children.text: śubhetarakarmajaṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā13 manīṣiṇo manasa īṣiṇo14
brahmabhāvāpāditamanovṛttayo15 janmaiva bandhas tato
children.translated_text: those whose mental modifications have been brought to the state of <s>Brahman</s> — from birth itself, which is bondage, from that

children.text: vinirmuktāḥ16 padaṃ viṣṇoḥ sthānaṃ gacchanty anāmayaṃ
children.translated_text: freed, they go to the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the state beyond affliction,

children.text: sarvopadravarahitam // 52 //
children.translated_text: free from all calamity. // 52 //
[Commentary:] Having abandoned the fruit born of good and other <s>karma</s>, the wise — those who rule the mind,

children.text: kadā punar evaṃ kramas tvaṃ śuddhatarabuddhir nirvedaṃ
pratipadyase / tad āha17 ---
children.translated_text: <s>nirveda</s> (dispassion)? To that he says:
[Commentary:] When will you, following this course and with a thoroughly purified intellect, attain

children.text: yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhir vyatitariṣyati /
children.translated_text: When your intellect shall cross beyond the thicket of delusion,

children.text: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca // BhG_2.53 //
children.translated_text: then you shall attain <s>nirveda</s> (dispassion) regarding what is yet to be heard and what has been heard. // BhG 2.53 //

2. ... nāravrakale janmāntarakṛte

4. tayārbhogatūpeṇa

6. samatvaṃ yogāya

children.text:
kalilaṃ gahanam ucyate / tathā cābhidhānakośe ---
kalilaṃ gahanaṃ viduḥ --- iti /
moha eva kalilam / moho 'jñānam / etad uktaṃ
bhavati --- ajñānaṃ durgaṃ yadā vyatikramiṣyasi
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ
children.translated_text: then you shall attain <s>nirveda</s> (dispassion)

children.text: śrotavyasya3 śāstrasya śrutasya ca /
children.translated_text: regarding scripture that is yet to be heard and what has been heard.

children.text: tadā ca mohadurgaṃ vyatitīrya te
children.translated_text: And then, having crossed the wilderness of delusion, your

children.text: buddhiḥ sthiram avasthāsyata2 iti // 53 //
children.translated_text: intellect will stand firm. // 53 //

[Commentary:] <s>Kalila</s> means 'thicket' or 'dense forest.' And thus in the lexicon: '<s>Kalila</s> is known as dense forest.' Delusion itself is the thicket. Delusion means ignorance. What is meant is: when you shall cross the impenetrable wilderness of ignorance,

children.text: śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā /
children.translated_text: When your intellect, confused by the contradictions of <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture), shall stand unshaken,

children.text: samādhāv acalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi // BhG_2.54 //
children.translated_text: immovable in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), then you shall attain <s>yoga</s>. // BhG 2.54 //

children.text:
acalā iti punar vivakṣyate3 / tadā paramātmayogam avāpsyasi /
tataḥ4 pūrvoktam upapannam --- padaṃ gacchanty anāmayam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Immovable' is stated again with further intent. Then you shall attain union with the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self). Therefore what was said earlier is established — 'they go to the state beyond affliction.'

children.text:
anantaravṛttena ślokadvayena buddher niścalatve pratipādite
paramātmano 'bhimukhīkaraṇāyāvasaraṃ labdhvārjuna uvāca5 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having established the steadiness of the intellect through the immediately preceding two verses, and having obtained the occasion to direct [<s>Arjuna</s>] toward the <s>Paramātman</s>, <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava /
children.translated_text: 'What is the description of one of steady wisdom (<s>sthitaprajña</s>), O <s>Keśava</s>, of one established in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption)?

children.text: sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta6 kim āsīta vrajeta kim7 // BhG_2.55 //
children.translated_text: How does the one of steady intellect speak? How does he sit? How does he move?' // BhG 2.55 //

children.text:
sthitaprajñaḥ kena lakṣaṇena bhāṣyate vyapadiśyata ity arthaḥ /
sa ca sthi(ta)dhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kim asau vaktīty arthaḥ /
kimparo bhūtvāsītety arthaḥ9 /
children.translated_text: With what as his highest [aim] does he remain — this is the meaning.

children.text: (a)karmakatvād asya dhātor evaṃ10 yojyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because this verbal root is intransitive, it should be construed thus.

children.text: kiṃ vā vrajeta gacchet prāpnuyād iti11 /
children.translated_text: Or 'how does he move' — how does he go, i.e., what does he attain?

children.text: vyatyayenātmanepadam // 55 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) is used by interchange. // 55 //

[Commentary:] One of steady wisdom — by what characteristic is he described, i.e., designated? — this is the meaning. And how does that one of steady intellect speak — what does he say? — this is the meaning.

children.text: tatra --- kā bhāṣā --- ity etat prathamaṃ nirucyate12 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There, 'what is the description' — this is first explained:

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text:
1. śrutavyasya
2. vyatidhiramavasthāsyate
3. vivakṣyate
4. tato
5. anantaravṛtena ślokadayena paramātmābhimukhāyā buddheniścalatve
pratipādite vasaraladhyārtuna uvāca 55
6. prabhāseta
7. vrajota kim
8. vakratyarthaḥ
9. kiṃ parā bhūtvāsītity artha
10. dhyetorevaṃ
11. vrajetarāchetprāpnu^
12. ityatatpra ... nirucyate 56
children.translated_text: [Manuscript variant readings:] 1. śrutavyasya 2. vyatidhiramavasthāsyate 3. vivakṣyate 4. tato 5. anantaravṛtena ślokadayena paramātmābhimukhāyā buddheniścalatve pratipādite vasaraladhyārtuna uvāca 55 6. prabhāseta 7. vrajota kim 8. vakratyarthaḥ 9. kiṃ parā bhūtvāsītity artha 10. dhyetorevaṃ 11. vrajetarāchetprāpnu^ 12. ityatatpra ... nirucyate 56

children.text: śrībhagavān uvāca ---
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: aiśvaryasya sa(ma)grasya dharmasya (ya)śasaḥ śriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Etymology of <s>Bhagavān</s>:] 'Of sovereignty complete, of <s>dharma</s>, of fame, of beauty,

children.text: vairāgyasyātha mokṣasya ṣaṇṇāṃ1 bhaga iti dhvaniḥ //
children.translated_text: of renunciation, and of liberation — of these six, <s>bhaga</s> is the designation.'

children.text: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān /
children.translated_text: 'When one completely abandons all desires arising from the mind, O <s>Pārtha</s>,

children.text: ātmany evātmanā tuṣṭaḥ2 sthitaprajñas tadocyate // BhG_2.56 //
children.translated_text: content in the self alone by the self — then one is called a person of steady wisdom (<s>sthitaprajña</s>).' // BhG 2.56 //

children.text:
bāhyārthaviṣayān3 nānāsāṅkalpān yadā tyajati (tadā)
bāhyaviṣayasaṅkalpābhāve kvāyaṃ vartate4 /
kena tuṣṭaś caratīty
āha ---
ātmany evānandasvarūpe 'mohitenātmanāntaḥkaraṇena5
janmamaraṇajamohādiviṣādena
mahauṣadhabrahmāmṛtapānāsvādajanitapremaprabandhaniścalavṛttinā
parituṣṭaḥ6 sthitaprajñas tadocyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When one abandons the various resolutions pertaining to external objects — [the question arises:] in the absence of resolutions about external objects, where does he abide? And content with what does he conduct himself? He says: content in the self alone, which is of the nature of bliss, with an undeluded inner organ, with a mental disposition made steady by a continuous flow of love generated by tasting the nectar of <s>Brahman</s>, the great medicine [that cures] the despondency born of the delusion arising from birth and death — one is then called a <s>sthitaprajña</s>.

children.text:
yānīha sthitaprajñalakṣaṇāni vakṣyante
(tāny eva) sādhanāni
prayatnato 'nuṣṭheyānīti /
na hy ananuṣṭhīyamānāni sattāṃ
labhamānāni7 lakṣaṇāni bhavantīti /
tatra yad etad ucyate8 pūrvāvasthāyāṃ lakṣaṇam9 ---
iti tad anupapannam /
tasminn eva kāle sādhanatvaṃ tasmi(nn eva ca kāle)
children.translated_text: — [and] at that same time it is a means, and at that same [later] time

children.text: lakṣaṇa(tva)m --- iti tad anupapannam10 /
children.translated_text: it is a characteristic — that is untenable.

children.text: (na) tasmi(n) yaugapadyaṃ sādhanatvalakṣaṇatvayoḥ // 56 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The simultaneity of being both a means and a characteristic in the same [thing] is not [possible]. // 56 //

[Commentary:] The characteristics of the <s>sthitaprajña</s> that will be stated here are themselves the means to be practiced with effort. For characteristics do not come into existence without being practiced. Therefore, the claim that 'this is a characteristic of the prior stage'

children.text: kiṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: duḥkheṣv anudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One whose mind is not agitated in sorrows, who is free from longing for pleasures,

children.text: vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhī munir ucyate // BhG_2.57 //
children.translated_text: from whom passion, fear, and anger have departed — he is called a sage of steady intellect.' // BhG 2.57 //

children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text:
1. ṣasmāṃ
2. ātmanastuṣṭa
3. vāllārthaviṣayān
4. tkvāyaṃ vartanaḥ
5. ^svarūpemāhitemātmānāntakaraṇena
6. janmajamaraṇamahārāviṣādena mahoṣadhī niścalabṛttīnaḥ parituṣṭa
7. ... prapatnatonuṣṭepāni / nahyanuṣṭīyani sattāṃ labhadhamānāni
8. yattvetaducyate
9. pūrvāvasthāyāṃ vasthāyāṃ
10. tadanupapannaṃ
children.translated_text: [Manuscript variant readings:] 1. ṣasmāṃ 2. ātmanastuṣṭa 3. vāllārthaviṣayān 4. tkvāyaṃ vartanaḥ 5. ^svarūpemāhitemātmānāntakaraṇena 6. janmajamaraṇamahārāviṣādena mahoṣadhī niścalabṛttīnaḥ parituṣṭa 7. ... prapatnatonuṣṭepāni / nahyanuṣṭīyani sattāṃ labhadhamānāni 8. yattvetaducyate 9. pūrvāvasthāyāṃ vasthāyāṃ 10. tadanupapannaṃ
[Page 76]

children.text: yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śubhāśubham /
children.translated_text: 'One who is without attachment everywhere, upon encountering good or evil,

children.text: nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā // BhG_2.58 //
children.translated_text: who neither rejoices nor hates — his wisdom is firmly established.' // BhG 2.58 //

children.text: yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And when this one withdraws the senses from sense-objects completely, as a tortoise its limbs,

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyaḥ sthitaprajñas tadocyate // BhG_2.59 //
children.translated_text: then he is called one of steady wisdom.' // BhG 2.59 //

children.text: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sense-objects turn away from the abstinent embodied being,

children.text: rasavarjaṃ raso 'py asya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate // BhG_2.60 //
children.translated_text: except for the taste. But even the taste of this one turns away upon seeing the Supreme.' // BhG 2.60 //

children.text: yatato hy api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the turbulent senses, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, of even a striving man of discernment,

children.text: indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ // BhG_2.61 //
children.translated_text: forcibly carry away the mind.' // BhG 2.61 //

children.text: tāni saṃyamya manasā yukta āsīta matparaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having restrained all of them, one should sit disciplined, intent on Me;

children.text: vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā // BhG_2.62 //
children.translated_text: for one whose senses are under control — his wisdom is firmly established.' // BhG 2.62 //

children.text: dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate /
children.translated_text: 'When a person contemplates sense-objects, attachment to them arises;

children.text: saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate // BhG_2.63 //
children.translated_text: from attachment is born desire; from desire arises anger.' // BhG 2.63 //

children.text: krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛtivibhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory;

children.text: smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśāt praṇaśyati // BhG_2.64 //
children.translated_text: from the destruction of memory comes the destruction of intellect; from the destruction of intellect, one perishes.' // BhG 2.64 //

children.text: rāgadveṣaviyuktais tu viṣayān indriyaiś caran /
children.translated_text: 'But one who moves among sense-objects with senses free from attraction and aversion,

children.text: ātmavaśyair vidheyātmā prasādam adhigacchati // BhG_2.65 //
children.translated_text: self-controlled, with a disciplined self — he attains clarity.' // BhG 2.65 //

children.text: prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānir asyopajāyate /
children.translated_text: 'In clarity, there arises the cessation of all sorrows;

children.text: prasannacetaso hy āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate // BhG_2.66 //
children.translated_text: for the intellect of one whose mind is clear quickly becomes firmly established.' // BhG 2.66 //

children.text: nāsti buddhir ayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: 'There is no intellect for the undisciplined, nor for the undisciplined is there contemplation;

children.text: na cābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham // BhG_2.67 //
children.translated_text: for one who does not contemplate, there is no peace; for the unpeaceful, whence happiness?' // BhG 2.67 //

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yan mano 'nuvidhīyate /
children.translated_text: 'For when the mind conforms to the wandering senses,

children.text: tad asya harati prajñāṃ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi // BhG_2.68 //
children.translated_text: it carries away his wisdom, as the wind a boat on the waters.' // BhG 2.68 //
[Page 77]

children.text: tasmād yasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, O mighty-armed one, he whose senses are completely restrained

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā // BhG_2.69 //
children.translated_text: from their objects — his wisdom is firmly established.' // BhG 2.69 //

children.text: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī /
children.translated_text: 'That which is night for all beings — therein the self-controlled one is awake;

children.text: yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ // BhG_2.70 //
children.translated_text: that in which beings are awake — that is night for the sage who sees.' // BhG 2.70 //

children.text: āpūryamāṇam acalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat /
children.translated_text: 'As the ocean, which remains unmoved and steady, [receives] the waters entering it,

children.text: tadvat kāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntim āpnoti na kāmakāmī // BhG_2.71 //
children.translated_text: so too, one into whom all desires enter [without disturbing] attains peace — not the desirer of desires.' // BhG 2.71 //

children.text: vihāya kāman yaḥ sarvān pumāṃś carati niḥspṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who abandons all desires and moves about free from longing,

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati // BhG_2.72 //
children.translated_text: without possessiveness, without egoism — he attains peace.' // BhG 2.72 //

children.text: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati /
children.translated_text: 'This is the state of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brāhmī sthiti</s>), O <s>Pārtha</s>; having attained it, one is not deluded.',

children.text: sthitvāsyām antakakāle 'pi brahmanirvāṇam ṛcchati // BhG_2.73 //
children.translated_text: 'Being established in it even at the time of death, one attains the <s>nirvāṇa</s> (extinction) of <s>Brahman</s>.' // BhG 2.73 //

children.text: iti śrībhagavadbhāskarakṛte gītābhāṣye dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter in the Blessed <s>Bhāskara</s>'s <s>Gītā Bhāṣya</s>.
[Page 78]

children.text: atha tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the third chapter.

children.text:
arjuna uvāca ---
jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana /
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava // BhG_3.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said: 'If intellect is considered by you to be superior to action, O <s>Janārdana</s>, then why do you engage me in this terrible action, O <s>Keśava</s>?' // BhG 3.1 //

children.text: vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me /
children.translated_text: 'With seemingly contradictory speech, you confuse my intellect, as it were.',

children.text: tad ekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo 'ham āpnuyām // BhG_3.2 //
children.translated_text: 'Tell me that one thing, having decided, by which I may attain the highest good.' // BhG 3.2 //

children.text: bhagavān uvāca ---
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: loke 'smiṃ dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha /
children.translated_text: 'In this world, a twofold discipline was taught by Me of old, O sinless one —

children.text: jñānayogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām // BhG_3.3 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yoga</s> of knowledge for the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, and the <s>yoga</s> of action for the <s>yogins</s>.' // BhG 3.3 //

children.text:
(asmin loke niṣṭhā dvividhā sthitiḥ lakṣaṇahetuḥ /
jñānam eva yogaḥ / tena sāṅkhyā jñānino lakṣyante /)
yathā1 tridaṇḍena tridaṇḍo 'nāśramī lakṣyate /
ekārthatvāt / evaṃ karmayogena yogināṃ samatvam ayogavatām
īśvarārādhanārthaṃ karma kurvatāṃ sākṣātkarmaṇo 'pi
jñānotpattyupāyatvāt2 / tathā coktam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In this world, the twofold discipline (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) is the twofold way of abiding, which is the characteristic cause. Knowledge itself is <s>yoga</s>; by it the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, the knowers, are characterized — just as by the triple staff the triple-staff-bearer, the non-resident ascetic, is characterized — because of having the same referent. Likewise, by the <s>yoga</s> of action, the <s>yogins</s> — those who lack equanimity but perform action for the sake of worshipping the Lord — [are characterized], since even action directly is a means for the arising of knowledge. And thus it is said:

children.text: jñānam utpadyate puṃsāṃ kṣayāt pāpasya karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Knowledge arises in persons from the exhaustion of sinful <s>karma</s>;

children.translated_text: 'Not through action, not through progeny, not through wealth — through renunciation alone did they attain immortality.' Here, because of the association with 'progeny,' what is praised is the renunciation of desire-motivated action for the attainment of the world [of <s>Brahman</s>]. The other <s>śruti</s> too: 'They say <s>nyāsa</s> surpasses austerity' — here the word '<s>nyāsa</s>' denotes <s>Brahman</s>, not the renunciation of action. [In the statement] 'the spoken word' — since restraint of the senses (<s>dama</s>), tranquility (<s>śama</s>), and austerities are means to attaining that [<s>Brahman</s>], the statement that [<s>nyāsa</s>] surpasses them is with reference to that [which is to be attained]. For what is to be attained surpasses the means of attaining. Others use the word '<s>sannyāsa</s>' in the same sense as '<s>nyāsa</s>' [i.e., <s>Brahman</s>]. Just as [in the expression] 'They praise with the <s>ājyas</s>' — the word '<s>ājya</s>' [meaning 'ghee' in ordinary usage] is used in [the context of] <s>stotras</s> (hymns of praise). Here, through confusion, [the word <s>nyāsa</s>] has been construed as meaning renunciation. For indeed: 'Confusion of understanding in people arises merely from the sound [of a word]; a word whose context has not been properly considered leads to a different understanding.' And in the <s>itihāsa</s> (epic literature), it is stated here and there that those seeking <s>mok���a</s> should perform action. As in the question of <s>Śuka</s>: 'One who is always devoted to <s>dharma</s> through action, mind, and speech, and who has achieved [the state of] desirelessness for fruits — he attains <s>mokṣa</s>.'

Moreover, if the renunciation of action were prescribed even for the ignorant, then the statement of the reason — 'because action is purposeless for the knower' — would be untenable. Thus, one who makes such contradictory statements —

children.translated_text: The claim that 'there is no adverse consequence for non-performance' is false — because of the <s>smṛti</s> [which says]: 'One who does not perform the prescribed action...' Nor is a renunciation performed by one's own whim in scripture capable of preventing adverse consequences. Nor can it be said that non-performance, being a non-entity, is not a cause of adverse consequences — because we observe the faults of punishment, imprisonment, and such for servants who do not carry out the orders of the king. As for [the <s>śruti</s>] 'How could the existent be born from the non-existent?' — this <s>śruti</s> has reference to material substance. The meaning there is: the production of a different material substance from a non-existent [substance] does not occur. For a [real] substance, such as gold and the like, must be accepted [as the cause]. And without a substance that has states, a [new] state is impossible — with this intent, the negation of production from non-being [is made]. Likewise, even in the performance of prescribed actions, there is purpose: for those seeking <s>mokṣa</s>, the exhaustion of sin; for others, worldly prosperity. Therefore, it is established that in the <s>Gītā</s> scripture and elsewhere, action is conducive to <s>mokṣa</s>, not that action should not be performed.

children.translated_text: But enough with this digression. (3)

How so? Because the meditation on the components of <s>udgītha</s> and the like is for the purpose of prosperity [of rituals], it does not lead to liberation. 'One should meditate on the syllable <s>Om</s> as the <s>udgītha</s>' — this prescribes the meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s> as a component of <s>udgītha</s>, not meditation on <s>Brahman</s>. Thus it is established there. And the connection with the meditation on <s>udgītha</s> and the like does not make this [<s>karma</s>] a cause of liberation. What then? 'Through sacrifice, through charity' — [it is] through the subsidiary role [of action] in conjunction with self-knowledge, and the application of this [is discussed]

sāṅkhyā parivrājakā bruvate ---
kevalād eva jñānān muktiḥ
sarvaṃ śrautaṃ smārtaṃ ca karma tyaktavyam ahetutvād7 iti /
teṣāṃ pratyākhyānāya bhagavān uvāca ---
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> — the wandering ascetics — say: 'Liberation comes from knowledge alone; all scriptural and traditional action must be renounced because it is not a cause [of liberation].' To refute them, the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śnute /
children.translated_text: Not by abstaining from action does a person attain freedom from action (<s>naiṣkarmya</s>);

anārambhān mokṣaṃ puruṣo nāśnute na
prāpnoti /

karmasāpekṣāj jñānān muktir na kevalād ityabhiprāyaḥ11 /
atha manya(se) kiṃ karmaṇā parivrajyāsahitāj
jñānān niḥśreyaḥ
sambhavaviṣyatīti12 cen nety āha ---
na ca sannyasanād eva ---
jñānasahitāt sannyāsād eva
children.translated_text: <s>Naiṣkarmya</s> (freedom from action) means the state of being free from <s>karma</s>. By the word '<s>karma</s>,' both merit and demerit are meant. Being free from that — <s>mokṣa</s> — is the meaning. Not by abstaining from action does a person attain <s>mokṣa</s>. The implied meaning is: through undertaking [action], one does attain [it]. The intent is: liberation comes from knowledge conjoined with action, not from knowledge alone. Now, if you think: 'Will the highest good come from knowledge combined with the renunciation of worldly life alone, without action?' — to that he says: 'Nor by renunciation alone' — not by renunciation conjoined with knowledge alone, through the taking of the fourth <s>āśrama</s> [i.e., <s>sannyāsa</s>],

turyāśramagrahaṇāt siddhiṃ mokṣaṃ nādhigacchati1 /
karmasahitam eva jñānaṃ siddhisādhanam /
āśramapāratantryān manasaḥ /

children.translated_text: does one attain perfection, i.e. <s>mokṣa</s>. Knowledge conjoined with action alone is the means to perfection. The mind is dependent on the <s>āśrama</s> [stages of life]. Perfection comes from the combination of all <s>āśramas</s> — this is the settled and certain view of the Blessed Lord.

children.text: yathedam eva3 sāṅkhyadarśanam āśritya sarvadharmatyāgam ekavaiṇavino
vadanti / te 'pi hy etenāpāstā veditavyāḥ4

children.text: nirākaraṇanyāyasyāviśeṣāt5 /
children.translated_text: since the principle of refutation applies equally [to them].
Just as those who, relying on this very <s>Sāṃkhya</s> philosophy, advocate the abandonment of all <s>dharma</s> while carrying a single bamboo staff (<s>ekavainavin</s>) —

children.text:
atra te pratyavatiṣṭhante ---
asmaddarśane 'pīyaṃ6 gītā ghaṭate /
kathaṃ karmārambhād eva naiṣkarmyam aśnute7
jñānotpattyupāyatvāt8 karmaṇāṃ /
tasmāt karma kartavyam / tato jñānotpattiḥ / tato mokṣa iti9 /
na ca sannyasanād eva jñānarahitāt siddhiṃ samadhigacchatīti10 /
children.translated_text: Here they counter-argue: 'This <s>Gītā</s> is compatible with our philosophy too. How so? Through the undertaking of action alone, one attains freedom from action — because actions are the means for the arising of knowledge. Therefore action must be performed. From that, the arising of knowledge. From that, <s>mokṣa</s>.' And: 'Nor by renunciation devoid of knowledge alone does one attain perfection.'

children.text:
tad idam apavyākhyānam anye pratyācakṣate /
yadi tāvad ayam artho

children.translated_text: then there would be a contradiction here: from the undertaking of action, there is no absence of action. Rather, it is only from non-undertaking [that the absence of action results].

sarvakarmaṇām17 --- iti /
children.translated_text: Now, if the word <s>naiṣkarmya</s> means 'devotion to knowledge,' [and the argument is that] 'without performing action, the arising of knowledge is impossible' — even so, [the opponent's] teaching of total renunciation of action for the ignorant would be contradicted. And thus it is said in the instructional text: 'For the purpose of discriminating the meaning of the word "you" (<s>tvam</s>), there is the renunciation of all actions.'
Others reject this as a misinterpretation. If the meaning were this — <s>naiṣkarmya</s> means 'freedom from action,' the absence of action —

asyāyam arthaḥ ---
naiṣkarmyaṃ18 mokṣaḥ /
karmārambhān mokṣaṃ19 prāpnotīti /
evam api
children.translated_text: The meaning of this [verse] is: <s>naiṣkarmya</s> means <s>mokṣa</s>. Through the undertaking of action, one attains <s>mokṣa</s>. Even so,

kevalakarmaṇāṃ mokṣaḥ prasajyata iti jñānopadeśānarthakyam1 /
atha jñānasahitāt karmaṇas tatprāptir ity evaṃ saty aṅgīkṛto
'smatpakṣo2 bhavatā bhadramukhena3 /
evaṃ ca pūrvārdhe vyākhyāte4 ---
na ca sannyasanād eva --- ity atiricyate /
karmatyāgam āśaṅkya --- na5 karmaṇām anārambhāt ---
ity uktam /
children.translated_text: [there would be the consequence that] <s>mokṣa</s> comes from action alone, making the teaching of knowledge purposeless. Now, if it is said that attainment [of <s>mokṣa</s>] comes from action conjoined with knowledge — then, good sir, you have accepted our position! And when the first half [of the verse] is explained thus, 'Nor by renunciation alone' becomes superfluous. Having anticipated the objection of renunciation of action, [the Lord] said 'Not by abstaining from action.'

children.text:
sannyā(sa)śabdenāpi karmatyāga eva tvatpakṣe 'bhidhīyate /
na ca jñānarahitāt karmatyāgān mokṣaḥ6 kenacit pratijñāto7
yenedaṃ nirākaraṇārthaṃ syāt /
yadi cāvidvāṃsaḥ karmākurvāṇā8 mucyeran
yugapad eva kṛtsnaṃ2 jagan mucyeta /
na ca jñānakarmaṇor virodhāt
karmatyāgo (varam) virodhasyāsiddhatvāt /
kin na paśyati bhagavantam10 --- varta eva ca karmaṇi --- iti vadantam /
sākṣād brahmaiva svayam evārjunasya sārathyaṃ gatavat11 /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By the word '<s>sannyāsa</s>' (renunciation) too, according to your position, only the abandonment of action is denoted. And no one has maintained that liberation comes from the abandonment of action without knowledge, such that this [argument] would serve as a refutation. If the ignorant were to be liberated by not performing action, the entire world would be liberated all at once. Nor [is the abandonment of action proper] because of a supposed contradiction between knowledge and action—since that contradiction is unestablished. Does he not see the Blessed Lord saying 'continue in action'? <s>Brahman</s> itself directly has become the charioteer of <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text:
kiṃ cāyaṃ vidvān brahmībhūto 'bhedam ekāntena na paśyati /
tasyām avasthāyāṃ na karma kartavyam iti brūmaḥ /
yadi tu vyutthitacitto 'śanayānādiṣu kartṛtvam anubhavati tasyaiva
sandhyopāsanādi12 kartavyaṃ syāt /
viśeṣahetur vā vaktavyaḥ /
yac coktam ātmopadeśīyo 'yaṃ granthaḥ /
tatrāśaṅkye kilottaṅkena gṛhītam amṛtam13 /
yathā karmanāśabhayāj jantor ātmajñānāgrahas
tatheti tathyaparyālocanam uktam /
uttaraṅkasya yuktasūtradvāravinirgatatvād amṛtadhārāyāḥ14
sūtrabhrāntyātmajñānāgrahaṇam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, does this wise one, having become one with <s>Brahman</s>, not see [any] difference at all? We say that in that state, action need not be performed. But if his mind has emerged [from absorption] and he experiences agency in eating, walking, and the like, then he too should perform <s>sandhyā</s> worship (<s>sandhyopāsana</s>) and such. Or else a specific reason must be stated. And as for what was said—'this text is for the purpose of teaching the <s>ātman</s>'—there, the case is like obtaining <s>amṛta</s> (immortality) grasped by means of a pair of tongs, where just as there is non-acceptance of self-knowledge due to fear of the destruction of action, so [by contrast] the proper consideration is stated. Since the stream of <s>amṛta</s> has emerged through the outlet of the pair of tongs, the non-acceptance of self-knowledge is due to the confusion of [mistaking] the tongs [for something else].

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And we shall explain how action is not a cause of bondage. (4)

[Commentary:] But here, for those who desire liberation through knowledge of the <s>ātman</s>, how can there be non-acceptance of self-knowledge? And if action were the cause of liberation, then they would make effort in its preservation. Here, if liberation is attained through the combination [of knowledge and action], then there is engagement in both.

children.text:
karmākurvataḥ kevalād eva jñānāt siddhir ity
ayam artho na6 kenacid
anunmattena śakyate pratijñātum iti7 /
tatra hetum āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That accomplishment comes from knowledge alone without performing action—this meaning cannot be maintained by anyone who is not deranged. Regarding this, he states the reason:

children.text: na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api8 jātu tiṣṭhaty akarmakṛt /
children.translated_text: No one, indeed, even for a moment, ever remains without performing action.

children.text: kāryate hy avaśaḥ9 karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijair guṇaiḥ10 // BhG_3.5 //
children.translated_text: For everyone is made to act, helplessly, by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) born of <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). (BhG 3.5)

children.text:
hīti hetau / neti pratiṣedhe11 / yasmāt kaścid api puruṣaḥ
kṣaṇamātraṃ jātu12 na kadācit tiṣṭhaty akarmakṛt13 /
tasmāt karmayoga(pratiṣedha)pratijñānupapannā /
kathaṃ punar akarmakṛn nāstīty āha /
kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma /
avaśo 'svatantraḥ pumāṃ karma kāryate balāt karmaṇi pravartyate14 /
kena / prakṛtijair guṇaiḥ / prakṛtir mahābhūtānāṃ
sūkṣmāvasthā14 /
tato jātaiḥ kāryakāraṇaiḥ sattvādiguṇādhiṣṭhitai(r guṇaiḥ) /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Hi</s>' indicates reason. '<s>Na</s>' indicates negation. Since no person whatsoever, even for a single moment, ever remains without performing action, therefore the claim that prohibits <s>karmayoga</s> (the yoga of action) is untenable. How then is there no one who is without action? He says: 'For everyone is helplessly made to act.' The helpless, unfree person is forcibly driven to action. By what? By the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>prakṛti</s>. <s>Prakṛti</s> is the subtle state of the great elements. From that arise the effects and causes, governed by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and others.

sarvaṃ6 karma bandhātmakam iti tad asad ity āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And as for what the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> think—that all action is of the nature of bondage—that is wrong. He says:

children.text: yajñārthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra loko 'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Except for action performed for the sake of <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), this world is bound by action.

children.text: tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara // BhG_3.9 //
children.translated_text: For that purpose, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, perform action free from attachment. (BhG 3.9)

tayor abhedena vyapadiśyate7 /

tato 'nyatra taṃ varjayitvā10 loko 'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ /
phalārthaṃ yat kriyate tena badhyate jantuḥ /
tadarthaṃ11 yajñārthaṃ kevaladharmasiddhyarthaṃ
karma muktasaṅgaḥ12 phalāsaktirahitaḥ samācara /
children.translated_text: perform action free from attachment, devoid of attachment to fruits.

children.text: itīdam evaṃ dhārayen mokṣāyeti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus should one hold this in mind for the sake of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: śāstram evātra pramāṇam13 /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Scripture alone is the authority here.

children.text: yathāyaṃ dharmo 'yam adharma iti // 9 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] As [it determines] this is <s>dharma</s>, this is <s>adharma</s>. (9)

[Commentary:] By the word '<s>yajña</s>' (sacrifice), <s>dharma</s> that endures through time is denoted—what the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> call '<s>apūrva</s>' (the unseen potency). Its presiding deity is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. From the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Yajña</s> is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' They are spoken of as non-different. This is what is stated: Because action is for the purpose of worshipping <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the human effort prescribed by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> is called by the term 'action.' Apart from that, excluding that, this world is bound by action. The living being is bound by that [action] which is performed for the sake of fruit. For that purpose—for the sake of <s>yajña</s>, for the sole purpose of accomplishing <s>dharma</s>—

children.text:
prajāpativacanāc ca śreyaskaraṃ karma /
ato 'nuṣṭheyam iti14 darśayann āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And because of the words of <s>Prajāpati</s>, action is conducive to the highest good. Showing that it must therefore be performed, he says:

children.text: sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca1 prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having created beings together with sacrifice, <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of Creatures) said in the beginning:

children.text: anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo 'stv iṣṭakāmadhuk2 // BhG_3.10 //
children.translated_text: By this may you prosper; may this be your wish-fulfilling cow. (BhG 3.10)

children.text:
saha yajñena vartanta iti sahayajñā brāhmaṇādyāḥ prajāḥ3
sargādau sṛṣṭvā tāḥ purovāca4 --- anena prasaviṣyadhvam /
prasavo vṛddhiḥ / tāṃ prāpnuta /
eṣa vo yuṣmākam iṣṭakāmadhug astu5 /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'May this be for you the wish-fulfilling cow' (<s>iṣṭakāmadhuk</s>).

children.text: kāmān dogdhīti kāmadhuk // 10 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which milks desires is the wish-fulfilling cow. (10)

[Commentary:] Those who exist together with sacrifice—'<s>sahayajñāḥ</s>'—are the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and other beings. Having created them at the beginning of creation, he said to them: 'By this may you prosper.' Prosperity means growth. Attain that.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ kāmadhug ity āha6 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But how is it a wish-fulfilling cow? He says:

children.text: devān bhāvayatānena te devā7 bhāvayantu vaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, nourish the gods, and may those gods nourish you.

children.text: parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ8 śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha // BhG_3.11 //
children.translated_text: Nourishing each other, you shall attain the supreme good. (BhG 3.11)

children.text: anena devān bhāvayata vibhūtyā yojayata9 / te cendrādayo
devā10 bhāvayantu yuṣmān vibhūtyā yojayantu11 vṛṣṭipradānādinā /
children.translated_text: nourish you, endow you with prosperity through the bestowal of rain and the like.

children.text: evam anyonyaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paraṃ svargārthinaḥ svargam
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus nourishing each other, you shall attain the supreme good—those who desire heaven, heaven;

children.text: apavargārthinopavargaṃ prāpsya(tha)12 // 11 //
children.translated_text: those who desire liberation, liberation. (11)
[Commentary:] By this, nourish the gods—endow them with prosperity. And may those gods—<s>Indra</s> and the others—

children.text: pratyupakāram akurvato 'niṣṭārthaprāptim āha13 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the adverse consequence for one who does not reciprocate:

children.text: iṣṭān kāmān hi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The gods, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the desired enjoyments.

children.text: tair dattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte14 stena eva saḥ // BhG_3.12 //
children.translated_text: One who enjoys what is given by them without offering [in return] to them is indeed a thief. (BhG 3.12)

children.text: iṣṭān kāmān iti / pūrvārdhena pūrvaślokānuvādaḥ15 /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'The desired enjoyments'—by the first half, the previous verse is restated.

children.text: tair devair dattāt bhogān yo bhuṅkte16 tebhyo 'dattvā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One who enjoys the pleasures given by those gods, without giving back to them,

children.text: tān uddiśya yāgam akṛtvā stena eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: without performing a sacrifice dedicated to them, is indeed a thief.

children.text: kartavyam akurvan17 pratyavaitīty arthaḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One who does not perform what is required incurs adverse consequences—this is the meaning. (12)

children.translated_text: And sacrifice arises from action. The activity of the sacrificer and the officiating priests is <s>karma</s> (action).

children.translated_text: The <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) manifested by that, denoted by the word <s>dharma</s>, is the cause of the variety of the world. (14)
[Commentary:] From food that is consumed, through blood, beings are born. And its production [comes] from rain. And that [rain] comes from sacrifice.

children.text: tac ca ---
children.translated_text: And that —

children.text: karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam10 /
children.translated_text: Know that action arises from <s>Brahman</s>, and <s>Brahman</s> arises from the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>).

children.text: tasmāt sarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam // BhG_3.15 //

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Action arises from <s>Brahman</s> — <s>Brahman</s> here means the <s>Veda</s>; it is made known by that [Veda]. And <s>Brahman</s> arises from the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) — <s>akṣara</s> is the designation of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) — 'This is the exhalation of that great being — the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>...' — thus the <s>śruti</s> states. Since this is so, therefore the all-pervading <s>Brahman</s> called <s>akṣara</s> — [qualified as] 'all-pervading' by the adjective —

The other <s>Brahman</s>, called the <s>Veda</s>, being a modification, is not all-pervading. That <s>Brahman</s> called <s>akṣara</s> is eternally, at all times, established in sacrifice.

uktena prakāreṇa karmamūlaṃ jagaccakram /
atas tad akurvato jīvanaṃ vyartham ity āha ---
children.translated_text: The world-cycle has action as its root, in the manner described. Therefore, the life of one who does not perform [action] is futile — thus he says:

children.text: evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who does not follow in this world the cycle thus set in motion,

children.text: aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati // BhG_3.16 //
children.translated_text: lives a sinful life, delighting in the senses, in vain, O <s>Pārtha</s>. (BhG 3.16)

children.text: evam ity uktaparāmarśaḥ / pravartitaṃ mayājātinā4 cakram iva
children.translated_text: 'Thus' refers back to what has been said. 'Set in motion by <s>Prajāpati</s>' — like a wheel,

jagaccakram5 / karmabhyo bhūtāni bhūtebhyaḥ karmeti /
tatra yaḥ karma na karoti tena jagaccakraṃ nānuvartitaṃ bhavati /
nimittākaraṇān naimittikam eva6 nāśitaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ /
so 'yam aghāyuḥ pāpāyur indriyair ārāma ākrīḍā viṣayeṣu7
yasyāsau indriyārāmāḥ8 / moghaṃ vṛthaiva
he pārtha9 sa jīvati // 16 //
children.translated_text: the world-cycle: from actions come beings, from beings come actions. Whoever does not perform action therein, by him the world-cycle is not followed. The meaning is: by not performing the cause, the effect itself is destroyed. Such a person lives a sinful life — a life of sin — one whose sport, whose playground, is the senses amid their objects — he is one who delights in the senses. He lives in vain, O <s>Pārtha</s>. (16)

children.text:
kiṃ kācid avasthāsti yasyāṃ karmatyāga iṣṭa iti10 /

children.translated_text: Is there any state in which the abandonment of action is desired? Yes, there is — in terms of worldly convention. Therefore, for one who has become <s>Brahman</s>, but in the state prior to that, he says:

children.text: yas tv ātmaratir eva syād ātmatṛptaś ca12 mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who delights in the self alone, who is satisfied with the self,

children.text: ātmany eva ca santuṣṭas tasya kāryaṃ na vidyate // BhG_3.17 //
children.translated_text: and who is content in the self alone — for him, there is nothing to be done. (BhG 3.17)

children.text:
yas tv ātmaratir eva syāt / tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ /
asyām evāvasthāyām adhikārahetvabhāvāt karmatyāgo bhavati13 /
ātmany eva
children.translated_text: But one who delights in the self alone — the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for emphasis. Only in this [particular] state, because of the absence of the ground for qualification, does the abandonment of action occur. In the self alone —

one whose delight is [in the self] — not in sense-objects — he is <s>ātmarati</s> (delighting in the self). The word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>) is for emphasis — there is not even the slightest delight in sense-objects. And satisfied by the self alone — not by the taste of food and the like. And content in the self alone — not by obtaining anything else. Thus, one qualified by this threefold

children.text: naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaśca(na) /
children.translated_text: For him, there is no purpose served by action performed, nor any by action not performed here;

children.text: na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścid arthavyapāśrayaḥ7 // BhG_3.18 //
children.translated_text: nor is there among all beings anyone on whom his purpose depends. (BhG 3.18)

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Through action performed — such as sacrifice and the like — he has no objective. Nor is there any purpose characterized by the avoidance of adverse consequences through action not performed. Nor does he have any dependence upon, any need from, any being — from <s>Brahmā</s> downward — [as the <s>śruti</s> states:] 'He himself becomes that.' But one who conforms to the properties of body and senses and performs activities such as sleeping and the like — how can he be said to delight in the self alone or to be satisfied by the self alone? This state is the [state of] abandonment of action as laid down by the Blessed Lord — considering this for oneself, one should abandon or continue performing action. The false instruction of someone else of the present time should not be heeded or taken as authoritative, due to [that person's] confusion and laziness.

children.translated_text: Even considering the welfare of the world alone, you ought to act. (BhG 3.20)

lokasaṅgraho lokaparipālanam uktena14 nyāyena /

kevalasya jñānasyāpavargaṃ prati
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By action alone (<s>karmaṇā eva</s>), <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Aśvapati</s>, and others attained perfection — liberation. The word 'hi' indicates reason. The particle 'eva' is for emphasis. The exclusion of the absence of action is made — not the exclusion of knowledge. Even if you consider yourself to have accomplished all that needs to be accomplished, still, considering the welfare of the world, you ought to act. The welfare of the world means the proper sustaining of people in the manner described. But in ultimate reality, action is to be performed for one's own [spiritual] purpose, since for knowledge alone — which is [merely] the means to liberation —

children.text: tasmāt karmaṇā vinā saṃsiddher asambhavāt karma kurv iti
children.translated_text: Therefore, since perfection is impossible without action, 'perform action' — this is the

children.text: gītārthaḥ16 // 20 //
children.translated_text: meaning of the <s>Gītā</s>. (20)

This is an imagination of a false meaning. For <s>Janaka</s> and others are traditionally remembered as knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. In the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> and <s>Viṣṇudharma</s> texts, seventy-six among the <s>Janakas</s> are remembered as having attained <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). And here it is said that they attained liberation through action — not that they sustained the world through action. [The rival interpretation] would involve the rejection of what is heard and the fabrication of what is not heard. Nor is the fact that they were engaged in action a reason [for saying they acted merely for the world's welfare]; for after action has begun, everyone is indeed engaged in action. If, upon the arising of right vision, the renunciation of action [were called for], then even <s>Janaka</s> and others would necessarily have had to perform action [for the same reason].

children.text: parārthaṃ veti bhāgavataṃ mataṃ mudritam11 // 24 //
children.translated_text: or for the sake of others — this is the sealed doctrine of the Blessed Lord. // 24 //

[Commentary:] The worlds would perish, be destroyed, if I did not perform action. And I would be the author of confusion — due to the absence of purpose and such. And thereby I would destroy these beings. Therefore, even by me — who am the Lord — action is performed for the sake of holding the people together. Thus, in both ways — following scripture — action must be performed, whether for one's own sake or for the sake of others. Action should not be abandoned through the pride of considering oneself a knower. Because the human being is the one qualified for the scripture, and because even the Blessed Lord, dwelling in a human body, has the qualification for <s>dharma</s>, the abandonment of action is untenable. For one who has engaged in action in the human body,

children.text: tatra ca12 karmaṇi pravṛttasya viduṣo 'viduṣaś cāyaṃ13 viśeṣaḥ ---

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By the <s>guṇas</s> — the unconscious properties in the form of cause and effect of <s>prakṛti</s> characterized by light, water, and food — actions are performed. For all actions, whether worldly or Vedic, take place in the body, senses, and mind — not in the <s>ātman</s>. The <s>ātman</s>'s agency is merely due to proximity, like a magnet's [effect] on iron — it is merely adventitious, not natural. Just as fire's capacity to produce smoke is due to its conjunction with fuel, so is the <s>ātman</s>'s agency due to conjunction with body and senses. [Commentary:] The knower of truth is one who knows the truth of the division of the <s>guṇas</s> and the division of actions. What is the division? The <s>guṇas</s> are the body and senses, the actions are [those of] the self — thus. And the division of actions: those performed with a view to fruits are for the sake of fruits; those performed for <s>Īśvara</s>'s sake serve the purpose of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).

children.text: prakṛter guṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante11 guṇakarmasu /
children.translated_text: Those deluded by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>prakṛti</s> become attached to the actions of the <s>guṇas</s>.

'Of incomplete knowledge and dull-witted' — those of incomplete knowledge are the ritualists who know only action. One of complete knowledge — the one who practices the combination of knowledge and action — should not unsettle them, should not cause a disturbance of their intellect. children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having performed all actions and renounced them — deposited them — in Me, the Supreme Lord, <s>Brahman</s>: this entire complex of action is the domain of <s>Brahman</s>, because of its consciousness. And since cause and effect are non-different, having understood their identity with It, they serve as means for attaining It — with a mind directed to the inner Self, free from the desire for fruits. One from whom possessiveness has departed is <s>nirmama</s>. 'My action does not belong to me; it is performed by <s>Brahman</s> alone, in me' — with this resolve, fight — freed from grief. // 30 //

And one should not desist from one's own <s>dharma</s> such as battle because of aversion to the taking of life — thus he says, recalling what <s>Arjuna</s> had said, 'better to perform...':

children.translated_text: 'Better is one's own <s>dharma</s>, though imperfectly performed, than the <s>dharma</s> of another well performed; death in one's own <s>dharma</s> is better than prosperity from another's <s>dharma</s>.' // BhG 3.35 //

anabhyudaya13 iti / svadharmaḥ kartavyaḥ14 / arthavādo 'yam // 35 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] the prosperity resulting from another's <s>dharma</s> is not better. But in reality it is not so — rather, from one's own <s>dharma</s> there is prosperity, and from resorting to another's <s>dharma</s> there is non-prosperity. [Therefore,] one's own <s>dharma</s> should be performed. This is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage). // 35 //

[Commentary:] 'Better' — one's own <s>dharma</s>, though deficient in qualities, meaning even if deficient in the fulfillment of obligations, even if performed somehow or other, is better, more praiseworthy. Why? Than another's <s>dharma</s> well performed — complete in all its obligatory aspects. Why is this so? Because death while abiding in one's own <s>dharma</s>, in battle and such, is better than the prosperity, i.e., the living, that comes from performing another's <s>dharma</s> — this is the meaning.

kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena vā // BhG_3.44 //)
children.translated_text: 'Knowledge is covered by this, the eternal enemy of the knower, in the form of desire, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, [which is like] an insatiable fire.' // BhG 3.44 //

children.text:
āvṛtam iti / etena8 jñānam āvṛta(m) / kasya (kena) /
jñānino9 nityavairiṇā kāmarūpeṇa nānārūpeṇa /
jñānino hy asau nityavairī / katham / kāmṃ dūrataḥ10 kṛtvāpavargam
adhigantum icchati11 jñānī / kāmaś ca12 tadīyaṃ jñānaṃ tiraskṛtya
saṃsāre kṣeptuṃ13 yatate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Covered' — by this, knowledge is covered. Of whom? By whom? Of the knower, by the eternal enemy in the form of desire, i.e., of many forms. For this [desire] is the eternal enemy of the knower. How? Because the knower, casting desire far away, wishes to attain liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); and desire, concealing his knowledge, strives to throw him into <s>saṃsāra</s>.

/

children.text: na vidyate alaṃ paryāptir asyety analaḥ // 44 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Anala</s>' means that for which there is no limit, no sufficiency. // 44 //

[Commentary:] But the ignorant person, having made effort, follows desire itself — there is no conflict for him with that [desire]. Therefore 'of the knower' is an appropriate qualifier, as is 'eternal enemy.' 'Insatiable' (<s>duṣpūra</s>) means

children.text: kim adhiṣṭhāno 'sau jñānam āvṛṇotīty āha3 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having what as its basis does it cover knowledge? He says:

children.text:
(indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam ucyate /
etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam // BhG_3.45 //)
children.translated_text: 'The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these, it deludes the embodied one by covering knowledge.' // BhG 3.45 //

children.text:
indriyāṇīti4 / indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam āśrayaḥ5 /
tair indriyādibhir jñānam āvṛtya dehinaṃ mohayati mohayitvā kāryeṣu
vartayati // 45 //6
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The senses, the mind, and the intellect are its seat, its refuge. Having covered knowledge through the senses and the rest, it deludes the embodied one, and having deluded [him], it engages him in [worldly] activities. // 45 //

children.text: yata evam ---
children.translated_text: Since this is so —

children.text:
(tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau niyamya bharatarṣabha /
pāpmānaṃ prajahīhy enaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam // BhG_3.46 //)
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, restraining the senses first, O best of <s>Bharatas</s>, slay this sinful one, the destroyer of knowledge and realization.' // BhG 3.46 //

children.text: tasmād iti / indriyaṃ7 mano buddhiṃ8 (ca) niyamyādau prathamam eva
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Therefore' — having restrained the senses, the mind, and the intellect, first of all, at the very outset,

children.text:
pāpmānam enaṃ9 śatruṃ jahi vināśaya / jñānavijñānanāśanam /
jñānam ātmayāthātmyaparijñānam10 /
vijñānam (viśiṣṭaṃ tajjñānam) /
tadubhayanāśanam11 / tad api pṛthakkartavyatayā vidhīyate śrutau ---
vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta --- iti /
children.translated_text: 'Having realized, one should cultivate wisdom' — thus.

children.text: anyathā jñānavijñānaśabdayor
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the words <s>jñāna</s> and <s>vijñāna</s>

children.text: arthe bhedo na syāt12 // 46 //
children.translated_text: would have no difference in meaning. // 46 //

slay, destroy this sinful enemy. 'The destroyer of knowledge and realization' — <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) is the full understanding of the true nature of the self; <s>vijñāna</s> (realization) is the distinguished, [direct experiential] knowledge thereof. That which destroys both. This too is separately enjoined in <s>śruti</s>:

children.text:
kasya sannidhau kāmas tiṣṭhatīti sākṣād darśayitum āha sthūlaṃ
śarīram apekṣya ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] To show directly in whose proximity desire abides, he says, with reference to the gross body:

(indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ /
manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ // BhG_3.47 //)
children.translated_text: 'The senses are said to be superior [to the body]; the mind is superior to the senses; the intellect is superior to the mind; and that which is beyond the intellect is He.' // BhG 3.47 //

children.text:
indriyāṇīti / indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur
viṣayagrāhakatvenotkṛṣṭatvāc
ca parastvam / indriyebhyaḥ1 paraṃ manaḥ saukṣmyāt prādhānyāc ca2 /
children.translated_text: and because of their pre-eminence — this is their superiority. The mind is superior to the senses, because of its subtlety and pre-eminence.

children.text:
manasas tu parā buddhiḥ3 / sa eva hetuḥ / atha buddhimanasoḥ4 ko bhedaḥ
/
saṅkalpavikalpavṛttihetur manaḥ / buddhir adhyavasāyātmikā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The intellect is superior to the mind — the same reason [applies]. Now, what is the difference between the mind and intellect? The mind is the cause of the function of thought and deliberation; the intellect has the nature of determination.

children.text: yathā sthāṇur vā puruṣo5 veti saṃśaye sthāṇur
children.translated_text: Just as in the doubt 'is this a post or a person?' — [the resolution]

children.text: evāyam ity adhyavasāyaḥ6 /
children.translated_text: 'this is indeed a post' is determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>).

children.text: yo buddheḥ parataḥ sa kāmaḥ parāmṛśyate7 tasya prakṛtatvāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'That which is beyond the intellect' — desire is referred to, because it is the topic at hand.

children.text: na punar ātmā sa iti nirdiśyate pūrvatrāsaṅkīrtanāt // 47 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But the <s>ātman</s> is not indicated here, because it was not mentioned earlier. // 47 //
[Commentary:] 'The senses' — the senses are said to be superior, because of their excellence in grasping objects,

children.text: idānīm upasaṃharati ---
children.translated_text: Now he concludes:

children.text:
(evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānam ātmanā /
jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam // BhG_3.48 //)
children.translated_text: 'Thus, knowing what is beyond the intellect, steadying the self by the self, slay the enemy, O mighty-armed one, in the form of desire, which is hard to overcome.' // BhG 3.48 //

children.text: evam iti / evam uktena prakāreṇa buddheḥ paraṃ kāmaṃ buddhvā8
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Thus' — in the manner described, having understood desire as beyond the intellect,

children.text:
jahi śatruṃ mahābāho / kāmarūpaṃ duḥkhenāsadanīyam9 / kiṃ kṛtvā
/
saṃstabhyātmānam ātmani10 saṃstabhya niruddhya cātmānaṃ kṣetrajñam
children.translated_text: 'Having steadied the self in the self' — having restrained and established the self, the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field),

children.text: ātmani11 paramātmani saṃyojyaikīkṛtya12 brahmarūpeṇāvasthāpya
children.translated_text: in the self — in the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) — having united, merged, and established [it] in the form of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: kāmaṃ13 jahīti tātparyārthaḥ14 // 48 //
children.translated_text: slay desire — this is the purport. // 48 //
slay the enemy, O mighty-armed one. 'In the form of desire, hard to overcome' — difficult to confront. How? —

children.text: iti śrībhagavadbhāskarakṛte15 gītābhāṣye tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter in the Blessed <s>Bhāskara</s>'s <s>Gītā Bhāṣya</s>.

śrībhagavān uvāca1 ---
children.translated_text: Now, the fourth chapter. The Blessed Lord said:

children.text:
(imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavān aham avyayam /
vivasvān manave prāha manur ikṣvākave 'bravīt // BhG_4.1 //)
children.translated_text: 'I taught this imperishable <s>yoga</s> to <s>Vivasvān</s>; <s>Vivasvān</s> told it to <s>Manu</s>; <s>Manu</s> spoke it to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.' // BhG 4.1 //

children.text: imam iti / vivasvān ādityaḥ tasmai2 proktavān aham avyayam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This' — <s>Vivasvān</s>, the sun god — to him I taught this imperishable [<s>yoga</s>].

children.text:
nityatvaṃ3 nityavedavihitatvāt / sa ca vivasvān svaputrāya manave4
daṇḍadharāya (prāha) manur ādirājāyekṣvākave 'bravīt5 // 1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Imperishable' — eternal, because it is eternally enjoined by the <s>Veda</s>. And that <s>Vivasvān</s> told it to his son <s>Manu</s>, the bearer of the rod [of justice]; <s>Manu</s> spoke it to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, the first king. // 1 //

children.text:
(evaṃ paramparākhyātam imaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ /
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa // BhG_4.2 //)
children.translated_text: 'Thus handed down in succession, the royal sages knew this; but with the long passage of time, this <s>yoga</s> has been lost here, O scorcher of foes.' // BhG 4.2 //

children.text: evam iti / evaṃ paramparākhyātam ācāryaparamparayā6 kathitam imaṃ
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Thus' — thus told through the succession of teachers, this

children.text: rājarṣayo viduḥ / rājānaś ca te darśanaśaktiyuktāś ceti7 rājarṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: the royal sages knew. 'Royal sages' — they are kings, and they are endowed with the power of vision, hence royal sages.

children.text:
sa yogaḥ kālena mahateha loke8 kathañcid viṣayāsaktacetasaṃ rājānām
āsādya9 naṣṭaḥ / parān śatrūṃs tāpayatīti he parantapa10 // 2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That <s>yoga</s>, in the course of a long time, having come to kings whose minds were attached to sense objects, was somehow lost in this world. 'O scorcher of foes' — he who torments the enemies. // 2 //

children.text:
(sa evāyaṃ mayā te 'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ /
bhakto 'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hy etad uttaram // BhG_4.3 //)
children.translated_text: 'That very same ancient <s>yoga</s> has been taught by Me to you today, because you are My devotee and friend — for this is a supreme secret.' // BhG 4.3 //

children.text:
sa eveti / sa eva sanātano yogo mayā proktaḥ / kasmāt /
bhakto 'si me sakhā ceti11 / rahasyaṃ hy etan mayoktam aprakāśitam /
yan mayi bhaktatvasakhitvābhyāṃ12 naitad avajñātum arhasi / idānīṃ
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'That very' — that very eternal <s>yoga</s> has been taught by Me. Why? Because you are My devotee and friend. For this has been spoken by Me as an unpublicized [teaching]. Because of your devotion and friendship to Me, you should not disregard this. Now

children.text: yuddha(āya) protsāhanārthaṃ prāptāvasaraṃ1 proktam ity
abhiprāyaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: this is the intent. (3)
was spoken at an opportune moment for the purpose of encouraging [<s>Arjuna</s>] to battle —

children.text: pūrvaparavirodhaṃ paśyann arjuna uvāca ---
children.translated_text: Seeing a contradiction between the earlier and later [statements], <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text:
(aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ /
katham etad vijānīyāṃ tvam ādau proktavān iti // BhG_4.4 //)
children.translated_text: 'Your birth is recent, the birth of <s>Vivasvat</s> is ancient. How am I to understand this — that You taught [this yoga] in the beginning?' (BhG 4.4)

children.text:
aparam iti / bhavato janmāparam idānīntanam2 / param ādityasya
sargādau / katham etad vijānīyāṃ jñātuṃ śaknuyām /
tvam ādau proktavān iti3 / yathāvirodhas tathā māṃ pratipādayeḥ // 4
//
children.translated_text: 'Recent' — Your birth is recent, i.e. of the present time. The birth of the Sun [<s>Āditya</s>] was at the beginning of creation. 'How am I to understand this?' — How can I know [this]? 'That You taught [it] in the beginning' — explain this to me in a way that resolves the contradiction. (4)

children.text: amarajīvavyatirikteśvarapratipādanadvāreṇottaraṃ4 dīyate ---
children.translated_text: The answer is given through establishing the Lord as distinct from [ordinary] immortals and living beings:

children.text:
(bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna /
tāny ahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa // BhG_4.5 //)
children.translated_text: 'Many births of Mine have passed, and of yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>. I know them all, but you do not know them, O scorcher of foes.' (BhG 4.5)

children.text:
bahūni5 / bahūni me vyatītāni6 prādurbhāvarūpāṇi / mayi
sarvāṇi --- iti vacanam idānīṃ siddhaṃ7 bhavati /
anyathā vyatirikteśvarābhāve8 kva karmāṇi sannyaseran / tāny ahaṃ
veda /
tvaṃ tāni na vettha jānāsy anīśvaratvāt9 // 5 //
children.translated_text: 'You do not know them,' because you are not the Lord. (5)

'Many' — many births of Mine have passed, in the form of divine manifestations. [The statement] 'all [things abide] in Me' is now established. Otherwise, in the absence of a distinct Lord, where would actions be renounced [i.e., offered]? 'I know them all.'

children.text:
kathaṃ punar īśvaro 'jaḥ10 san sambhavatīti11 codyam āśaṅkya12
nirākaroti ---
children.translated_text: Anticipating the objection 'How does the Lord, who is unborn, take birth?' — he refutes it:

children.text:
(ajo 'pi sann avyayātmā bhūtānām īśvaro 'pi san /
prakṛtiṃ svām adhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmy ātmamāyayā // BhG_4.6 //)
children.translated_text: 'Though I am unborn, though My self is imperishable, though I am the Lord of beings, establishing Myself in My own <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), I come into being through My own <s>māyā</s> (creative power).' (BhG 4.6)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: NOTES:

children.text:
1. yuddhaprotsāhanārthaṃ prāsāvasaraṃ
2. ^midānnītataṃ
3. jñātu na śaknuyāttvamodau proktavaniti
4. bharajīvyatirikraścara pratipādanadvāroṇotta^
5. vahunīti
6. vadvani me vyatīttāni
7. mapitsāṇītivacanamidānnīṃ sīddhaṃ
8. ṣyatiriktleśvarābhavi
9. veda tātāmināsyanīśvaratvāt
10. punarīśvarājaḥ
11. sabhyavasīti
12. coghamāśakya
children.translated_text: [Critical apparatus: variant readings for the preceding passage]

children.text: aja iti / na jāyate avinaśvara ātmā svarūpaṃ yasyāsāv avyayātmā /
prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya / prakṛtis tejo'bannalakṣaṇā1
children.translated_text: 'Establishing Myself in My own <s>prakṛti</s>' — <s>Prakṛti</s> is characterized by light (<s>tejas</s>), water (<s>ap</s>), and food (<s>anna</s>),

children.text:
parameśvarād utpannā / (tām) avaṣṭabhya āśritya sambhavāmy
ātmamāyayā3 / māyāśabdaḥ prajñāvacanaḥ / svecchayety arthaḥ4 /
nāhaṃ dharmaprayojyaḥ saṃsārī5 / vaśyaprakṛtitvād dehopādānāny
asau6 svecchayā grahīṣyatīti (a)virodhaḥ7 // 6 //
children.translated_text: originated from the Supreme Lord. Having established Himself in that — having taken recourse to it — 'I come into being through My own <s>māyā</s>.' The word <s>māyā</s> means 'wisdom' (<s>prajñā</s>). The meaning is: by My own will. 'I am not one compelled by <s>dharma</s>, a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being).' Because His <s>prakṛti</s> is under His control, He will assume the materials for a body by His own will — thus there is no contradiction. (6)
'Unborn' — He is not born; He whose self is imperishable — whose essential nature is indestructible — He is '<s>avyayātmā</s>' (of imperishable self).

children.text: kadā punar ātmānaṃ sṛjasīty āha ---
children.translated_text: 'But when do You create Yourself?' — to this he says:

children.text:
(yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata /
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham // BhG_4.7 //)
children.translated_text: 'Whenever there is a decline of <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>, and a rise of <s>adharma</s>, then I create Myself.' (BhG 4.7)

children.text: (yadeti) / yadā hi dharmasya varṇāśramādilakṣaṇasya glānir hāniḥ8 /
children.translated_text: 'Whenever' — whenever there is a decline, a diminution, of <s>dharma</s> characterized by the <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste and life-stage) system,

children.text: abhyutthānaṃ vṛddhir adharmasya / tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham // 7 //
children.translated_text: and a rise, an increase, of <s>adharma</s> — then I create Myself. (7)

children.text: tat ---
children.translated_text: For that purpose:

children.text:
(paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām /
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge // BhG_4.8 //)
children.translated_text: 'For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, for the establishment of <s>dharma</s>, I come into being age after age.' (BhG 4.8)

children.text:

children.translated_text: How? According to the division of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>karmas</s> (actions) — by the division of qualities and by the division of actions. There, the qualities of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> are uprightness, gentleness, clarity of mind, and the like, due to the predominance of <s>sattva</s>. The <s>Kṣatriya's</s> qualities are valor, energy, fortitude, and the like, due to a trace of <s>sattva</s> [mixed with <s>rajas</s>]. The <s>Vaiśya's</s> qualities are industry and fickleness of mind, due to the predominance of <s>rajas</s>. The <s>Śūdra's</s> quality is servitude, due to the predominance of <s>tamas</s>. As for actions: teaching and the like for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; warfare and the like for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>; agriculture and the like for the <s>Vaiśya</s>; service for the <s>Śūdra</s>. Therefore, those who are qualified for their respective actions accordingly follow My path. 'Know Me as the imperishable creator of this.'

children.translated_text: Now, [one might say] something contradictory is being stated. [Reply:] There is no contradiction. Because He is the creator of the world's creation, sustenance, and destruction by mere will alone, know Him as the creator; because He does not now produce through the union of male and female, know Him as the non-doer. The mention of the four-caste system is for the purpose of indicating the [entire] world.

children.text: yad vā svātantryeṇa pṛthivyādinirmā(ṇa)sadbhāvāt17 kartṛtvam /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, [He is] the agent because of the real existence of the creation of earth and other [elements] through His independence.

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of dependence on the actions of living beings, [the Lord's] non-agency follows from [this very] dependence. (13)

children.translated_text: Actions do not taint Me, nor have I any desire for the fruit of action. One who thus knows Me is not bound by actions. (BhG 4.14)

spṛhā /

/

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Not Me'—actions do not taint Me. Why? Because I have no desire for the fruit of action. For there is nothing to be obtained or accomplished by Me through the action of creation and the like, since I am one whose desires are already fulfilled (<s>āptakāma</s>). One who thus knows Me is not bound by actions.

nanu cāptakāmatvād īśvaraṃ5 na limpanti karmāṇi / anyaṃ punar

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, because He is one whose desires are fulfilled, actions do not taint <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). But another person, whose desires are not fulfilled—why do meritorious actions taint him? To this it is replied: This is the intended meaning here—freedom from craving is the cause of non-tainting. Any other person too who, free from craving regarding his own activities, engages in action dedicated to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), he too is not bound by actions—this is the more fitting statement. (14)

children.translated_text: What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. I shall explain to you that action, knowing which you shall be freed from evil. (BhG 4.16)

[They say:] 'In action, in engagement—one who sees the absence of action. For in ultimate reality, there is no such thing as action.' [They argue:] just as the cognition of movement in trees standing on the bank for those traveling in a boat is an error, so too is all cognition of action. Just as the Buddhists who hold the doctrine of momentariness do not accept the activity of going apart from the distinct entities <s>Devadatta</s> and the like—even so, here we say: the claim that action does not exist cannot be maintained. 'The finger moves,' '<s>Devadatta</s> walks,' '<s>Brahmadatta</s> cooks,' 'the leaf moves'—because [these] are directly perceived by all living beings.
