children.translated_text: it should be performed with a mind established in non-duality, through the principle of offering to <s>Brahman</s>. // 20 //

[Commentary:] 'Having abandoned' — one whose mind has turned away from impermanent fruits, content with the eternal <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) — ever content. Without dependence — one for whom the support that is the means to fruits does not exist. He, even while performing, does not act — because of the absence of connection with fruits. 'Your right is to action alone' — although the qualification for <s>dharma</s> and disqualification for fruits was stated, here there is no repetition — because this section has a specific purpose.

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By the word '<s>ātman</s>' (self), the body together with the senses is meant. One who does not have the proprietary attitude — 'these sons and such are mine, I belong to them' — such a person has relinquished all possessions. What does 'bodily' (<s>śārīra</s>) mean? Does it mean what is accomplished by the body, or what is for the sustenance of the body? Not for sustenance, because for one whose body is already being maintained, the instruction would be pointless — and because it was said 'even bodily sustenance.' Therefore <s>śārīra</s> means action accomplished by body and senses, prescribed by scripture. Now, prohibited action too is accomplished by the body! This is no fault — because the context is about Vedic action. 'Only' (<s>kevalam</s>) means 'without fruits.' Now, one who performs scriptural action does not incur sin — so this would be the fallacy of prohibiting the non-existent! To this it is replied: here the fault lies in not understanding the purport of the sentence. 'While performing, he does not incur' — but not performing the prescribed, he does incur sin, i.e., demerit. Or alternatively, <s>kilbiṣa</s> means <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is another interpretation.

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Others interpret it as performing begging for alms, eating, drinking, and such for the sustenance of the body. That too means 'only' — free from identification. But this is a misinterpretation. For even one who says 'I am free from the identification that I am begging for alms' — his deliberate engagement in it is indeed conceivable. One who, tormented by hunger and thirst, experiences agency in eating and such as a remedy for them — how would he not accept agency in Vedic action? This is the behavior of a prince. If in Vedic action, agency has ceased because of opposition to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, then in worldly action too there is no difference. Or if agency is not obtained in both cases — that is the half-and-half fallacy. Therefore this interpretation is fitting for those of undeveloped and misled intellects. Not for us who follow the course of valid means of knowledge. // 21 //

[Commentary:] 'Of one who is free from attachment, who is liberated' — of one free from attachment, who is liberated from faults such as <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the like, whose mind is established in self-knowledge, who undertakes [action] for the sake of sacrifice — for the worship of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) — of one who commences action, the entirety [of action dissolves]. children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Brahman</s>' — the instrument by which [the oblation] is offered, the <s>juhū</s> ladle and the hand and such — that instrumental agent is <s>Brahman</s>. From the association with the word <s>havis</s> (oblation), '<s>arpaṇa</s>' is understood as the offering of the oblation. The <s>havis</s> — the substance being offered, such as <s>soma</s>, clarified butter, milk, and the rest. Since it is offered addressing a deity, the recipient-agent, i.e. the deity, is also implied. <s>Brahman</s> alone is the fire — the <s>brahmāgni</s>, the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and <s>Smārta</s> and <s>Upāsanīya</s> [fires] — in that locus, by <s>Brahman</s> itself as the agent, the offering is accomplished — the act of oblation is completed.

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By that very [<s>Brahman</s>] which performs [the sacrifice], <s>Brahman</s> alone is to be reached — attained. The action that has <s>Brahman</s> as its nature is <s>brahmakarma</s> (action that is <s>Brahman</s>); <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) in that action — one who has that is one of <s>brahmakarmasamādhi</s>; by that [means]. The mention of the five agents (<s>kāraka</s>) is for illustration. Whatever class of <s>kārakas</s> — Vedic or <s>Smārta</s> — exists in any [ritual], all of that is to be understood as <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Brahman</s> is indeed the entire world of manifestation — 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' — thus the <s>śruti</s> states. Therein, one who sees <s>Brahman</s> pervading all modifications in the form of the cause — he sees rightly. Just as the nature of clay pervades pots and the like. And here, it is not the meditation on the agents [as] <s>Brahman</s> that is enjoined — as in 'the mind is <s>Brahman</s>' — but rather the vision of truth. For there, from the use of the word <s>iti</s>, symbol-meditation [is indicated]. And precisely because of the vision of the universal self, the statement '<s>Brahman</s> alone is to be reached' is appropriate.

And thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text states]: 'By knowledge [one attains] the world of the gods — having become a god, he reaches the gods.' The <s>karma-yogins</s> worship [this]. Even in the state of [becoming] gods and the like, the arising of knowledge is accepted. 'Whoever among the gods awakened to it — he became that very thing; likewise among the <s>ṛṣis</s>, likewise among humans' — thus the <s>śruti</s>. <s>Brahman</s> itself is the fire; in that [fire], sacrifice — one's own self, the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is intended, not the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul). 'That which knows whatever is to be known' — thus the word 'sacrifice' (<s>yajña</s>) is here indicated as a designation for the self. By sacrifice — by the self, by the mind that is close to the self — they offer. The unification of <s>Brahman</s> and the self is intended. (25)

yadi tarhi yajñair eva mokṣaṃ prāpyate kim ātmajñānenety āśaṅkyām
āha5 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] If liberation is attained through sacrifices alone, what need is there for self-knowledge? — apprehending this doubt, he says:

children.text:
(śreyān dravyamayād yajñāj jñānayajñaḥ parantapa /
sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate // BhG_4.33 //)
children.translated_text: 'The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to the sacrifice of material things, O scorcher of foes; all action in its entirety, O <s>Pārtha</s>, culminates in knowledge.' // BhG 4.33 //

children.text:
śreyān iti / pūrvatra kevalād eva jñānān mokṣo nāsti / kiṃ tarhi /
karmasahitād ity uktam --- na karmaṇām anārambhād6 iti ārabhya / atra
punaḥ kevalād eva karmaṇo mokṣaḥ syād ity āśaṅkya nirasyate /
asti cedam api darśanam / yājñikānāṃ keṣāñcin mokṣo nāma svarga
eva
tāratamyāvasthitaḥ7 / sa ca karmasādhyo8 nānyo 'stīty
āśaṅkābījaṃ9
cedam / evaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyasa10 iti / śreyān praśasyataro11
dravyamayād
agniṣṭomāder jñānayajñaḥ / kutaḥ / sarvaṃ hi jñāne sati
parisamāpyate 'pavargāya samarthaṃ12 bhavatīty arthaḥ /
tathā ca śrutiḥ --- sa ya ātmānam eva lokam upāste hāsya karma
kṣīyate13 --- iti / jñānasahitaṃ karmākṣayaphalatvān na kṣīyata
ity ucyate /
svarūpato14 hi kṣaṇikaṃ karma /
tathā --- yo vā etad akṣaram aviditvā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Superior' — it was stated earlier that liberation is not from knowledge alone; rather, it is from [knowledge] combined with action — [as said from] 'not by non-commencement of actions' onwards. Here again, apprehending the doubt that liberation might come from action alone, it is refuted. And there is this view too: for some <s>yājñikas</s> (ritualists), <s>mokṣa</s> is nothing other than heaven arranged in degrees of hierarchy. And that is accomplished by <s>karma</s> alone, there being nothing else — this is the seed of the doubt. [The reply to] 'knowing thus, you shall be liberated' is: superior, more praiseworthy than the material sacrifice of <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and such, is the sacrifice of knowledge. Why? Because when knowledge is present, all [action] culminates, i.e., becomes capable of [producing] liberation — this is the meaning. And thus <s>śruti</s> states: 'He who contemplates the self alone as the [true] world — his <s>karma</s> does not diminish.' <s>Karma</s> combined with knowledge, because it bears imperishable fruit, is said not to diminish. For <s>karma</s> by its very nature is momentary. Likewise — 'He who, without knowing this Imperishable,

O <s>Gārgi</s>, offers oblations, gives gifts, and performs austerities in this world, even for many thousands of years —

children.translated_text: 'Learn that through prostration, through inquiry, and through service; the knowers, the seers of truth, will teach you knowledge.' // BhG 4.34 //

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore he specifies — 'seers of truth' (<s>tattvadarśinaḥ</s>).

children.text: sākṣātkṛtātmasattattvā10 ity arthaḥ // 34 //
children.translated_text: Meaning: those who have directly realized the truth of the self. // 34 //

[Commentary:] 'That' — prostration (<s>praṇipāta</s>) means bowing down with full extension, i.e., full-length obeisance and such — through that, know it. Inquiry (<s>paripraśna</s>) means [asking]: 'What is the truth of the self? What is knowledge? And what is ignorance?' Service (<s>sevā</s>) means devoted attendance.

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ taj jñānam iti11 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What kind of knowledge is that?

children.text:
(yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava /
yena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi // BhG_4.35 //)
children.translated_text: 'Having known which, you will not again go to delusion thus, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>; by which you will see all beings without exception in the self, and then in Me.' // BhG 4.35 //

children.text: yad iti / yaj jñātvādhigamya12 pūrvavan mohaṃ na yāsyasi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Which' — having known, having understood which, you will not go to delusion as before.

parameśvare13 / yathā samudre sarvā āpaḥ praviśyaikībhavanti
tathātmani

/
kāryakāraṇayor
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By which knowledge you will see all beings in their entirety in the self, and then in Me, the Supreme Lord. Just as all waters enter and become one with the ocean, so too all this manifold [creation] enters and becomes one with the self, which is the cause of all — this is the meaning. Because of the non-difference of cause and effect,

/

so too the fire of knowledge reduces all <s>karmas</s> to ashes — those that have begun to bear fruit, those performed in previous births and standing as causes for future bodies, and those performed in this birth before the arising of knowledge — it reduces all these to ashes.

(na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitram iha vidyate /
tat svayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhiḥ kālenātmani vindati // BhG_4.38 //)
children.translated_text: 'For there exists nothing in this world as purifying as knowledge; one who has attained perfection through <s>yoga</s> in time finds it within the self.' // BhG 4.38 //

children.text:
nahīti / na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitraṃ pāvanam iha śāstrīye
'rthe2 vidyate / nirdhāraṇe saptamī / tac ca jñānaṃ svayam ity
ātmavācī3 / karmayogena saṃsiddhaḥ kālena4 paripākahetunātmani
svabuddhāv eva labhate // 38 //
children.translated_text: in one's own intellect. // 38 //

[Commentary:] 'For' — there exists nothing equal to knowledge as a purifier, a means of purification, in this matter of scriptural import. The locative is in the sense of determination. And that knowledge — 'itself' — this word refers to the self; one who has attained perfection through the <s>yoga</s> of action, in time, through the maturation [of spiritual practice], finds it in the self,

children.text: praṇipātādi bāhyanimittam uktam5 / idānīm ābhyantaraṃ6 nimittam āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The external cause — prostration and such — has been stated. Now he states the internal cause:

children.text:
(śraddhāvāṃl labhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ /
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntim acireṇādhigacchati // BhG_4.39 //)
children.translated_text: 'The one endowed with faith obtains knowledge, being devoted to it and with senses controlled; having obtained knowledge, one quickly attains supreme peace.' // BhG 4.39 //

children.text:
śraddhāvān iti / śraddhāstikyabuddhir ādarapratyayas tadvāṃs
tatparaś ca śravaṇamananādiṣu vyāpṛtaḥ / kaś ca vyāpriyate /
saṃyatendriyaḥ7 / sa labhate / tac ca labdhvā8 parāṃ śāntiṃ muktim
acireṇa kṣipraṃ cādhigacchati9 // 39 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'The one endowed with faith' — <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is the conviction of truth, an attitude of reverence; one who possesses it, and who is devoted to it — engaged in hearing, reflection, and such. And who engages [thus]? One whose senses are controlled. He obtains [knowledge]. And having obtained it, one quickly, swiftly attains supreme peace, i.e., liberation. // 39 //

children.text: śraddhāvān ity uktam / tasya pratyudāharaṇārtham āha10 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'One endowed with faith' was stated. For its counterexample, he says:

children.text:
(ajñaś cāśraddadhānaś ca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati /
nāyaṃ loko 'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ // BhG_4.40 //)
children.translated_text: 'The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self perishes; for the doubting self, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.' // BhG 4.40 //

children.text: ajñeti / ajño 'nātmavādī11 yathokte 'rthe śraddhām akurvann
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'The ignorant' — the ignorant is the non-believer in the self; one who does not place faith in the meaning as stated,

aśraddadhāno
bhavati vā mokṣo na veti12 saṃśayātmā sa vinaśyati / ajñānāt /

children.text:
yogeti4 / yogena brahmārpaṇanyāyena paramātmani sannyastaṃ samyag
nyastam ekīkṛtaṃ karma yenātmajñānena5 ca (samyak) chinnaḥ saṃśayo
yena6 tam ātmavantam apramādinaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti7 // 41 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Through <s>yoga</s>' — through <s>yoga</s>, by the principle of offering to <s>Brahman</s>, actions have been properly renounced — deposited, unified — in the <s>Paramātman</s>; and by the knowledge of the self, doubt has been properly cut. Him — the self-possessed, the vigilant one — actions do not bind. // 41 //

children.text: prakaraṇārtham upasaṃharati ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He concludes the topic of the section:

children.translated_text: Therefore, cutting with the sword of knowledge this doubt born of ignorance dwelling in the heart, resort to <s>yoga</s> — arise, O <s>Bhārata</s>! // BhG 4.42 //

children.text: tasmād iti / tasmād ajñānasambhūtam ajñānād utpannaṃ hṛdaye8

sthitaṃ
saṃśayaṃ jñānam evāsis tena chittvā nirasya9 yogam ātiṣṭha
brahmārpaṇanyāyena karmānutiṣṭha / utthiṣṭha ca /
kim āsse viṣaṇṇamanā10 iveti /

brahmaiva kartṛ kārakānantaraṃ2 karma ca ity uktam / anayoḥ

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Brahman</s> itself is the agent, the instruments, and the action — this was stated. Since between these two — <s>karmasannyāsa</s> (renunciation of action) and <s>karmayoga</s> (yoga of action) — which are the subjects of knowledge of difference and non-difference respectively, there is mutual contradiction, making it impossible for a single person to practice both, which of the two is more praiseworthy? — wishing to ask, <s>Arjuna</s> said:
[Commentary:] 'Renouncing all actions in Me' — by this, the renunciation of actions performed by the agent was stated as being into <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).

(sannyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punar yogaṃ ca śaṃsasi /

sannyāsam iti / mayi sarvāṇi --- iti sannyāsaṃ kathayasi ---
brahmārpaṇam --- yogasannyastakarmaṇām --- yogam ātiṣṭha ---
iti karmayogam / śeṣaṃ nigadavyākhyātam // 1 //

children.text: śrībhagavān uvāca5 ---

tayos tu karmasannyāsāt karmayogo viśiṣ.yate // BhG_5.2 //)

children.text: sannyāsa iti / mayi sarvāṇi --- iti ya uktaḥ6 sannyāso yaś cāyam
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Renunciation' — the renunciation spoken of as 'renouncing all actions in Me,' and this

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Should be known' — one who does not hate what is extremely beneficial, nor desire beneficial fruit, who performs obligatory action thinking 'this is simply to be done' and offers its fruit to <s>Īśvara</s> — he should be understood as the eternal renouncer. And this one, though stationed in action, being free from pairs of opposites — free from attraction, aversion, and the like — is easily, without difficulty, released from the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>, i.e., attains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). // 3 //

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, it is objected that it is improper for renunciation and <s>karma-yoga</s> to have the same fruit of the highest good, since, like the difference in their nature, a difference in fruits would be proper. To remove this doubt, he says:

children.translated_text: The childish speak of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> as different, not the wise. One who is properly established in even one of them obtains the fruit of both. // BhG 5.4 //

kim idam avāntaram aprastutam upanyasyate13 / nāyaṃ doṣaḥ / tāv eva
sannyāsayogau sāṅkhyayogaśabdābhyāṃ nirdiṣṭau / yogaśabdas
tāvat prakṛtaṃ yogaṃ na
children.translated_text: What is this irrelevant, unrelated topic being introduced? This is no fault. Those very <s>sannyāsa</s> and <s>yoga</s> are denoted by the words <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>yoga</s>. The word '<s>yoga</s>' certainly does not abandon the <s>yoga</s> that is the topic under discussion.

children.translated_text: denotes the renouncer. Here the suffix has the meaning of 'possessing,' by the <s>arśādi</s> rule. Just as '<s>pāpa</s>' (sin) — one possessing it is so called. The renouncer can attain <s>Brahman</s> without <s>yoga</s> only with difficulty. 'With difficulty' modifies the verb — meaning 'with greater hardship.' The sage endowed with <s>yoga</s> — the vision of non-difference — the renouncer, reaches <s>Brahman</s> before long. Therefore he too, at the time of offering, is established in the vision of non-difference — thus the equal fruitfulness is established. // 6 //

[Commentary:] 'Renunciation' — the word '<s>sannyāsa</s>' means the renouncer (<s>sannyāsin</s>). Because the designation uses the nominative case, it is not that renunciation itself is to be attained.

If the non-applicability of action is asserted because of a contradiction between knowledge of the <s>ātman</s> and the <s>yoga</s> of action—'for the <s>yoga</s> of action is caused by false knowledge, and that false knowledge has been removed by true knowledge'—[we respond:] that is a sequence of progressive stages. [Commentary:] If this is so, then the simultaneous cessation of both worldly and Vedic action would absurdly follow, since the presence of false knowledge applies without distinction [to both]. And consequently, there would be the absence even of bathing, sipping water, begging for alms, and the like. For things that are bound to a single cause must either all function together or all cease together—there is no other course. And for whom would bathing [be prescribed]?

[Commentary:] Like another's body, as with the abandonment of action, the abandonment of the body [too] would be fitting. Since its purpose has been served, there is no [need for] its nourishment through food and the like. And through [the newly attained] lordly power, the liberated one has the capacity for abandonment. Who, being independent, would carry a corpse on his shoulder? Moreover, one who desires liberation through the cessation of the cognition of difference and through the abandonment of all action would thereby be maintaining that liberation itself does not exist—because it is impossible. Just as bathing is impossible by removing waves from the ocean. For the body, sense faculties, and mind are the [ever-present] causes; when they exist, the occasioned cognition of difference and the threefold action—bodily, mental, and verbal—inevitably operate, like smoke when there is a conjunction of fire and fuel. Therefore, 'because of a contradiction between knowledge and action' is a specious reason, presented for the purpose of confusing others—and it is unestablished, because we hear of great knowers of <s>Brahman</s> such as <s>Uddālaka</s>, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, and others engaging in teaching sons and the like.

children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> would have already understood it. In that case, since the abandonment and the yoga of action pertain to different persons, how could there be an occasion for the question? And the Lord's answer too would not be appropriate: 'Both lead to the highest good.' 'And the yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action.' How can both the abandonment of action and its performance be productive of the highest good? For abandonment is [mere] absence—it cannot be a cause of the highest good because it is not a real thing. If the highest good were attained from non-existence, who would carry the heavy burden of action on his head? And a question-and-answer pertaining to abandonment and action as performed by [respectively] the wise and [the unwise] is not possible—since the abandonment of action even by the wise has been shown to be untenable, by reasoning and by scripture.

children.translated_text: Now, the root '<s>ās</s>' (to sit) is used in the sense of indifference [i.e., abiding without action]. Just as [in the expressions] 'he sits occupying a house,' 'he sits occupying a field' — [the verb] indicates indifference, not instruction. [Similarly here.] Now,

'All' — the word 'all' refers to what is under discussion. Having renounced — having properly deposited — both worldly and Vedic action in <s>Brahman</s> through the spiritual mind (<s>adhyātmacetas</s>), perceiving the unity that all action is <s>Brahman</s> alone, that <s>Brahman</s> alone is the agent and the fruit of action — first, in the state of [active] practice; afterward, having attained illumination and become one with the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), he sits happily — free from all bondage, like the <s>Antaryāmin</s> (Inner Controller). Because it is declared that <s>karma</s> whose fruits have already begun to manifest is exhausted through experience alone, this [state continues] until the fall of the body. And thus the <s>śruti</s> says: 'His delay is only until he is not freed from this body — then he will attain.' As long as he is not freed from the body — because of the obstruction caused by the experience of the fruits of <s>karma</s> whose results have already begun to manifest — that long alone is the delay for this knower. But he experiences that <s>karma</s> [naturally], since there is no obstruction [to its exhaustion through experience].

this <s>Paramātman</s>, having become [one with the self], in the city of nine gates — seven openings in the head: two nostrils, two eyes, two ears, one mouth; and below, two — the anus and the genitals — in the city that is the body, the embodied one neither acts nor causes action. Because the connection with the body has ceased [in terms of identification], there is consequently no effect of it [upon him]. But in the prior state, because the connection with the body continues, he acts and causes action. 'Acting' refers to independent agency; 'causing action' refers to instrumental agency — as in 'he cooks' and 'he causes to cook.' children.translated_text: sitting in the body like a corporeal entity is not appropriate. But 'sitting' is merely due to [false] identification — 'This body is mine, I am its master' — and the qualifications 'neither acting nor causing action' too do not fit in this [alternative] interpretation. Moreover, since the word 'all' — [which would include] purification, sipping water, eating, drinking, and the like, instructing students, and countless other [actions that are in fact] being performed — the verse is all the more inexpressive for the advocates of total renunciation.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, the use of 'mind' [in the verse] is required [to indicate that] all actions are renounced — abandoned — by the mind alone. And the use of '<s>sannyasya</s>' (having renounced) should not be taken [as indicating formal <s>sannyāsa</s>]; he should have said '<s>santyajya</s>' (having given up), to avoid doubt. Therefore, '<s>manasā sannyasya</s>' (having renounced mentally) is for the understanding of the kind of renunciation previously described [i.e., offering to <s>Brahman</s>], as in [the expression] 'those whose actions are renounced through <s>yoga</s>.' Therefore, the meaning as explained [by us] alone is established. (13)

children.text: kartṛtvādinibandhanaṃ
children.translated_text: The basis for agency and the like

'Not' — the liberated Lord, the sovereign, the one who has attained [perfection] — He is spoken of [in terms of agency] because, like [the master of] a living being [who has] children, servants, and spouse that are to be governed, [such entities] exist here [in the world]. He does not [create] agency and the like — He does not provide for His own dependents, because the relationship of master and owned has ceased [for Him]. Nor does He create a fruit corresponding to action characterized by service and the like, because He is one whose desires are [already] fulfilled.

children.translated_text: How then is there agency and the connection of action with fruit for the world? To that he says: 'Rather, [one's own] nature operates.' <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) arise from <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance). <s>Karma</s> is rooted in them. From that, the assumption of a body. Then again <s>karma</s>; again ignorance; again <s>rāga</s> and <s>dveṣa</s> — thus this wheel simply revolves. The state of non-engagement of the Lord — the condition of the <s>yogin</s> whose <s>yoga</s> has fully ripened, being equal to the Lord — is stated here for the purpose of illustration. But for the Lord in His state of engagement, His role as the arranger of the world in accordance with the <s>karma</s> of living beings is established by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. (14)

children.translated_text: 'Does not take on' — He does not accept the sin belonging to anyone. Nor does He accept merit — because there is no motive [for Him to do so]. Since the Lord does not employ the world for His own purpose — then by what are beings deluded? To this he says: By nature — by <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), by <s>avidyā</s> (nescience). <s>Avidyā</s> is inverted knowledge — the identification of the self with the body and the like, and the non-apprehension of the nature of <s>Brahman</s> — this is called <s>avidyā</s>. By that, knowledge is covered — concealed. By that [covered knowledge], they are deluded. (15)

The mention of the dog and the dog-eater is for the purpose of [illustrating] the utterly untouchable and contemptible categories. (śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prāk śarīravimocanāt /
kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ // BhG_5.23 //)
children.translated_text: (One who is able to endure, even here, before the release from the body, the force arising from desire and anger — that one is a <s>yogin</s>, that one is a happy person.) (BhG 5.23)

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'One who is able' — to endure, to restrain, even here in this body — not merely superficially,

lakṣaṇamātraṃ

krodhodbhavaṃ3

children.translated_text: but rather before the release from the body, i.e. until death. The force born from desire and the force born from anger. Desire is the wish for the attainment of what is not yet obtained. The mental activity impelled by that is the force of desire — the restraint of the mental activity of attachment is the restraint of the upsurge of desire, [which is] indicated by distortions of the eyes and face. And [the restraint of] the force arising from anger. One who restrains these two forces — he is a <s>yogin</s>, he is a happy person. (23)

children.text: yaś caivaṃ kāmakrodhau jitvātmani10 vartate sa mukta evam ucyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And one who, having thus conquered desire and anger, abides in the self — he is called 'liberated' in this way.

(antaḥsukho 'ntarārāmas tathāntarjyotir eva yaḥ /
sa pārtha paramaṃ yogaṃ brahmabhūto 'dhigacchati // BhG_5.24 //)
children.translated_text: (One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and likewise whose light is within — that one, O <s>Pārtha</s>, having become <s>Brahman</s>, attains the supreme <s>yoga</s>.) (BhG 5.24)

children.text: antar iti / antarātmani11 sukhaṃ yasyāsāv antaḥsukhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Within' — one whose happiness is in the inner self — he is one of inner happiness.

brahmabhūto 'dhigacchati // 24 //14
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One whose delight and play is in the inner self — he is one of inner delight. Likewise, one whose light is the inner self — he is one of inner light, not the light of wind, sun, and the like. He, O <s>Pārtha</s>, [attains] the supreme <s>yoga</s>. '<s>Yoga</s>' means that which is attained — that <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self); having become <s>Brahman</s>, he attains [It]. (24)

children.text: kiṃ ca

children.translated_text: (For ascetics who are freed from desire and anger, who have controlled their minds, who have realized the self — <s>brahmanirvāṇa</s> exists close at hand.) (BhG 5.26)

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Or, [it refers to] householders and others, or <s>yatins</s> meaning those who are diligent. The etymological explanation of that is

children.text:
yatacetasām iti / abhito nikaṭe samīpakāla ity arthaḥ / nirvāṇaṃ
niratiśayānandarūpam7 / abhita ubhayata ity eke / jīvatāṃ8 mṛtānāṃ
ceti / tad asat / jīvatāṃ cen nirvāṇaṃ9 siddhaṃ mṛtānāṃ
daṇḍāpūpikayā siddham iti na vaktavyaṃ mṛtānām iti // 26 // 10
children.translated_text: 'those whose minds are controlled.' '<s>Abhitas</s>' means near, in close proximity — this is the meaning. <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is of the nature of unsurpassed bliss. Some [interpret] '<s>abhitas</s>' as 'on both sides' — [meaning] for the living and the dead. That is incorrect. If <s>nirvāṇa</s> for the living is established, then for the dead it is established as a corollary — hence there is no need to say 'for the dead.' (26)
[Commentary:] '<s>Yatins</s>' means renunciants, wandering mendicants. This is for illustration.

(sparśān kṛtvā bahir bāhyāṃś cakṣuś caivāntare bhruvoḥ /

manasāntarātmani nopasarpanti15 tadā viṣayā bahir eva bhavanti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Contacts' — having made the external sense-objects to remain outside — when they do not approach the inner self through the mind, then the objects remain outside indeed.

Having equalized <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> — inhalation and exhalation — moving within the nostrils; one should neither make the inhalation excessive nor the exhalation. The meaning is: having allowed them to proceed according to their natural course. (27)

vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ // BhG_5.28 //)
children.translated_text: (The sage (<s>muni</s>) who has controlled the senses, mind, and intellect, whose supreme goal is liberation, who is free from desire, fear, and anger — he is forever liberated.) (BhG 5.28)

children.text:
yateti / niyatānīndriyāṇi mano buddhiś ca yasya sa vaśī /
mananān muni(ḥ) / mokṣaḥ param ayanaṃ gatir yasyāsau
mokṣaparāyaṇaḥ /
vigatecchā bhayaṃ ca krodhaś ca yasyāsau vigatecchābhayakrodhaḥ /
icchā kāmaḥ / ya evaṃ sadā varta(te) mukta eva saḥ /
nāsty atra vicāraṇā3 // 28 //4
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One whose senses, mind, and intellect are controlled — he is self-mastered. '<s>Muni</s>' — from '<s>manana</s>' (reflection). One whose supreme destination and goal is liberation — he is <s>mokṣaparāyaṇa</s>. One from whom desire, fear, and anger have departed — he is '<s>vigatecchābhayakrodha</s>.' Desire means <s>kāma</s> (craving). One who abides thus always is indeed liberated. There is no deliberation needed here. (28)

children.text:
muktyupāyo darśitaḥ / jñeyas tu sākṣād darśayitavyo yaṃ jñātvā
mucyetety āha5 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The means of liberation has been shown. But the one who is to be known — who should be directly revealed, knowing whom one becomes liberated — to that he says:

children.text:
(bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram /
suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntim ṛcchati // BhG_5.29 //)
children.translated_text: (Knowing Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all worlds, the friend of all beings — one attains peace.) (BhG 5.29)

children.text:
bhoktāram iti / yajñānāṃ tapasāṃ ca phalam / tasya bhoktā /
bhoktaiḥ samarpitāni6 phalāni7 dṛṣṭvā tṛṣyati8 tuṣyatīty arthaḥ
/
na punas tasyāptakāmasyānyādṛśo9 bhogo 'sti yathā nivedya samarpaṇe10
devatā prīyate / sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ mahāntaram īśvaram /
(suhṛdaṃ) pratyupakārānapekṣayo 'pakāriṇaṃ jñātvā māṃ11
śāntiṃ mokṣam ṛcchati
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'The enjoyer' — of sacrifices and austerities, [He is] the fruit. He is the enjoyer thereof. Having seen the fruits offered to him, he is pleased, he is satisfied — this is the meaning. It is not that this one whose desires are fulfilled has some other kind of enjoyment, as when a deity is pleased by offerings. [He is] the great Lord of all worlds. [He is] the friend (<s>suhṛd</s>) — one who does good without expecting reciprocation. Knowing Me — one attains peace, liberation,

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the immediately preceding text, because of the mention of knowledge alone, one whose mind is confused by the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> view might think: 'From that [knowledge] alone, liberation would result; therefore, renunciation of action should be undertaken' — and such a thought might arise in a seeker of liberation, out of the ease [of renunciation]. To refute this, he says:

children.text: śrībhagavān uvāca ---
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text:
(anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ /
sa sannyāsī sa yogī ca na niragnir na cākriyaḥ // BhG_6.1 //)
children.translated_text: 'One who performs obligatory action without depending on its fruit — he is the <s>sannyāsin</s> (renouncer) and the <s>yogin</s>, not one who is without fire and without activity.' // BhG 6.1 //

children.text:

karma svāśrayam avihitaṃ3 karoti yaḥ sa sannyāsī4 sa yogī ca /
sa sannyāsī --- mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi --- ity uktalakṣaṇo5
yogī ca --- brahmārpaṇam --- iti / na niragnir nirastāgniḥ /
akriyas tyaktakarmā / naivaṃvidhaḥ6 sannyāsī yogī ca yaḥ7 /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Without activity' means one who has abandoned action. Such a person is not a [true] <s>sannyāsin</s> or <s>yogin</s>.

children.text: (i)ha vidyayā saha sambandho nakartuḥ8 / sāṅkhyānāṃ prasiddhas
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here, there is no association to be made between [mere] knowledge and a non-doer. The well-known

children.text: tyaktakarmā caturthāśramī so 'tra pratiṣidhyate / yo hi buddhipūrvaṃ9
children.translated_text: <s>Sāṅkhya</s> renouncer of action in the fourth <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) is being rejected here. For one who intentionally

children.text: kartavyaṃ na karoti nāsāv āśrāmī /
children.translated_text: does not perform obligatory actions is not a [legitimate] member of an <s>āśrama</s>.

children.text: prāyaścittī hi saḥ / tena saha vidyayā10 saha sambandho na kartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He is [rather] one who requires expiation. Association should not be made between him and knowledge.

children.text: atraikaveṇupāṇayaḥ karmatyāginaṃ mūrdhni11 padaṃ nihitam upalabhya
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here, those who carry a single staff [i.e., the followers of Śaṅkara's ekadaṇḍī sannyāsa], finding that their foot has been placed on the head of the renouncer of action,

[Commentary:] 'Without depending' — one who has abandoned the intention of the fruit of action, [yet] performs the obligatory, ever-to-be-done action, as ordained for his own <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) — he is the <s>sannyāsin</s>, he is the <s>yogin</s>. He is the <s>sannyāsin</s> — as characterized by 'renouncing all actions in Me'; and the <s>yogin</s> — as characterized by '<s>Brahman</s> is the offering.' 'Not one without fire' — not one who has cast away the sacred fires.

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And the purpose of this sentence is to negate those without fire and without activity, who were [mistakenly] accepted based on previous statements — no other meaning for this sentence exists. Just as —

[Commentary:] striving to interpret it otherwise, thunder forth much that is incoherent. [They say:] '<s>Sannyāsin</s>-hood and <s>yogin</s>-hood are said for the purpose of praising the householder.' But [they claim] that the rejection of one without fire and without activity is not being made. That is wrong — because this sentence is directed toward the rejection of the other [view]. One who always performs obligatory action has <s>sannyāsin</s>-hood and <s>yogin</s>-hood.

Moreover, the <s>sannyāsin</s> who is without fire and without activity is well known; the <s>karmayogin</s> possesses activity. Therefore, the <s>sannyāsin</s> is different [from the <s>yogin</s>], and the <s>karmayogin</s> is different — anticipating this opposing view, [the Lord] shows the non-contradiction:

Just as the word '<s>vaidya</s>' (physician) is conventionally restricted to a medical practitioner, but etymologically applies everywhere — 'one born of knowledge is a <s>vaidya</s>' — so whoever possesses knowledge is called [a <s>vaidya</s>].

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What was said — '[<s>sannyāsin</s>-hood and <s>yogin</s>-hood] cannot coexist simultaneously' — this is not a fault, because the reason [for their coexistence] is present. Thus he says: 'For no one who has not renounced intention' — one whose intention regarding action has been deposited [in the Lord], such that he is one of renounced intention — one who is the opposite of that does not become a <s>yogin</s> at all. The consciousness of those who have been conditioned by the awareness of difference through many births does not suddenly [attain] the awareness of non-difference — 'I am <s>Brahman</s>.' Therefore, from all [stages of life], one who through His grace attains the knowledge of non-duality — therefore, this is merely the fruit of differences in the person's stages.

Special knowledge—[such as] 'I am He' (<s>so'ham</s>) and the like. 'This' refers to what was previously mentioned. I shall declare—completely. The knowledge which, having known, nothing further remains to be known here in this world. (2)

children.text: durlabhaṃ ca matsvarūpajñānam / katham ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And knowledge of My true nature is rare. How so?

children.text:
(manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid yatati siddhaye /
yatatām api siddhānāṃ kaścin māṃ vitti tattvataḥ // BhG_7.3 //)
children.translated_text: (Among thousands of human beings, scarcely one strives for perfection. And of those who strive, even among the perfected, scarcely one knows Me in truth.) (BhG 7.3)

children.text:
manuṣyeti / manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu madhye kaścid yatati siddhaye
yatnaṃ1 karoti / yatatām api teṣāṃ siddhānāṃ2 siddhyarthaṃ3
pravṛttānām ity arthaḥ / kaścin māṃ vetti tattvataḥ4
children.translated_text: scarcely one knows Me in truth—

children.text: yāthātathyena // 3 //
children.translated_text: as I truly am. (3)

[Commentary:] 'Among humans'—among thousands of human beings, scarcely one strives for perfection, makes effort. And even among those who strive, among those who have attained perfection—meaning, among those who have engaged for the purpose of attainment—

children.text: śrotāram abhimukhīkṛtyedānīṃ5 savistaram ātmānaṃ kathayati ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, having engaged the listener's attention, He describes Himself in detail:

children.text:
(bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca /
ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā // BhG_7.4 //)
children.translated_text: (Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego-sense—this is My <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), divided eightfold.) (BhG 7.4)

children.text:
bhūmir iti / bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ kham iti pañcāpi bhūtamātrā
nirdiśyante6 sthūlaśarīrārambhiṇyaḥ / mano buddhir ity antaḥkaraṇaṃ
nirdiśyate / manograhaṇena bāhyam api karaṇaṃ gṛhyate
buddhīndriyakarmendriyalakṣaṇam7 /
ahaṅkāra ity anātmany ātmābhimāna ātmani cānātmābhimānaḥ /
sa8 ubhayavidho viparītapratyayaḥ saṃsārahetur yam avidyety
ācakṣate / me madīyāṣṭadhā bhinnā prakṛtiḥ
sthāvarajaṅgamalakṣaṇasya bhūtajātasya // 4 //
children.translated_text: of the totality of beings characterized as stationary and moving. (4)

[Commentary:] 'Earth'—earth, water, fire, air, space—all five elemental substrates are indicated, which are the originators of the gross body. 'Mind and intellect'—the inner organ is indicated. By the mention of 'mind,' the external organs too are included—characterized as cognitive senses and motor senses. '<s>Ahaṅkāra</s>' (ego-sense)—the false identification of the self with the non-self, and of the non-self with the self. This twofold erroneous cognition is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, which they call <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). My—this is My <s>prakṛti</s>, divided eightfold,

children.text: imām acetanāṃ prakṛtiṃ pṛthakkṛtya cetanāṃ nirdeṣṭum āha8 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having separated this unconscious <s>prakṛti</s>, in order to indicate the conscious [<s>prakṛti</s>], he says:

children.text:
(apareyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām /
jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat // BhG_7.5 //)
children.translated_text: (This is the inferior [<s>prakṛti</s>]. But know My other, superior <s>prakṛti</s>, which has become the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), O mighty-armed one, by which this world is sustained.) (BhG 7.5)

children.text: apareti10 / apareyam aṣṭadhā11 bhinnā prakṛtir aparā bhogyarūpā12
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Inferior'—this <s>prakṛti</s>, divided eightfold, is the inferior one, of the nature of what is to be enjoyed,

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] dependent [on another]. Know My other, principal <s>prakṛti</s> as different from this,

children.translated_text: related to Me. 'Which has become the <s>jīva</s>'—which has attained the state of a living being,

children.text: (tathā ca) śrutiḥ --- anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya6 nāmarūpe
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Having entered [the world] through this living self,

children.text: vyākaravāṇi --- iti // 5 //
children.translated_text: let me differentiate names and forms.' (5)

children.text: dvābhyāṃ prakṛtibhyāṃ bhūtāni jāyanta ity āha7 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Beings are born from these two <s>prakṛtis</s>. He says:

children.text:
(etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇīty upadhāraya /
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā // BhG_7.6 //)
children.translated_text: (Know that all beings have these [two] as their source. I am the origin and dissolution of the entire world.) (BhG 7.6)

children.text: etad iti / ete dve8 prakṛtī yonī yeṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ tāny etadyonīni /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This'—these two <s>prakṛtis</s> are the source of those beings—those [beings] have these as their source.

children.text:
tatra yācetanā prakṛtiḥ sā kāryakāraṇarūpeṇa pariṇamate /
yā tu cetanā sā svakarmopārjitaphalabhoktṛrūpeṇāvatiṣṭhate9 /
tāny etāni jīvāviṣṭāni bhūtāni10 sarvāṇīty upadhāraya /
te ca matsambandhinyau11 / katham acetanā matto jātāś cetanāḥ punar
madasambhūtāḥ / yata evam ato 'haṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ
pralayas
tathā / prabhavanty asmād iti12 prabhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prabhava</s>' (origin)—[meaning:] they originate from this [<s>Brahman</s>], hence [it is called] the origin.

children.text:
pralīyante 'sminn iti pralayaḥ13 /
kathaṃ punar gamyate samastasya jagato mūlakāraṇaṃ brahma iti /
śruteḥ --- sad eva saumyedam agra āsīt --- iti /
tadaikṣata sa ātmā --- iti /
sadātmaśabdābhyāaṃ parāmarśāc cetanaṃ14 kāraṇaṃ niścīyate /
na hy anumānena15 kevalenātyantātīndriyaṃ jagatkāraṇaṃ kaścit
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Pralaya</s>' (dissolution)—they dissolve into this, hence dissolution. But how is it known that <s>Brahman</s> is the root cause of the entire world? From the <s>śruti</s>: 'Being alone, O dear one, this was in the beginning' [ChU 6.2.1]. 'That saw... that Self...' [TU 2.6]. Through the reference by the words '<s>sat</s>' (Being) and '<s>ātman</s>' (Self), it is ascertained that the cause is conscious. For no one is capable of establishing, by means of inference alone, the cause of the world which is completely beyond the senses—

children.text: samarthayituṃ śaktaḥ / asiddhānaikāntikaviruddhadoṣaduṣṭatvāt16 /
children.translated_text: because [such inference] is vitiated by the defects of being unestablished, non-exclusive, and contradictory.

[Commentary:] Among these, the unconscious <s>prakṛti</s> transforms in the form of cause and effect. But the conscious one abides in the form of an experiencer of the fruits earned by one's own <s>karma</s>. All these beings, pervaded by the <s>jīva</s>—know [them] thus. And both of these [<s>prakṛtis</s>] are related to Me. How? The unconscious one is born from Me; the conscious ones, in turn, are produced from Me. Since this is so, I am the origin and dissolution of the entire world.

tatra sāṅkhyāḥ pradhānaṃ jagatkāraṇaṃ varṇayanti /
naiyāyikavaiśeṣikāḥ paramāṇūn /
tatra vādinaḥ parasparaviruddhaṃ jalpanto nādyāpy antaṃ gatāḥ1 /
śrutivirodhāc cānumānam ābhāsībhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In that regard, the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> describe <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) as the cause of the world. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, [it is] the atoms. The proponents there, arguing contradictorily with each other, have not reached a conclusion even to this day. And because of contradiction with <s>śruti</s>, inference becomes a mere appearance [of valid knowledge].

children.text:
yat punar anumānaṃ śrutyanusāri tadanugrāhakatvenopanyasyate
tadāśrīyate / yena sarvajñaḥ sarvaśaktiś cetano jagatkartā sādhyate /
tārkikānumānena2 tu yasya yatra kartṛtvaṃ tatparijñānavatas
tacchaktiyuktasya3 kartṛtvopapatteḥ / rathaprāsādādikartṛvad iti4 /
anena5 cāsarvajñasyāsarvaśakter anīśvarasya6 siddheḥ
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By this [same inference], since one who is not omniscient, not omnipotent, and not the Lord cannot be established [as the world-cause],

children.text: prakṛtavastvasiddher
children.translated_text: [and since] the entity under discussion would remain unestablished—

children.text: anāśrayaṇam iti // 6 //
children.translated_text: it should not be relied upon. (6)

[Commentary:] But that inference which follows <s>śruti</s> is adduced as corroborative and is accepted—by which an omniscient, omnipotent, conscious creator of the world is established. For, through the logician's inference: wherever there is agency, there the tenability of agency follows for one who has complete knowledge of that [thing] and is endowed with the corresponding power—like the maker of chariots, palaces, and the like.

children.text: yata evam7 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since this is so:

children.text:
(mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya /
mayi sarvam idaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva // BhG_7.7 //)
children.translated_text: (There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>. All this is strung on Me, like clusters of gems on a thread.) (BhG 7.7)

children.text:
matta iti / mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyad aham eva sarvasmāj jagataḥ parataro
mūlakāraṇatvāt / kathaṃ punar asya kāraṇatvam / śaktipariṇāmāt /
tathā ca śrutiḥ8 --- tadātmānaṃ svayam akuruta ---
yathorṇanābhiḥ9 sṛjate gṛhṇate10 ca /
11apracyutasvarūpasyāpy acintyaśaktitvāt pariṇāmo bhavatīti /
yathākāśo12 vāyurūpeṇa pariṇamate na svarūpavināśo vāyoś ca
pañcavṛttirūpeṇādhyātmam13 /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Than Me'—there is nothing higher than Me. I alone am higher than the entire world, because of being the root cause. But how is His causality [to be understood]? Through the transformation of [His] power. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'That Self made itself by itself.' 'Just as a spider emits and withdraws.' Even though His own nature remains undiminished, transformation occurs because of [His] inconceivable power. Just as space transforms into the form of wind without the destruction of its own nature, and wind [transforms] into the form of the five functions internally [in the body].

children.text:
acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃs tarkeṇa sādhayet /
prakṛtibhyaḥ3 paraṃ yat tu tad acintyasya4 lakṣaṇam // iti /

na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca vidyate
na5 tatsamaś cābhyadhikaś ca vidyate /
parāsya śaktir vividhaiva6 śrūyate
svābhāvikī7 jñānabalakriyā ca // iti /
children.translated_text: 'No effect or instrument is known of His; no one equal or superior to Him is found. His supreme power is heard of as manifold and natural—consisting of knowledge, strength, and action.'

children.text: arthaḥ /

praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu // BhG_7.8 //)
children.translated_text: (I am the flavor in water, O <s>Kaunteya</s>; I am the radiance in the moon and sun; I am the <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) in all the <s>Vedas</s>; I am sound in space and manhood in men.) (BhG 7.8)

But in the section on divine manifestations (<s>vibhūti</s>), whatever being is eminent—whether a cause or a non-cause—that is taught. That which is eminent among beings is taught as [what should be an object of] contemplation—

children.translated_text: it too is a cause of excellence, because of its use in meditation, chanting, and the like. 'I am the sound in space' —

children.text: śabdena hi3 sarvalokavyavahāraḥ pravartate / puruṣasyedaṃ pauruṣaṃ
children.translated_text: for through sound, all worldly transactions proceed. Manliness (<s>pauruṣam</s>) of a man

children.text: puṃstvaṃ prajananakāraṇam // 8 //
children.translated_text: is virility — the cause of procreation. (8)

Some connect [the verse as] 'waters pervaded by taste and form.' That is wrong — because it would break the syntactic connection as heard [in the text]; and because the attributes that are causes of sustenance are intended to be stated here. 'I am the radiance' — radiance means power. <s>Praṇava</s> is the <s>Oṃkāra</s>;

children.text:
(puṇyaṃ pṛthivyāṃ gandho 'smi tejaś cāsmi vibhāvasau /
jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaś cāsmi tapasviṣu // BhG_7.9 //)
children.translated_text: 'I am the holy fragrance in the earth, and I am the radiance in fire, the life in all beings, and I am the austerity in ascetics.' (BhG 7.9)

children.text: kiṃ ca ---

children.text:
(bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam /
buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham // BhG_7.10 //)
children.translated_text: 'Know Me, O <s>Pārtha</s>, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent, and the splendor of the splendid.' (BhG 7.10)

nityam / buddhir asmi buddhimatāṃ8 bṛhaspatibhārgavādīnām9 /
children.translated_text: permanent. 'I am the intelligence of the intelligent' — of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Śukra</s>), and the like.

children.text: tejaḥ prabhāvo 'smi tejasvināṃ10 rājñām // 10 //
children.translated_text: 'Splendor' — I am the power of the splendid, i.e. of kings. (10)
'Seed' — know Me as the seed, the root cause. 'Eternal' —

children.translated_text: 'And I am the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and passion. I am that desire in beings which is not opposed to <s>dharma</s>, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>.' (BhG 7.11)

children.translated_text: 'Many' — because even the distressed and the rest have latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) from previous births regarding the Blessed Lord — which is why they worship <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone and not other deities. The man of knowledge, however, is of single devotion, independent of any other purpose, endowed with <s>sannyāsa</s> (renunciation) and <s>karmayoga</s> (discipline of action) — at the end of many births, he takes refuge in Me. How does he take refuge? [Realizing] '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is everything.' <s>Vāsu</s> — all beings dwell (<s>vasanti</s>) in Him; or He dwells (<s>vasati</s>) in all beings as the <s>Antaryāmin</s> (Inner Controller) — hence '<s>Vāsu</s>.' '<s>Deva</s>' — from <s>devana</s>, meaning 'shining.' <s>Vāsu</s> and <s>deva</s> — hence <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the <s>Paramātman</s>. 'The Self alone is all this' — 'This was Being alone in the beginning, O dear one' — 'All this is this Self' — from <s>śruti</s>. He understands that [<s>Vāsudeva</s>] abides as the cause and as the manifest universe. Such a great soul is very rare. For there are also devotees who hold the vision of duality. (19)

prakaṭabhāvam āpannaṃ manyante mām abuddhayo 'lpabuddhayaḥ /
ayam api nārāyaṇākhyo viṣṇur mahādevādivad devatāviśeṣa eva
nātrādhikyaṃ kiñcid astīti /
paraṃ bhāvam ajānantaḥ samastasya jagato mūlakāraṇam īśvarāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Not knowing My supreme nature — [not knowing that I am] the root-cause of the entire world, the Lord

children.text: brahmarudrendrādīnām apy adhīśvaro 'yam ity ajānanto na māṃ
children.translated_text: even of the lords such as <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the rest — not knowing this, they do not

children.text: bhajante // 24 //
children.translated_text: worship Me. (24)

[Commentary:] 'Unmanifest' — Me, who by nature am unmanifest, extremely subtle, yet existing — they think to have come to manifestation, to a state of being perceptible — the unintelligent, those of little intelligence [think]: 'This <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, called <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is just a particular deity like <s>Mahādeva</s> and the rest — there is no superiority here.'

children.text:
kasyacid evāham anekasmin janmani bhaktim udvahataḥ svarūpaṃ
vivṛṇomi na sarvasya ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Only to someone who cultivates devotion over many births do I reveal My true form — not to everyone:

children.text:
(nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogam āyāsam āvṛtaḥ /
mūḍho 'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam // BhG_7.25 //)
children.translated_text: (I am not manifest to all, veiled by <s>yogamāyā</s>. This deluded world does not know Me, the unborn and imperishable.) (BhG 7.25)

children.text:
nāham iti / nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya / katham / yogamāyayā
sañcchanna aiśvaryayogaḥ sa eva / māyāsaṃvaraṇahetutvāt /
tasmān mūḍho 'yaṃ nābhijānāti mām ajam avyayam // 25 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this deluded [world] does not know Me, the unborn and imperishable. (25)

[Commentary:] 'I am not manifest to all.' How so? Concealed by <s>yogamāyā</s> — the <s>yoga</s> of lordly power is itself that [<s>māyā</s>]. Because it is the cause of the concealment by <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ tu sarvajñaḥ katham ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But I am omniscient — how?

children.text:
(vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna /
bhaviṣyanti ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana // BhG_7.26 //)
children.translated_text: (I know, O <s>Arjuna</s>, the beings that are past, present, and those yet to come; but Me, no one knows.) (BhG 7.26)

children.text:
vedeti / vedāhaṃ trikālaviṣayāṇi bhūtāni jānāmi /
māṃ tu veda na kaścana / ayaṃ mūḍho loka iti / yaḥ punar
jñānī sa jānāti vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti // 26 //
children.translated_text: is wise knows — '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is everything.' (26)
[Commentary:] 'I know' — I know beings pertaining to the three times — I know them. But Me, no one knows — this deluded world, that is. But the one who

children.text: kenāyaṃ loko mūḍhatvam āpannas tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What then causes this world to become deluded? That is stated:

children.text:
(icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata /
sarvabhūtāni sammohaṃ yānti sarge parantapa // BhG_7.27 //)
children.translated_text: (O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>, by the delusion of dualities arising from desire and aversion, all beings fall into complete bewilderment at the time of creation, O scorcher of foes.) (BhG 7.27)

children.text:
iccheti / icchā rāgaḥ / rāgadveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena /
(dvandvāni) śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhādīni tatsambandho moho dvandvamohaḥ /
upakāriṣu parārtheṣu rāgāt sukhaṃ tatsambandhī mohas tannibandhanā
ca pravṛttir apakāriṣu dveṣo duḥkhaṃ tannibandhanā ca nivṛttir iti /
evaṃ pravṛttinibaddhāni bhūtāni sarge śarīragrahaṇeṣu sammohaṃ
yānti / yadi punar dvandvaśabdena rāgadveṣayoḥ parāmarśaḥ kriyate
tadā1
dvandvagrahaṇam anarthakam icchādveṣasamutthena mohenety etāvad
vaktavyaṃ
syāt // 27 //2
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Desire' — desire means <s>rāga</s> (attachment). By the delusion of dualities arising from attachment and aversion — the dualities are cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and the like; the contact with them is the delusion, which is the delusion of dualities. From attachment to beneficial, external things comes pleasure; the delusion connected with that, and the engagement caused by it. From aversion to harmful things comes pain, and the disengagement caused by it. Thus, beings bound by engagement [and disengagement], at the time of creation — i.e. upon taking on bodies — fall into complete bewilderment. Now, if by the word 'dualities' attachment and aversion are referred to, then the word 'dualities' would be superfluous — it would suffice to say 'by the delusion arising from desire and aversion.' (27)

children.text: tatra tu ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But therein —

children.text:
(yeṣāṃ tv antaṃ gataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām /
te dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ // BhG_7.28 //)
children.translated_text: (But those persons of meritorious deeds, in whom sin has come to an end — they, freed from the delusion of dualities, worship Me with firm vows.) (BhG 7.28)

children.text: yeṣām iti / yeṣāṃ tv antaṃ gataṃ pāpaṃ kṣīṇaṃ pāpaṃ3
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Those in whom sin has come to an end' — whose sin has been exhausted

bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: worship Me with firm vows. (28)
through the accumulation of meritorious deeds — they, freed from the delusion of dualities arising from attachment and aversion,

children.text: evam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus:

children.text:
(jarāmaraṇamokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye /
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛcchram adhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam // BhG_7.29 //)
children.translated_text: (Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me — they know <s>Brahman</s>, the totality of the individual self, and action in its entirety.) (BhG 7.29)

children.text:
(jareti) / ye jarāmaraṇamokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti prayatante te
brahma tadviduḥ / kṛcchram adhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam /
vastutrayam etad arjunapraśnād anantaram uttaraṃ vakṣyāmaḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: These three things we shall explain as the answer following <s>Arjuna</s>'s question. (29)

[Commentary:] Those who strive, who make effort, for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me — they know that <s>Brahman</s>. And the totality of the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>), and action (<s>karma</s>) in its entirety.

children.translated_text: (And those who know Me together with the <s>adhibhūta</s>, the <s>adhidaiva</s>, and the <s>adhiyajña</s> — they, with minds united [in meditation], know Me even at the time of death.) (BhG 7.30)

children.text: sādhibhūteti // 30 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Together with the <s>adhibhūta</s>...' (30)

children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh chapter in the <s>Gītā</s> commentary composed by the Blessed <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: athāṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the eighth chapter.

children.text:
te brahma tad viduḥ --- iti ye bhagavatopakṣiptāḥ padārthās tāṃs
tattvato jñātum arjunaḥ pṛcchati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'They know that <s>Brahman</s>...' — the terms that were briefly introduced by the Blessed Lord — <s>Arjuna</s> asks about them in order to know them truly.

children.text: arjunaḥ (uvāca) ---
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: (kiṃ tad brahma kim adhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: (What is that <s>Brahman</s>? What is the <s>adhyātma</s>? What is <s>karma</s>, O Supreme Person?

children.text: adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktam adhidaivaṃ kim ucyate // BhG_8.1 //
children.translated_text: And what is called <s>adhibhūta</s>? What is said to be the <s>adhidaiva</s>? (BhG 8.1)

children.text:
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko 'tra dehe 'smin madhusūdana /
prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo 'si niyatātmabhiḥ // BhG_8.2 //)
children.translated_text: Who is the <s>adhiyajña</s> and how is He here in this body, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>? And at the time of death, how are You to be known by those of controlled minds?) (BhG 8.2)

children.text: kiṃ tad iti / ka iti svarūpapraśnatātparyam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'What is that?' — the purport of 'what?' is a question about the essential nature.

children.text:
katham iti prakārapraśnaḥ / kena prakāreṇāsau dehe 'smin bhavatīti /
prayāṇakāle maraṇakāle kena prakāreṇa jñeyo 'si niyatacittaiḥ //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'How?' is a question about the mode — by what mode does He exist in this body? 'At the time of death, at the time of departing — by what mode are You to be known by those of controlled minds?'

children.text: bhagavān (uvāca) ---
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text:
(akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate /
bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasañjñitaḥ // BhG_8.3 //)
children.translated_text: (The supreme imperishable is <s>Brahman</s>. One's own nature is called <s>adhyātma</s>. The creative act that brings about the existence of beings is designated as <s>karma</s>.) (BhG 8.3)

children.text:
akṣaram iti / na kṣaratīty akṣaraṃ paramaṃ brahma /
etad vai tad akṣaraṃ
gargi brāhmaṇā abhivadanti -- iti śruteḥ /
svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate / akṣaraśabdavācyasya paramātmana ātmīyo
bhāvo 'ṃśo jīvo 'dhyātmam ātmānaṃ deham adhikṛtya bhoktṛtvena
vartata
iti / bhūtānāṃ jīvānāṃ bhāvo bhāvanā karma / tasya pralayakāle
stimitasyāvasthitasyodbhavo vyaktiḥ phaladānayogyatāpādanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Imperishable' — that which does not decay is the imperishable, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. 'This indeed is that imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, which the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> speak of' — thus the <s>śruti</s>. 'One's own nature is called <s>adhyātma</s>' — the nature that is one's own, the portion of the <s>Paramātman</s> designated by the word 'imperishable' — the <s>jīva</s> (individual self), which is the <s>adhyātma</s>, functioning as the experiencer in relation to the body. The becoming (<s>bhāva</s>) of beings, i.e. <s>jīvas</s> — this is [their] conditioning, which is <s>karma</s>. The manifestation, the bringing to ripeness and fitness for fruit-giving, of that [<s>karma</s>] which has been quiescent at the time of dissolution —

children.text:
taṃ karotīti bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargo visṛṣṭir
hiraṇyagarbhādeḥ /
tathā ca mantraḥ --- hiraṇyagarbhaṃ janayāmāsa pūrvaṃ mano buddhyā
śubhayā saṃyunaktu --- iti / so 'yam īśvarasyāntaryāmiṇo
vyāpāraḥ karmasañjñitaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] that which does this is the <s>visarga</s> (creative emission) — the emanation from <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and the like. And thus the <s>mantra</s>: 'He gave birth to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> first; may he endow us with a pure intellect.' This activity of the Lord, the inner controller, is designated as <s>karma</s>.

children.text:
apareṣāṃ vyākhyā --- yajamānasya vyāpāraś carupuroḍāśādīnāṃ
devatoddeśena tyāgo visargaḥ / sa eva buddhidvāreṇa bhūtāny eva
bhāvās teṣām udbhavaṃ karotīti bhūtabhāvodbhavakaraḥ
children.translated_text: [and] the becoming of those entities — it brings about the arising of them — thus it is the '<s>bhūtabhāvodbhavakara</s>' (that which produces the arising of the states of beings),

children.text: karmasañjñita
children.translated_text: designated as
<s>karma</s>. (3)

[Commentary:] The interpretation of others: the activity of the sacrificer — the offering of <s>caru</s>, <s>puroḍāśa</s>, and the like to the deity — is the <s>visarga</s> (offering). That very [offering], through the medium of the intellect, [becomes] the entities themselves;

children.text:
(adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaś cādhidaivatam /
adhiyajño 'ham evātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃvara // BhG_8.4 //)
children.translated_text: (The <s>adhibhūta</s> is the perishable nature. The <s>adhidaivata</s> is the <s>puruṣa</s>. The <s>adhiyajña</s> is Myself alone, here in this body, O best of the embodied.) (BhG 8.4)

children.text: adhīti / adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ / kṣarati vinaśyatīti śarīre
viṣayalakṣaṇaḥ / cetano1 bhogyavargo jāyamāno 'niruddhyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: [it is] characterized by the objects of experience. The sentient aggregate of enjoyable [objects], arising and not being obstructed —

children.text:
puruṣaś cādhidaivatam / yo 'sāv ādityamaṇḍale hiraṇyagarbhaḥ
sarvadevatāmayaḥ / kṛtsnaṃ vairājaṃ śarīram āpūryāvasthitaḥ
puruṣo 'dhiyajño 'ham eva / atra yajñānām adhidevatāham eva /
yajño vai viṣṇuḥ --- iti śatapathaśruteḥ /
deho 'dhikaraṇatvena vyapadiśyate --- na mama idaṃ devatāyā iti
mānasas tyāgo yāga ucyate / ye ca dravyayajñā jñānayajñāḥ
svādhyāyayajñas teṣām aham evādhidevatety abhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] the <s>adhidaivata</s> is the <s>puruṣa</s>. That <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> in the solar orb, who comprises all deities, who pervades and fills the entire cosmic (<s>Vairāja</s>) body — that <s>puruṣa</s>. The <s>adhiyajña</s> is Myself alone. Here — of all sacrifices, I am the presiding deity. 'Sacrifice is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — thus the <s>Śatapatha</s> <s>śruti</s>. The body is mentioned as the locus — 'not mine, but the deity's' — the mental offering is what is called sacrifice. And for the material sacrifices, the knowledge-sacrifices, and the self-study-sacrifice — of all of them, I alone am the presiding deity — this is the purport.
[Commentary:] 'Adhi-' — the <s>adhibhūta</s> is the perishable nature; that which decays and perishes — in the body,

children.text:
anyeṣāṃ vyākhyā ---
dehasmin vaiśvānaravidhyaṅgabhūtāhutisādhanabhūta2 iti /
viśiṣṭāhutisādhanopalakṣaṇārthe dehaśabdo yajñaśabdaś ca
viśiṣṭayajñalakṣaṇapara iti / tad ayuktam /
yato yajñaviśeṣavyākhyānād yajñasāmānyavyākhyānaṃ yuktataram /

children.translated_text: The explanation of <s>visarga</s> as creation is appropriate. (4)

[Commentary:] The interpretation of others: in this body, as the limb of the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> meditation, [the <s>adhiyajña</s>] is the one through whom the specialized offering is accomplished. The word 'body' and the word 'sacrifice' are intended to denote the specialized sacrifice. That is untenable,

yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ // BhG_8.5 //)
children.translated_text: (And at the end of life, remembering Me alone while leaving the body — one who departs thus attains My state. There is no doubt about this.) (BhG 8.5)

anteti / vayaso 'nte tyaktvā kalevaraṃ śarīraṃ yaḥ prayāti sa

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] It is not only by remembering Me that one attains Me. Rather —

children.text:
(yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalevaram /
taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ // BhG_8.6 //)
children.translated_text: (Whatever being one remembers while leaving the body at the end — that very [state] one attains, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, being always conditioned by that very thought.) (BhG 8.6)

children.text:
yam iti / yaṃ yaṃ bhāvaṃ devatāviśeṣam anyad vā vastu smarann ante
dehaṃ tyajati1 taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvanayā bhāvito
vāsitāntaḥkaraṇaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: having an inner organ saturated [by that thought]. (6)

[Commentary:] Whatever being — whatever particular deity or any other entity — one remembers while leaving the body at the end, that very [state] one attains, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, being always conditioned by that very contemplation —

children.text: yata evam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since this is so —

children.text:
(tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yuddhya ca /
mayy arpitamanobuddhir mām evaiṣyasy asaṃśayam // BhG_8.7 //)
children.translated_text: (Therefore, at all times, remember Me and fight. With mind and intellect offered to Me, you shall come to Me alone — there is no doubt.) (BhG 8.7)

children.text:
tasmād iti / tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu madanusmaraṇaṃ kuru /
yuddhaṃ ca svadharmaṃ kurv ity arthaḥ / mayi samarpitaṃ mano
buddhiś ca yasya te sa tvaṃ mayy arpitamanobuddhiḥ / manovṛttiviśeṣo
vṛttimatī buddhiḥ /
ekam evāntaḥkaraṇaṃ paramārthataḥ / vyavahārasiddhyarthas tu
bhedavyapadeśaḥ / mām evaiṣyasy asaṃśayam / nāsminn arthe saṃśayo 'sti
/
na caitad āśaṅkitavyam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Therefore' — therefore, at all times, engage in remembrance of Me. And fight — perform your own <s>dharma</s>, that is the meaning. One whose mind and intellect are offered to Me — you are that one of mind and intellect offered to Me. The mental activity is a specific function; the intellect is that which possesses functions. The inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is in reality one alone. The differentiated designation is for the sake of pragmatic convention. 'You shall come to Me alone — there is no doubt.' There is no doubt in this matter. And this should not be feared —

children.text:
antakāle 'nyathāpi smṛtir bhavatīti / īśvaro hi sarvajñaḥ
karmānusārī
cittavṛtter niyantā // 7 //
children.translated_text: and is the controller of mental activity. (7)
[Commentary:] that at the time of death, memory may be otherwise. For the Lord is omniscient, follows <s>karma</s>,

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] To show the just-stated meaning in detail, he says:

(abhyāsayogayuktena cetasānanyavṛttinā /
paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārthānucintayan // BhG_8.8 //)
children.translated_text: (With a mind united through the <s>yoga</s> of practice, not wandering to anything else, constantly meditating, one goes to the supreme divine <s>Puruṣa</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>.) (BhG 8.8)

children.text:
abhyāseti / abhyāsaḥ samānapratyayaprabandho
vijātīyapratyayāvṛttikīlaḥ so 'yam abhyāsayogaḥ / tadyuktena
cetasānanyavṛttinā paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pratipadyate
cetasā tam evānucintayan // 8 //
children.translated_text: constantly meditating upon Him with the mind. (8)

[Commentary:] '<s>Abhyāsa</s>' (practice) is the continuous flow of similar cognitions, serving as the wedge that blocks dissimilar cognitions. That is the <s>yoga</s> of practice. With a mind united through that, not wandering to anything else — one goes to, attains, the supreme divine <s>Puruṣa</s>,

children.text: tam eva paramaṃ puruṣaṃ punar api viśinaṣṭi ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He further qualifies that very supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>:

children.text:
(kaviṃ purāṇam anuśāsitāram aṇor aṇīyāṃsam anusmared yaḥ /
sarvasya dhātāram acintyarūpam ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt // BhG_8.9 //)
children.translated_text: (One who meditates upon the ancient sage, the ruler, smaller than the smallest, the sustainer of all, of inconceivable form, sun-colored, beyond darkness —) (BhG 8.9)

children.text:
kavim iti / kaviṃ sarvajñam anuśāsitāraṃ niyantāram / tathā hi
śrutiḥ
--- etasya vākṣarasya praśāsane gargi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau2
tiṣṭhataḥ --- iti / aṇor aṇīyāṃsaṃ sūkṣmād api sūkṣmataram /
sūkṣmatvam ihāvayavopacayābhāvo vivakṣitaḥ / nabhaso 'pi sakāśād
atisūkṣmaḥ / paramakāraṇatvāt sarvakarmaphalasya dhātāraṃ
vidhātāram acintyarūpam / nahīdaṃ tad iti cintanīyam /
asya rūpaṃ (na) vidyate / asthūlam anaṇv ahrasvam adīrgham alohitam ---
iti rūpapratiṣedhāt / tathāpy upāsakānām anugrahārthaṃ rūpaṃ
nirdiśyate / ādityavarṇaṃ jyotirmayam ānandaikasvabhāvaṃ tamaso
jñānāndhakārāt parastād avasthitam ajñānatimirāpanudaṃ
children.translated_text: situated beyond the darkness of ignorance, dispelling the gloom of nescience,

children.text: svayaṃprakāśam anusmared yaḥ sa ity uttaragītāyāṃ
children.translated_text: self-luminous — one who meditates [upon such a Being] — the meaning of the sentence is completed in the

children.text: vākyārthaṃ samāpyate // 9 //
children.translated_text: following verse. (9)

[Commentary:] 'The sage' — the omniscient one, the ruler — the controller. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'By the command of this imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon are held in their positions.' Smaller than the smallest — subtler than even the subtle. Subtlety here means the absence of an aggregate of parts. Even subtler than space. Because of being the ultimate cause, the sustainer — the ordainer — of the fruit of all actions. Of inconceivable form — it is not to be conceived as 'it is this.' 'Its form is not [perceptible]'; 'not gross, not minute, not short, not long, not red...' — because of the negation of form [in the <s>śruti</s>]. Nevertheless, for the benefit of worshippers, a form is indicated: sun-colored — luminous, of the nature of pure bliss alone, beyond darkness —
