children.text:
1. viśeṣya
2. vivatau
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: kasmin punaḥ kāle 'nusmaret ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] At what time should one meditate?

children.text:
(prayāṇakāle manasācalena bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva /
bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam // BhG_8.10 //)
children.translated_text: (At the time of death, with an unshaken mind, endowed with devotion and with the power of <s>yoga</s>, having properly placed the <s>prāṇa</s> between the brows — that one attains that supreme divine <s>Puruṣa</s>.) (BhG 8.10)

children.text:
prayāṇeti / antakāle niścalena manasā bhaktyā
tadanusmaraṇāhlāditahṛdayena yogabalena ca
yogajanitasaṃskārapātisthair
children.translated_text: with firmness born of the dispositions produced by <s>yoga</s> practice,

children.text: yeṇa1 bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya suṣumṇayā2 nāḍyā
children.translated_text: having placed the <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) between the eyebrows through the <s>suṣumṇā nāḍī</s> (central channel),

children.text: niṣkramyety arthaḥ3 // 10 //
children.translated_text: departing — this is the meaning. // 10 //
[Commentary:] 'At the time of departure' — at the hour of death, with a steady mind, with a heart gladdened by devotion and the remembrance of that [Lord], and by the power of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: prāptavyaṃ padam anūdya tatprāptyupāyaṃ kathayiṣyann āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having restated the state to be attained, he is about to describe the means to attain it — he says:

children.text:
(yad akṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti viśanti yad yatayo vītarāgāḥ /
yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṅgraheṇābhidhāsye // BhG_8.11 //)
children.translated_text: 'That Imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) which the knowers of the <s>Veda</s> speak of, which the ascetics free from passion enter, desiring which they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) — that state I shall describe to you in brief.' // BhG 8.11 //

children.text:
yad iti / edad vai tadakṣaraṃ gargi --- atha parā yayā tadakṣaṛam
adhigamyate --- iti / viśanti pratipadyante / yatayo yatnavanto yad icchanto
brahmacaryaṃ maithunanivṛttim (caranti) / gṛhasthasyāpi sarvatra vā
pratiṣiddhavarjam ity anujñātagamanānivṛttasyāvaśyakaṛtukālagāmino
brahmacaryam asty eva / tat te padaṃ tat padaprāptyupāyaṃ saṅgraheṇa
saṅkṣepeṇa kathayiṣyāmi // 11 //
children.translated_text: in brief. // 11 //

[Commentary:] 'That' — 'This indeed is that Imperishable, O <s>Gārgi</s>' — and 'Now, the higher [knowledge], by which that Imperishable is attained' — thus from <s>śruti</s>. 'Enter' means attain. 'Ascetics' means those who strive. 'Desiring which, they practice <s>brahmacarya</s>' — abstinence from sexual intercourse. Even for a householder, <s>brahmacarya</s> exists everywhere or [at least] the cessation of prohibited [sexual contact] — that is, for one who does not abstain from permitted intercourse and who frequents [his wife only] at the obligatory times, <s>brahmacarya</s> indeed exists. That state and the means to attain that state — I shall tell you

children.text:
(sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi niruddhya ca /
mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yogadhāraṇām // BhG_8.12 //)
children.translated_text: 'Having restrained all the gates [of the senses], and confined the mind in the heart, having placed one's own <s>prāṇa</s> in the head — established in the concentration of <s>yoga</s>.' // BhG 8.12 //

children.text:
sarveti / sarvāṇīndriyadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdayakamalanilaye
parameśvare sanniruddhya tālumūlavinirgatayā brahmanāḍyā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'All' — having restrained all the gates of the senses, and having firmly confined the mind in the Supreme Lord who dwells in the lotus of the heart, through the <s>brahma-nāḍī</s> (channel of <s>Brahman</s>) that issues from the root of the palate —

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text:
1. ^stheryeṇa
2. suvanyayā
3. niṣkrametyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: [Manuscript variant readings.]
[Page 185]

children.text:
suṣumṇākhyayorddvam udgamayyātmanaḥ prāṇaṃ mūrdhnyādhāyāsthito
yogadhāraṇām / yogadhāraṇāṃ gṛhītvety arthaḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] called the <s>suṣumṇā</s>, ascending upward, having placed one's own <s>prāṇa</s> in the head — established in the concentration of <s>yoga</s>; 'established in the concentration of <s>yoga</s>' means having taken up — this is the meaning. // 12 //

children.text:
(om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran /
yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // BhG_8.13 //)
children.translated_text: 'Uttering the single-syllable <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Oṃ</s>, remembering Me — one who departs, abandoning the body, goes to the supreme goal.' // BhG 8.13 //

children.text:
om iti / śabdabrahmaikākṣaram iti viśeṣaṇaṃ
saṃhitādibrahmanivṛttyartham / vyāharann uccārayan1 / māṃ
paramātmānam
ākāśavat sarvavyāpinaṃ sarvajñam ānandam amṛtam / tyajaṃ dehaṃ yaḥ
prayāti sa yāti paramāṃ gatim / antakāle ca mām evaiti --- (iti yat)
sāmānyenoktaṃ tad idānīṃ viśeṣitam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Oṃ</s>' — the qualifier 'single-syllable' for the word-<s>Brahman</s> is for the purpose of distinguishing it from the <s>Brahman</s> of <s>saṃhitā</s> (compiled text) and such. 'Uttering' means pronouncing. Me — the <s>Paramātman</s>, all-pervading like space, omniscient, blissful, immortal. One who departs abandoning the body — he goes to the supreme goal. What was stated in general terms — 'and at the end, remembering Me alone' — that has now been specified.

children.text:
kecid atra kramamuktyabhiprāyam idaṃ na sadyomuktipradarśanārtham iti
vadanti / etad vai satyakāma paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yad oṅkāraḥ ---
iti śruteḥ / oṅkārālambanopāsanaphalam idaṃ kathyata iti /
tadapavyākhyānam / paravidyādhikārāt / yad akṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Some here say that this [passage] has the intention of gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>), not the demonstration of immediate liberation (<s>sadyomukti</s>), citing the <s>śruti</s>: 'This indeed, O <s>Satyakāma</s>, is the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>, which is <s>Oṃkāra</s>.' [They say] this [verse] describes the fruit of meditation using <s>Oṃkāra</s> as a support. That is a wrong interpretation — because the topic pertains to the higher knowledge. Since the promise was 'that Imperishable which the knowers of the <s>Veda</s> speak of' —

children.text: iti pratijñānāt kathaṃ kālāntaramuktirūpaṃ2 varṇyate // 13 //
children.translated_text: how can a result that is liberation at a later time be being described? // 13 //

children.text: na cāhaṃ durlabhaḥ satatābhiyuktasya ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And I am not hard to attain for one who is constantly devoted —

children.text:
(ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ /
tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ // BhG_8.14 //)
children.translated_text: 'One who, with undivided mind, remembers Me constantly, always — for him I am easy to attain, O <s>Pārtha</s>, for the ever-disciplined <s>yogin</s>.' // BhG 8.14 //

children.text:
ananyeti / yasyānyatra3 ceto nāsty asāv ananyacetāḥ / satataṃ
sarvadā nairantaryeṇa / nityaśa iti yāvajjīvam / tenaitad darśitaṃ
vākyārthajñānamātreṇa kṛtārthatā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] the mere knowledge of the meaning of sentences does not constitute the fulfillment [of the goal].

children.text: satatopāsanayā jñānaṃ paripakvaṃ muktikṣamaṃ sambhavatīti /
children.translated_text: Through constant meditation, knowledge becomes mature and capable of [producing] liberation.

children.text: tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ sukhena labhyo nityayuktasyeti nigamanam // 14 //
children.translated_text: 'For him I am easy to attain' — easily obtainable 'for the ever-disciplined' — this is the conclusion. // 14 //

[Commentary:] 'Of undivided mind' — one whose mind is not elsewhere, that is one of undivided mind. 'Constantly' means always, without interruption. 'Always' means as long as one lives. By this, the following is shown:

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text:
1. uścārayan
2. kālāntaraṃ muktirūpaṃ
3. kasyānyatra
children.translated_text: [Manuscript variant readings.]
[Page 186]

children.text:
tatpadaprāptāv upāya uktaḥ / tatprāptau satyāṃ kaḥ
puruṣārthaviśeṣa
iti ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The means to attaining that state has been stated. What specific human purpose [is gained] upon that attainment? —

children.text:
(mām upetya punar janma duḥkhalayam aśāśvatam /
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ // BhG_8.15 //)
children.translated_text: 'Having attained Me, the great souls who have gone to the supreme perfection do not again obtain birth, which is the abode of suffering and is impermanent.' // BhG 8.15 //

children.text:
mām iti / māṃ prāpya punar janma duḥkhasyālayaṃ sthānaṃ na
prāpnuvanti / sthānāntaraprāptau punarāvṛttiḥ / matprāptir
evānāvṛttihetur iti darśayati // 15 //
children.translated_text: is the cause of non-return. // 15 //

[Commentary:] 'Me' — having attained Me, they do not again obtain birth, which is the abode, the dwelling-place, of suffering. Upon attaining another abode, there is return. [The Lord] shows that the attainment of Me alone

children.text:
(ā brahmabhuvanāl lokāḥ punarāvartino 'rjuna /
mām upetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate // BhG_8.16 //)
children.translated_text: 'From the world of <s>Brahmā</s> downward, all worlds are subject to return, O <s>Arjuna</s>; but having attained Me, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, there is no rebirth.' // BhG 8.16 //

children.text: ābrabmeti / ā brahmabhuvanād / brahmaṇo hiraṇyagarbhasya bhuvanaṃ
nivāso brahmalokas tena saha / abhividhāv ākāro brahmalokasahitāḥ1
children.translated_text: Together with that [world] — the prefix 'ā' has an inclusive sense — [all] beings together with <s>Brahmaloka</s>

children.text: prāṇina ucyante / nanu ca --- yo ha vai2 tat paramaṃ brahma veda
children.translated_text: are referred to. Now, [one might object:] 'He who knows that supreme <s>Brahman</s>

children.text:
brahmaiva bhavati / tasya tāvad eva ciraṃ yāvan na vimokṣye 'tha
sampatsye3 --- ityādhiśrutiprāmāṇyād viduṣaḥ prārabdhakarmakṣaye
śarīrapātānantaraṃ mokṣāvadhāraṇāt kathaṃ brahmavidāṃ
nivṛttakalmaṣāṇāṃ punar āvartanam / tathā yāvad adhikāram
avasthitir
adhikāriṇām4 --- iti śārīrakasūtrād adhikāre
lokānugrahārthe vyāpāre
ye 'vasthitās teṣāṃ prājāpatyādāv adhikāre5 īśvarānuśāsanād
yāvad adhikāram avasthitir bhavati / tatra ca jñānaśeṣam abhyasyatāṃ
prārabdhaphalakarmakṣaye muktiḥ / yo yo devānāṃ pratyabuddhyata
sa sa
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself; so long only is the delay until I shall be liberated; then I shall attain [<s>Brahman</s>]' — from the authority of this and other <s>śrutis</s>, since it is certain that for the knower, upon the exhaustion of <s>prārabdha karma</s> (karma that has begun to bear fruit), liberation [occurs] immediately upon the fall of the body — how can there be return for the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> whose impurities have ceased? Also, from the <s>Śārīraka Sūtra</s>: 'There is continuance [in the cosmic office] as long as the entitlement lasts' — those who are established in the cosmic office for the sake of benefiting the world, for them, in the office of <s>Prajāpati</s> and such, by the Lord's command, there is continuance as long as the entitlement lasts. And there, for those who continue to practice the remainder of knowledge, liberation [comes] upon the exhaustion of <s>prārabdha karma</s>. 'Whoever among the gods became awakened — he
[Commentary:] 'Up to <s>Brahmā</s>'s world' — the world of <s>Brahmā</s> is the abode, the dwelling-place, of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>).

children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

1. ^śabdena tātsthātsthāninastannivāsinaḥ
2. yo heva
3. vimokṣyeta sampatsa iti
4. ^sthitirādhikārikārikāṇām
5. prajāpatyādāvadhikāreśvarānuśāsanād
children.translated_text: [Manuscript variant readings.]
[Page 187]

children.text:
tad abhavat1 --- iti brahmasvarūpāpatteḥ / na ha vai devān pāpaṃ
gacchati --- iti punarjanmapratiṣedhāc ca / etad anupapannam /
atrocyate / prārabdhakarmaphalabhogakṣaye sarveṣāṃ muktir uktā /
tac cārabdhaphalaṃ karma keṣāñcid ekaśarīrabhogyam / anyeṣām
anekaśarīrabhogyam / ekajanmakṛtasyāpi karmaṇo 'nekaśarīrabhogyatāpi
smaryate / yathāvāntaratamanāmnaḥ purāṇarṣeḥ kalidvāparayoḥ
sandhau viṣṇuśāsanād vyāsapadaprāptiḥ / evaṃ muktiphalāniyamas
tattadavasthāprāpter iti2 śārīrake 'pi karmaphalatāratamyavaśena
mukter aniyamadarśanād avirodho 'tra / mām upetya he kaunteya punar janma
śarīragrahaṇaṃ na vidyate // 16 //
children.translated_text: i.e., the taking of a body, does not exist. // 16 //

[Commentary:] became that [<s>Brahman</s>]' — because of the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>'s own nature. 'No evil approaches the gods' — and because of the prohibition of rebirth. This [objection] is not tenable. Here it is replied: liberation has been stated for all upon the exhaustion of the fruit of <s>prārabdha karma</s>. And that <s>prārabdha karma</s> is for some to be experienced in a single body, and for others, in multiple bodies. Even for karma performed in a single birth, the possibility of its being experienced through multiple bodies is recorded — just as the sage <s>Vāmana</s>, of the intermediate <s>tamanāman</s> lineage, attained the position of <s>Vyāsa</s> by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s command at the juncture of <s>Kali</s> and <s>Dvāpara</s> [ages]. Thus, there is no fixed rule for the fruit of liberation — since in the <s>Śārīraka</s> [Sūtras] too, the absence of a fixed rule regarding liberation is seen due to the varying hierarchy of karmic fruits — there is no contradiction here. Having attained Me, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, rebirth,

children.text:
kasya hetor itareṣāṃ lokānām āvṛttiḥ / kālaparicchinnatvāt /
parasya kāraṇaprāptasya pracyutir nāsti kāryalokeṣu hi vartamānasya /
teṣāṃ vināśitvād āvṛttir avaśyaṃ bhāvinī3 tad etad āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For what reason is there return for the other worlds? Because they are bounded by time. For one who has attained the [ultimate] cause, there is no fall; it is for one situated in the effect-worlds — because of their destructibility, return is inevitable. He states this:

children.text:
(sahasrayugaparyantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ /
rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te 'horātravido janāḥ // BhG_8.17 //)
children.translated_text: 'Those who know the day of <s>Brahmā</s>, which lasts for a thousand ages, and the night, which ends after a thousand ages — they are the knowers of day and night.' // BhG 8.17 //

children.text: sahasreti / tathā coktam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'A thousand' — and thus it is said:

children.text:
daivikānāṃ yugānān tu sahasraṃ parisaṅkhyayā /
brāhmam ekam ahar jñeyaṃ tāvatī rātrir eva4 ca // iti /
children.translated_text: 'A thousand divine ages, by exact count, should be known as one day of <s>Brahmā</s>; and the night is of the same extent.'

children.text:
sahasrayugaparyantam ahar brahmaṇo jāgaritāvasthā / caturdaśam
anvantarāvacchinnaḥ kālaḥ / tāvatī rātrir avāntarapralayo
brahmaṇaḥ svapnāvasthā / tad evam ahorātrau saṃvatsarakalpanayā
varṣaśasam āyur
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The day of <s>Brahmā</s> lasting a thousand ages is the state of waking, a period delimited by fourteen <s>manvantaras</s>. The night of the same extent is the intermediate dissolution (<s>avāntarapralaya</s>), <s>Brahmā</s>'s state of sleep. Thus, with day and night [reckoned] by the calculation of the year, the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s> is a hundred years.

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text:
1. sa sa tadābhavat
2. ^tadavasthāvapṛteriti
3. avaśyabhāvinī
4. mahārātrim iti manusmṛtau pāṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: [Manuscript variant readings.]
[Page 188]

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ / tato brahmā mucyate / mahāpralayo bhavati /
pṛthivyādīny api bhūtāni tadā pralīyante // 17 //
children.translated_text: The elements such as earth and the rest are also dissolved then. // 17 //
[Commentary:] After that, <s>Brahmā</s> is liberated. The great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>) occurs.

children.text: tatrāhani rātrau ca yo vyāpāro bhūtānāṃ sa kathyate ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The activity of beings during the day and night is now described:

children.text:
(avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanty aharāgame /
rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasañjñake // BhG_8.18 //)
children.translated_text: 'From the unmanifest, all manifest [beings] come forth at the coming of day; at the coming of night, they dissolve into that very [state] called the unmanifest.' // BhG 8.18 //

children.text:
avyakteti / avyaktam avyākṛtam ucyate pañcānāṃ bhūtānāṃ
sūkṣmāvasthā / karmāvidyāsahitāś ca jīvāḥ / antaryāmīśvaro
'dhiṣṭhātā / tad etad vyākṛtam ucyate / tathā ca śrutiḥ ---
tad dhedaṃ tarhy avyākṛtam āsīt --- iti / vyaktaṃ yac ca2
children.translated_text: 'This indeed was then undifferentiated.' The manifest —

children.text: carācarāṇi bhūtāni mahābhūtāni ca prabhavaty aharāgame /
children.translated_text: i.e., the moveable and immoveable beings and the great elements — come forth at the coming of day.

children.text: rātryāgame tu pralīyante /
children.translated_text: At the coming of night, they dissolve.

children.text: tatra vā vyākṛte 'vāntarapralaye carācarāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ pralayo
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There, in the differentiated [state], in the intermediate dissolution, there is the dissolution of moveable and immoveable beings;

children.text: mahāpralaye tu mahābhūtānām apīti viśeṣaḥ // 18 //
children.translated_text: but in the great dissolution, even of the great elements — this is the distinction. // 18 //

[Commentary:] 'Unmanifest' — the undifferentiated is called the unmanifest: it is the subtle state of the five elements, the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) together with <s>karma</s> and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and the indwelling Lord (<s>antaryāmin</s>) as the presiding controller. That is called the differentiated [state]. And thus <s>śruti</s> states:

children.text:
kṛtakarmavināśo 'kṛtakarmaphalasya cāgama3 iti doṣadvayaṃ
pariharann āha---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Averting the two faults — the destruction of karma already performed and the arrival of the fruit of karma not performed — he says:

children.text:
(bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate /
rātryāgame 'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavaty aharāgame // BhG_8.19 //)
children.translated_text: 'This very same multitude of beings, having come into existence again and again, dissolves at the coming of night, helpless, O <s>Pārtha</s>, and comes forth at the coming of day.' // BhG 8.19 //

children.text:
bhūteti / saṃsārasyānāditvāt pūrvakalpakṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ
stimitaṃ nāmāvasthānaṃ4 na vināśaḥ / tannibandhano 'yaṃ
punaḥ suranaratiryakprabhedena vicitraḥ sarga iti /
sa evāyam iti / samānanāmākṛtitvā(d a)bhedo vyapadiśyate /
tannāmanas tadākṛtayaś ca jāyante / vyaktīnām anyatve 'pi
yathā ta eva śālayo bhujyante (tadvat) / śeṣaṃ gatārtham // 19 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Beings' — since <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless, the <s>karmas</s> performed in previous <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles) have a state called 'quiescence' — not destruction. This variegated creation, in the form of gods, humans, and animals, is dependent on that. 'This very same' — the designation of non-difference is due to sameness of name and form. Those with the same names and forms are born [again]. Even though individuals are different, just as 'those same rice grains are eaten' [is said], so too here. The rest is clear in meaning. // 19 //

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text:
1. tatra vyākṛtamāsīt
2. vyaktayaś ca
3. kṛtakarmavināśokṛtasya ca karmaphalasyāgama iti
4. stimitānāmavasthāna

children.text: yad etad vyaktaṃ varṇitaṃ1 (tasmāt) ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That manifest [state] has been described. Beyond that —

children.text:
(paras tasmāt tu bhāvo 'nyo vyakto 'vyaktāt sanātanaḥ /
yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati // BhG_8.20 //)
children.translated_text: 'But beyond that unmanifest, there is another unmanifest, eternal being, which does not perish when all beings perish.' // BhG 8.20 //

children.text:
para iti / paras tatkāṣṭhā2 / sarvajño 'vyaktaḥ karaṇāgocaratvāt /
tasmād avyaktāt pūrvoktād acetanād ayaṃ cetanaḥ paramātmā
sanātano nityaḥ (paraḥ) / katham / yaḥ sa sarveṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
/
so 'yam īśvaraḥ pratipattavyaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: This Lord is to be understood. // 20 //

[Commentary:] 'Beyond' — beyond, the ultimate limit. Omniscient, unmanifest because of being beyond the reach of the organs [of perception]. This <s>Paramātman</s>, who is conscious, is different from and beyond that previously mentioned unconscious unmanifest — eternal, imperishable. How? He who does not perish when all perish.

children.text:
(avyakto 'kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṃ gatiṃ /
yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama // BhG_8.21 //)
children.translated_text: 'He who is called the Unmanifest, the Imperishable — Him they call the supreme goal; having attained which, they do not return — that is My supreme abode.' // BhG 8.21 //

children.text:
avyakteti / yo 'yam avyaktaḥ paramātmākṣara ity ukto vede ---
tato 'kṣarāt sambhavatīha viśvam --- iti tam āhuḥ śrutayaḥ /
paramāṃ gatiṃ kathaṃ prāpya na nivartante / taddhāma sthānaṃ
paramaṃ
mama // 21 //
children.translated_text: My abode. // 21 //

[Commentary:] 'Unmanifest' — this <s>Paramātman</s>, who is unmanifest and called the Imperishable in the <s>Veda</s> — 'From that Imperishable, this universe is born' — Him the <s>śrutis</s> call the supreme goal. Having attained which, they do not return. That is My supreme abode,

children.text: sa punaḥ kenopāyena labhyata ity āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By what means is He obtained? He says:

children.text:
(puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyas tv ananyayā /
yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṃ tatam // BhG_8.22 //)
children.translated_text: 'That supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is attainable through exclusive devotion — He within whom all beings abide, by whom all this is pervaded.' // BhG 8.22 //

children.text:
puruṣa iti / bhaktyā ananyayā tatparayā
stutinamaskāradhyānadhāraṇādibhis tam eva bhajate / na devatāntaram /
tasya lakṣaṇam ucayate pratipattisaukaryārtham / yasyāntaḥsthāni hi
bhūtāni /
kāraṇe hi kāryam antarbhavati mṛdīva śarā(vam) / ... yogena cedaṃ
sarvaṃ tataṃ vyāptam // 22 //
children.translated_text: is pervaded, filled. // 22 //

[Commentary:] '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — through exclusive devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), devoted entirely to Him — [one who] worships Him through praise, salutation, meditation, concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), and such — not another deity. His characteristic is stated for ease of understanding: He within whom all beings abide — for the effect is contained within the cause, just as a pot [is contained] within clay. And by the power of <s>yoga</s>, all this

children.text:
īśvarasatattvaṃ nirdhāritam3 / tatprāptyupāyaś ca --- prayāṇakāle
manasā --- ity ārabhyoktaḥ / (puruṣaṃ) prāptānāṃ cānāvṛttir
uktā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The truth of the Lord has been ascertained. And the means to attaining Him has been stated from 'at the time of departure, with the mind...' onwards. And the non-return of those who have attained [Him] has been stated.

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES:]

children.text:
1. valitaṃ
2. tatkṛṣṭhā
3. nivāritam

[Page 190]

children.text:
athedānīṃ yena mārgeṇa gatānām anāgamo 'nāvṛtir yena cāvṛttir
iti vibhāgena darśayann āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, by which path those who go do not return, and by which [path] there is return — showing this distinction, he says:

children.text:
(yatra kāle tv anāvṛttim āvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ /
prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha // BhG_8.23 //)
children.translated_text: 'At what time the <s>yogins</s> who have departed attain non-return or return — that time I shall declare, O best of <s>Bharatas</s>.' // BhG 8.23 //

children.text: yatreti / kālagrahaṇaṃ mārgopalakṣaṇārtham / karmayogino
jñānayoginaś
children.translated_text: and the <s>jñānayogin</s> (practitioner of knowledge),

children.text: ca devayānapitṛyānamārgam arcirādilakṣitaṃ prathamaṃ darśayati
children.translated_text: the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) and the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāna</s>), characterized by <s>arcis</s> (flame) and so forth, is first shown

children.text: prādhānyāt // 23 //
children.translated_text: because of its primacy. // 23 //
[Commentary on] 'where' (<s>yatra</s>): the word 'time' (<s>kāla</s>) is for the purpose of indicating the path. For the <s>karmayogin</s> (practitioner of action)

children.text:
(agnir jyotir ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam /
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ // BhG_8.24 //)
children.translated_text: (Fire, light, day, the bright [fortnight], the six months of the northern solstice — departing therein, those who know <s>Brahman</s> go to <s>Brahman</s>.) (BhG 8.24)

children.text:
agnir iti / agnir jyotir ity arcirdevatā lakṣyate /
tathā śuklapakṣadevatottarāyaṇadevatety ātivāhinyo1 devatā iti
sthitaṃ śārīrake / tena tu prayātā gacchanti brahma paramātmānam /
brahmaśabdasya tatra mukhyatattvaṃ na kāryaloko gṛhyate
parabrahmaprakaraṇāc ca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Fire' (<s>agni</s>) — by '<s>agni</s>, <s>jyotis</s>' (fire, light), the deity of <s>arcis</s> (flame) is indicated. Likewise, the deity of the bright fortnight (<s>śuklapakṣa</s>) and the deity of the northern solstice (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>) — these are the conveying deities (<s>ātivāhinyaḥ devatāḥ</s>). This is established in the <s>Śārīraka</s> [<s>Brahmasūtra</s>]. By that [path], those who have departed go to <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>). The word '<s>Brahman</s>' there has its primary meaning — the ultimate reality — not the created world (<s>kāryaloka</s>), because the context concerns the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
tatra yat kaiścid uktam --- arcirādimārgagāmiṇāṃ2
hiraṇyagarbhalokaprāptir iti tad asat / ihānāvṛttir ucyate
brahmaprāpteḥ svatantravṛttiḥ / tathā coktam --- ā brahmabhuvanāl
lokāḥ --- iti // 24 //
children.translated_text: the worlds [are subject to return]' — [BhG 8.16]. // 24 //

Now, what some have said — 'those who travel the path of <s>arcis</s> and so forth attain the world of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>' — that is incorrect. Here, non-return (<s>anāvṛtti</s>) is stated, which operates independently from the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>. And thus it has been said: 'Up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text:
idānīṃ kevalakarmiṇāṃ pitṛyānaḥ na punaḥ punarāvṛttilakṣaṇo
mārgo nirdiśyate prasaṅgāt kathaṃ3 cānabhijñā nāma parābhaveyur
iti darśanārtham ---
children.translated_text: Now, for those who are mere performers of ritual action (<s>kevalakarmin</s>), the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāna</s>), characterized by repeated return, is indicated incidentally — also for the purpose of showing how those who are ignorant would [otherwise] fall into ruin —

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES]

children.text:
1. ātivāhinyo
2. ^gāmināṃ
3. kathaṃ nāma jñānaṃ parā^
children.translated_text: [Variant readings: 1. ātivāhinyaḥ; 2. -gāmināṃ; 3. kathaṃ nāma jñānaṃ parā-]

children.text:
(dhūmo rātris tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam /
tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotir yogī prāpya nivartate // BhG_8.25 //)
children.translated_text: (Smoke, night, the dark [fortnight], the six months of the southern solstice — therein the <s>yogī</s>, having attained the lunar light, returns.) (BhG 8.25)

children.text:
dhūma iti / dhūmo rātris tathā kṛṣṇa ity atrāpi devatā eva
lakṣyante / nātrottarāyaṇaṃ dakṣiṇāyanaṃ rātrirahar veti
vivakṣitam / yatra kvacana mṛtānāṃ samuccayakāriṇām arcirādir
eva / itareṣām api dhūmādir eva / bhīṣmasyottarāyaṇapratīkṣā
tatra maraṇaṃ praśastam iti protsāhanārthā na niyamārthā /
children.translated_text: 'Death therein [during the northern solstice] is auspicious' — that was said for encouragement, not as an invariable rule.

children.text: śeṣaṃ gatārtham // 25 //
children.translated_text: The rest is self-evident. // 25 //

[Commentary:] 'Smoke' (<s>dhūma</s>) — 'smoke, night, the dark [fortnight]' — here too, deities alone are indicated. Here the northern solstice, southern solstice, night, day — these are not what is intended. Wherever those who have died while performing combined [practices] (<s>samuccayakārin</s>) [go], for them [the path is] that of <s>arcis</s> and so forth. For others too, [the path is] that of smoke and so forth. <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s waiting for the northern solstice —

children.text:
(śukrakṛṣṇe gatī hy ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate /
ekayā yāty anāvṛttim anyayāvartate punaḥ // BhG_8.26 //)
children.translated_text: (These two paths, the bright and the dark, are considered eternal for the world. By one, one goes to non-return; by the other, one returns again.) (BhG 8.26)

children.text: śukleti / ete ca gatī śuklakṛṣṇe jagataḥ / śāśvate1 mate
vedoktatvāt --- ekayā yāty anāvṛttim anyayāvartate2 punar iti /
children.translated_text: because they are stated in the <s>Vedas</s>. By one [path] one goes to non-return; by the other one returns again.

children.text: arthasya punar vacanaṃ nigamanam // 26 //
children.translated_text: The repetition of the meaning serves as a concluding summary (<s>nigamana</s>). // 26 //
[Commentary:] 'Bright' (<s>śukla</s>) — these two paths, the bright and the dark, of the world, are considered eternal,

children.text:
mārgadvayābhijñaḥ kevalaṃ karma nārabhate samuccayārtham eva yatate
niḥśreyasārthatvād iti darśayitum āha ---
children.translated_text: One who knows both paths does not undertake mere ritual action alone but strives only for the purpose of combined [knowledge and action], since the goal is the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) — to show this, he says —

children.text:
(naite sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaścana /
tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna // BhG_8.27 //)
children.translated_text: (The <s>yogī</s> who knows these two paths, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is never deluded. Therefore at all times be engaged in <s>yoga</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>.) (BhG 8.27)

children.text: naita iti // 27 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Not these' (<s>naite</s>) — [self-evident]. // 27 //

children.text:
tad etad adhyāyoktaṃ jñānam anyanindayā stūyate /
śraddhālavaḥ katham atrābhiyuktā bhaveyur iti /
children.translated_text: This knowledge taught in the chapter is now praised through the disparagement of other [practices] — 'How would the faithful become devoted to this?' —

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES]

children.text:
1. śāśvatī
2. anyathāvartate
children.translated_text: [Variant readings: 1. śāśvatī; 2. anyathāvartate]

children.text:
(vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam /
atyeti tat sarvam idaṃ viditvā yogī paraṃ sthānam upaiti cādyam // BhG_8.28 //)
children.translated_text: (Whatever meritorious fruit is declared for the <s>Vedas</s>, for sacrifices, for austerities, and for gifts — the <s>yogī</s>, having known all this, transcends it and attains the supreme, primal abode.) (BhG 8.28)

children.text:
vedeṣv iti / vedeṣu caturṣv api yat puṇyaphalaṃ yajñeṣv
agniṣṭomādiṣu tapaḥsu cāndrāyaṇādiṣu gobhūmihiraṇyadāneṣu
tat sarvam idam atyeti /
katham / idaṃ jñānaṃ viditvā yogī paraṃ sthānam upaiti cādyam /
sarvasthānānām ādyaṃ pārameśvaraṃ padam iti // 28 //
children.translated_text: The primal [abode] of all abodes is the station of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). // 28 //

[Commentary:] 'In the <s>Vedas</s>' — whatever meritorious fruit [is obtained] in the four <s>Vedas</s>, in sacrifices such as the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and so forth, in austerities such as the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> and so forth, in gifts of cows, land, gold — all that, this [knowledge] transcends. How? Having known this knowledge, the <s>yogī</s> attains the supreme, primal abode.

children.text: (iti) bhagavadbhāskarakṛte gītābhāṣye aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eighth chapter of the <s>Gītābhāṣya</s> composed by the Blessed <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: atha navamo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now the ninth chapter.

children.text: devayānena gatānām apunarāvṛttir uktā --- mām upetya punarjanma na
vidyate --- iti / yat1 prāpyāpunarāvṛttis tasya brahmaṇo
children.translated_text: [BhG 8.16]. That <s>Brahman</s>, upon reaching which there is no return —

children.text:
viśiṣṭaśaktiyuktasya satattvaṃ punar api kathayiṣyann āha /
atyantātīndriyatvāt punaḥ punaḥ kathitam api na cetasi
sthitipadaṃ labhate keṣāñcid eva
puṇyakṛtāṃ cetasi sthirībhavatīti bhagavān yatate /
children.translated_text: its true nature, endowed with distinctive power (<s>viśiṣṭaśakti</s>), he will again describe. Because of its being utterly beyond the senses, even when spoken of again and again, it does not find a stable place in the minds of some. Only in the minds of those who have performed meritorious deeds does it become established — thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> makes effort.
Non-return for those who have gone by the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) has been stated — 'Having attained Me, there is no rebirth'

children.text: bhagavān uvāca ---
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said —

children.text:
(idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave /
jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt // BhG_9.1 //)
children.translated_text: (To you who are free from envy, I shall declare this most secret knowledge together with realization, knowing which you shall be freed from evil.) (BhG 9.1)

children.text:
idaṃ tv iti / idaṃ tu te guhyatamam / tuśabdo 'tiśayārthaḥ /
anasūyave paraguṇeṣu doṣāviṣkaraṇam asūyā / tadrahitāya /
jñānaṃ (pra)vakṣyāmi / vijñānasahitam / yaj jñānaṃ jñātvā
mokṣyase 'śubhāt saṃsārabandhāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This' (<s>idam</s>) — 'This most secret [knowledge] to you' — the word 'tu' is for emphasis. 'To one free from envy' — <s>asūyā</s> (envy) is the disclosure of faults in the virtues of others. To one free from that. 'I shall declare knowledge' — together with realization (<s>vijñāna</s>). 'Knowing which knowledge, you shall be freed from evil' — from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth).

children.text:
keṣāñcid eva puṇyakṛtām arcirādinā2 vartmanā kramamuktir uktā /
idānīṃ sadyomuktir ucyata ity āhuḥ / tad asat / arcirādinaiva
saṃsāramaṇḍalam atikramya liṅgaśarīraviyogān muktir nātraiva
śarīre (mucya)te / tasmād ihaiva muktir ity apasiddhāntaḥ3 // 1 //
children.translated_text: Some say: 'For some who have performed meritorious deeds, gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>) through the path of <s>arcis</s> and so forth has been stated. Now immediate liberation (<s>sadyomukti</s>) is being stated.' That is incorrect. Only through the path of <s>arcis</s> and so forth, having crossed over the sphere of <s>saṃsāra</s>, liberation occurs through separation from the subtle body (<s>liṅgaśarīra</s>) — one is not liberated in this very body. Therefore, 'liberation here in this [body]' is a heterodox doctrine (<s>apasiddhānta</s>). // 1 //

children.text: taj jñānaṃ stūyate śraddhājananārtham ---
children.translated_text: That knowledge is praised for the purpose of generating faith —

children.text:
(rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitram idam uttamam /
pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartum avyayam // BhG_9.2 //)
children.translated_text: (This is the king of sciences, the king of secrets, the supreme purifier, directly realizable, righteous, easy to practice, and imperishable.) (BhG 9.2)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES]

children.text:
1. yaṃ
2. ^kṛtāṃ mandirādinā
3. keṣāñcideva ... apasiddhāntaḥ iti aṃśoyaṃ guhyatamam
ityetadanantaraṃ vidyate mūlakoṣe
children.translated_text: [Variant readings: 1. yaṃ; 2. -kṛtāṃ mandirādinā; 3. keṣāñcideva ... apasiddhāntaḥ passage location note]

children.text:
rājeti / rājñām aśvapatijanakādīnām / teṣāṃ ca gopyaṃ pavitraṃ
pāvanaṃ pratyakṣaṃ spaṣṭo 'vagamo yasya tad idaṃ pratyakṣāvagamam /
naitatparokṣam ity arthaḥ / yathā mahāmerujñānam /
dharmād anapetaṃ dharmyam / kartuṃ susukhaṃ sukaram ity arthaḥ /
akṣayaphalahetutvād avyayam // 2 //
children.translated_text: Imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>) — because it is the cause of inexhaustible fruit. // 2 //

[Commentary:] 'King' (<s>rāja</s>) — of kings such as <s>Aśvapati</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, and others. Their secret; the purifier, the purifying one; that of which the realization (<s>avagama</s>) is direct (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) — that is 'directly realizable' (<s>pratyakṣāvagama</s>). This is not remote (<s>parokṣa</s>) — that is the meaning. Like the knowledge of the great <s>Meru</s> [mountain]. Not deviating from <s>dharma</s> — hence 'righteous' (<s>dharmya</s>). Easy to practice (<s>susukha</s>) means easy to perform — that is the meaning.

children.text: ye punaḥ ---
children.translated_text: But those who —

children.text:
(aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa /
aprāpya māṃ nirvartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani // BhG_9.3 //)
children.translated_text: (People who have no faith in this <s>dharma</s>, O Scorcher of Foes, not attaining Me, return on the path of death and <s>saṃsāra</s>.) (BhG 9.3)

children.text:
aśraddadheti / aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya vakṣyamāṇasya
jñānarūpasya te mām aprāpya nivartante mṛtyugraste
saṃsāravartmani // 3 //
children.translated_text: of <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is seized by death. // 3 //
[Commentary:] 'Without faith' — people who have no faith in this <s>dharma</s> that is to be stated, which has the form of knowledge — they, not attaining Me, return on the path

children.text: idānīṃ tatjñānaṃ kathayati ---
children.translated_text: Now he states that knowledge —

children.text:
(mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyaktamūrtinā /
matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ // BhG_9.4 //)
children.translated_text: (By Me, in My unmanifest form, this entire world is pervaded. All beings abide in Me, but I do not abide in them.) (BhG 9.4)

children.text: mayeti / mayā tatam idaṃ sarvam avyaktamūrtinātīndriyeṇa1
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'By Me' — by Me, this entire [world] is pervaded, in an unmanifest form — beyond the senses,

children.text:
sūkṣmeṇātmanā / mayi tiṣṭhantīti matsthāni / na cāhaṃ teṣv
avasthitaḥ / svamahimni sthitatvāt // 4 //
children.translated_text: by [My] subtle Self. 'Abide in Me' — therefore [they are called] 'abiding in Me' (<s>matstha</s>). 'But I do not abide in them' — because I am established in My own greatness. // 4 //

children.text: (mama yogam aiśvaraṃ paśya2) ---
children.translated_text: ('Behold My lordly <s>yoga</s>') —

children.text:
(na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram /
bhūtabhṛn na ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ // BhG_9.5 //)
children.translated_text: (Nor do beings abide in Me — behold My lordly <s>yoga</s>! My Self, the sustainer of beings, does not abide in beings but brings beings into existence.) (BhG 9.5)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES]

children.text:
1. ^mūrtinā atendriyeṇa
2. caturthaślokavyākhyānānantaram 4 // kuṇḍa iti tāni akṣarāṇi tatpatrānte yoga iti /
avyahitaparapatrārambhe prathamapaṅktau
si tvat na ceti iti dvitīyapaṅktau vartante
children.translated_text: [Variant readings and manuscript notes]

children.text:
na ceti / bhūtāni bibhartīti bhūtabhṛt / na ca bhūteṣu /
yathā śarīrī jīvaḥ / śarīrākārapariṇatāni bhūtāni bibharti
teṣu cāvasthito na caivam aham / bhūtāni bhāvayatīti
bhūtabhāvanaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>bhūtabhāvanaḥ</s>. // 5 //

[Commentary:] 'Nor' — the sustainer of beings (<s>bhūtabhṛt</s>) — He who bears beings. Not in beings — not like an embodied <s>jīva</s> (individual soul). [The <s>jīva</s>] bears beings that have transformed into the form of a body and abides in them — but I am not thus. The one who brings beings into being (<s>bhūtabhāvana</s>) —

children.text: (matsthāni na ca matsthāni iti viruddhaṃ paśyaṃ dṛṣṭāntam āha ---
children.translated_text: ('Abiding in Me' and 'not abiding in Me' — seeing this contradiction, he gives an illustration —)

children.text:
(yathākāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān /
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānīty upadhāraya // BhG_9.6 //)
children.translated_text: (Just as the mighty wind, moving everywhere, eternally abides in space, so know that all beings abide in Me.) (BhG 9.6)

children.text:
yatheti / yathākāśe vyāpaketi sūkṣmo vāyuḥ sthitaḥ sarvatrago
lokatrayavyāpī tathā bhūtāni matsthānīty upadhāraya /
na saṃśleṣasambandhena / kiṃ tarhi / vyāpake mayi viṣayabhūte
'lpaparimāṇāni (bhūtāni) parivartanta iti sthityavasthā darśitā // 6
children.translated_text: beings of small measure revolve — thus the condition of abiding is shown. // 6

[Commentary:] 'Just as' — just as the subtle, all-pervading wind abides in space, moving everywhere, pervading the three worlds — so know that beings abide in Me. Not through a relationship of contact. Rather, in Me who am all-pervading and who serve as the domain,

children.text: adhunā pralayāvasthocyate ---
children.translated_text: Now the condition of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) is stated —

children.text:
(sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām /
kalpakṣaye punas tāni kalpādau visṛjāmy aham // BhG_9.7 //)
children.translated_text: (All beings, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, enter into My <s>Prakṛti</s> at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>. At the beginning of a <s>kalpa</s>, I send them forth again.) (BhG 9.7)

children.text:
sarveti / sarvabhūtāni kaunteya madīyāṃ prakṛtiṃ yānti /
kadā kalpakṣaye / kalpādau ca punas tāni visṛjāmi // 7 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'All' — all beings, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, enter into My <s>Prakṛti</s>. When? At the end of a <s>kalpa</s>. And at the beginning of a <s>kalpa</s>, I send them forth again. // 7 //

children.text: katham ---
children.translated_text: How? —

children.text: (prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: (Resting upon My own <s>Prakṛti</s>, I send forth again and again

children.text: bhūtagrāmam imaṃ kṛtsnam avaśaṃ prakṛter vaśāt // BhG_9.8 //
children.translated_text: this entire multitude of beings, powerless, by the force of <s>Prakṛti</s>.) (BhG 9.8)

children.text:
prakṛtim iti1 / prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhyāvalambya bhūtagrāmaṃ
(bhūta)samūhaṃ visṛjāmi / avaśaṃ paratantraṃ prakṛter vaśāt /
yathākarma prāṇināṃ prakṛtiḥ pariṇamate atas tadvaśāt sṛjāmi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Prakṛti</s>' — resting upon, i.e., supporting My own <s>Prakṛti</s>, I send forth the multitude of beings — the aggregate of beings. Powerless — dependent — by the force of <s>Prakṛti</s>. <s>Prakṛti</s> transforms according to the <s>karma</s> of living beings, and therefore by its force I create.

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES]

children.text: 1. prakṛtāmiti
children.translated_text: [Variant readings: 1. prakṛtāmiti]

children.text:
kā punar iyaṃ prakṛtiḥ / pañcānāṃ bhūtānāṃ sūkṣmāvasthā
vīryabhūtā / atreyaṃ vedāntaprakriyā --- paraṃ brahma
niścalam ākāśakalpaṃ prathamam avasthitam / tata(s tasya) roṣād
vikṛtaḥ sṛṣṭīcchāviśiṣṭo 'ntaryāmīśvaraśabdavācyo bhavati /
tato bhūtasūkṣmam avyākṛtam ākāśam utpadyate / tataḥ
sūkṣmātmāyaṃ
hiraṇyagarbha ity ācakṣate /
tataḥ sthūlāni viyadādīni mahābhūtāni krameṇotpadyante /
tato 'ṇḍaṃ tato virāṭ prajāpatiḥ /
tasmin vairāje sthūlaśarīre sarve lokāḥ sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi ca
children.translated_text: In that cosmic body of <s>Virāṭ</s>, all worlds, all gods, and all

children.text: sthāvarajaṅgamāni bhūtānīti vastubhūte 'yaṃ prakṛtir na
children.translated_text: beings — both stationary and moving — [exist]. Thus, being a real entity, this <s>Prakṛti</s> is not

children.text: māyāmātram avastubhūtam // 8 //
children.translated_text: merely <s>māyā</s> (illusion), not something unreal. // 8 //

What then is this <s>Prakṛti</s>? It is the subtle state of the five elements, which is their potent form (<s>vīryabhūtā</s>). Here is the <s>Vedānta</s> method: First, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, motionless, resembling space, exists primordially. Then, from its will, a modified [form] — distinguished by the desire to create, called the Inner Controller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>), designated by the word '<s>Īśvara</s>' — comes into being. Then, from that, the subtle element (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>), the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), space (<s>ākāśa</s>), arises. Then, this subtle self — they call <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. Then the gross great elements — space and so forth — arise in sequence. Then the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>), then <s>Virāṭ</s>, [then] <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text:
na cāvidyā nāma kācid anātmany ātmabuddhiḥ / jīvasya pratipuruṣaṃ
parabrahmasvarūpaṃ tadagrahaṃ ca muktvā kadācid āśaṅkyeta1 ---
viṣamāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ kurvato doṣā(ya tat) syād ity āha2 ---
children.translated_text: Nor is there anything called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is [merely] the cognition of self in what is not-self. Setting aside the question of the individual soul's (<s>jīva</s>'s) identity with the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in each person and its non-apprehension — lest it be suspected that 'there would be a fault in creating an unequal creation' — he says —

children.text:
(na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya /
udāsīnavad āsīnam asaktaṃ teṣu karmasu // BhG_9.9 //)
children.translated_text: (These actions do not bind Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>, seated as one indifferent, unattached to those actions.) (BhG 9.9)

children.text:
na ceti / na ca māṃ nibadhnanti karmāṇi / kasmāt /
udāsīnavad āsīnatvāt / teṣu karmasu asaktatvāt / anyo 'pi yaḥ
phalāsaktas tam api karmāṇi na nibadhnanti nyāyatulyatvāt // 9 //
children.translated_text: him too actions do not bind, because the principle is the same. // 9 //
[Commentary:] 'Not' — actions do not bind Me. Why? Because I am seated as one indifferent. Because I am unattached to those actions. And anyone else who is unattached to the fruit —

children.text:
nanu ca prakṛtir nityā svatantrā bhūtasṛṣṭau pravartata iti
sāṅkhyā vadanti / tad asat / tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> say: '<s>Prakṛti</s> is eternal and independently operates in the creation of beings.' That is incorrect. To this he says —

children.text:
(mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram /
hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate // BhG_9.10 //)
children.translated_text: (Under My supervision, <s>Prakṛti</s> brings forth the world of moving and non-moving [beings]. By this cause, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, the world revolves.) (BhG 9.10)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES]

children.text:
1. na cāvidyā nāma kācit pratipuruṣamnātmabuddhiryattujjīvasya paraṃ
brahmasvarūpaṃ tadagrahaṃ ca muktvā kadācidāśaṅkyeta
2. syādityāha
children.translated_text: [Variant readings for the preceding passage]

children.text:
mayeti / mayādhyakṣeṇa matta utpannā satī
mayādhyakṣeṇādhiṣṭhātrā
pravartitā sūyate janayati / na hy acetanā prakṛtis triguṇātmikā
sāṅkhyaparikalpitā satī pravartitum arhati prāṇināṃ
vicitrakarmavipākāparijñānāt / kathaṃ suranaratiryakprabhedabhinnaṃ
bhuvanaṃ nirmīyate rathādīnām acetanānāṃ svataḥ pravṛttyadarśanāc
ca
cetanādhiṣṭhitāḥ pravartanta iti yuktam / ato matpravartitā prakṛtiḥ
/
(anena) prasavahetunā1 jagad (vi)parivartate // 10 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'By Me' — under My supervision — having arisen from Me, being directed by Me as supervisor, [<s>Prakṛti</s>] brings forth, i.e., produces. For the unconscious <s>Prakṛti</s>, consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s> as conceived by the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, is not capable of operating [on its own], because it does not comprehend the diverse ripening of <s>karma</s> of living beings. How could a world differentiated into divisions of gods, humans, and animals be produced? And since we see that unconscious things like chariots and the like do not operate on their own, it is proper that they operate when directed by a conscious [agent]. Therefore, <s>Prakṛti</s> is directed by Me. By this cause of production, the world revolves. // 10 //

children.text: prakṛter adhyakṣam api santam ---
children.translated_text: Though being the supervisor of <s>Prakṛti</s> —

children.text:
(avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanum āśritam /
paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram // BhG_9.11 //)
children.translated_text: (The deluded disregard Me, dwelling in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the Great Lord of beings.) (BhG 9.11)

children.text: aveti / avajānanti māṃ mūḍhāḥ prādurbhāveṣu mānuṣīṃ
tanum āśritaṃ vāsudevo nāma kṣatriyo manuṣyo 'yam ity anādaraṃ
children.translated_text: bodies [saying]: '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is just a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a mere human being'—thus they show disregard,

children.text: kurvanti
paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto bhūtamaheśvaraṃ mama // 11 //
children.translated_text: not knowing My supreme nature as the great Lord of beings. (11)
[Commentary:] 'Despise'—the foolish despise Me, when I appear in [what seem to be] human

children.text: te ca ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And they—

children.text:
(moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ /
āsurīṃ rākṣasīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ // BhG_9.12 //)
children.translated_text: (Of vain hopes, of vain actions, of vain knowledge, senseless— they have resorted to the deluding nature of <s>asuras</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>.) (BhG 9.12)

children.text: mogheti / moghāśā moghakarmāṇo vṛthāsaṅkalpāḥ / karmāṇi ca
teṣām
agnihotrādīni vṛtaiva jñānaṃ cānātmaviṣayatvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>agnihotra</s> and the like—are in vain. Their knowledge too [is in vain] because it does not pertain to the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: vicetaso 'vivekinaḥ rākṣasīṃ tāmasīṃ prakṛtim āsthitāḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Senseless'—without discrimination—they have resorted to a <s>rākṣasī</s> (demonic), i.e. <s>tāmasī</s> (darkness-characterized), nature. (12)
[Commentary:] 'Of vain'—of vain hopes, of vain actions—their aspirations are futile. And their actions—

children.text: ye tu ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But those who—

children.text:
(mahātmānas tu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtim āsthitāḥ /
bhajante 'nanyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam // BhG_9.13 //)
children.translated_text: (Great souls, O <s>Pārtha</s>, having resorted to the divine nature, worship Me with undivided minds, knowing [Me as] the imperishable origin of beings.) (BhG 9.13)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: 1. prasave hetunā
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
maheti / mahātmānas tu lokottaraprajñā daivīṃ prakṛtiṃ
sattvaguṇasambhūtā cittavṛttim āśritā bhajante sevante bhūtānām
ādiṃ1 māṃ jñātvā // 13 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Great'—great souls, of wisdom beyond the ordinary, having resorted to the divine nature—the mental disposition born of the <s>sattva</s> quality—they worship, they serve [Me], having known Me as the imperishable origin of beings. (13)

children.text: kena prakāreṇa bhajante ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In what manner do they worship?

children.text:
(satataṃ kīrtayantaś ca yatantaś ca dṛḍhavratāḥ /
namasyantaś ca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate // BhG_9.14 //)
children.translated_text: (Always glorifying [Me], striving with firm vows, bowing to Me with devotion, ever united [with Me], they worship [Me].) (BhG 9.14)

children.text: satatatam iti / satataṃ matsvarūpakathane pravṛttacetaso yatantaś ca
matprāptyupāyeṣu yatnavanto dṛḍhavratāḥ dṛḍhaṃ2 sthiraṃ
children.translated_text: making effort in the means of attaining Me, of firm vows—firm, stable

children.text: vrataṃ niyamaḥ karmety a(na)rthāntaraṃ tad yeṣāṃ te dṛḍhavratāḥ /
children.translated_text: vow, meaning discipline, meaning action—that which they maintain is different [from mere talk]; those who have that are 'of firm vows.'

children.text: bhaktyā cādareṇa māṃ namasyantaḥ pādapatanādinā vyāpāreṇa
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] With devotion, meaning with respect, bowing to Me through activities such as falling at [My] feet and the like,

children.text: nityayuktāḥ santa upāsate // 14 //
children.translated_text: ever united, they worship [Me]. (14)
[Commentary:] 'Always'—with minds engaged in the telling of My true nature, striving—

children.text: anye tu paripakvajñānāḥ ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Others, however, whose knowledge has matured—

children.text:
(jñānayajñena cāpy anye yajante mām upāsate /
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham // BhG_9.15 //)
children.translated_text: (And others too, worshipping Me with the sacrifice of knowledge, worship [Me]—as one, as different, as manifold, as facing everywhere.) (BhG 9.15)

children.text:
jñāneti / jñānam eva yajño jñānayajñaḥ / yajantaḥ pūjayanto
mām upāsate / sātatyena parameśvare cittadhāraṇam upāsanam /
te caikatvenātmānam idaṃ sarvaṃ vāsudevaḥ sarvam ity anayā (buddhyā)
samastabhedaprapañcaṃ3 paramakāraṇaparamātmani4 cetaḥ pravilāpya
tadātmanāvatiṣṭhante / te caite brahmavidaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ /
anye punar evam asaktāḥ pṛthaktvenopāsate / bahudhā bahubhiḥ
prakārair
āditye candramasy agnau paramātmānaṃ cintayanti / viśvatomukhaṃ sarvato
mukhāni
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Knowledge'—knowledge itself is the sacrifice; that is the sacrifice of knowledge. Worshipping, honoring Me, they worship. Worship is the continuous holding of the mind on <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord). And they [worship] as one—[thinking] 'all this is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, everything'—with this understanding, having dissolved all the manifold diversity into the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), the supreme cause, they abide as one with That. These are the foremost among the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. Others, however, being unable to do so, worship as different [from the Lord]. As manifold—in many ways—they contemplate the <s>Paramātman</s> in <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), in the moon, in fire. Facing everywhere—whose faces,

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. bhūtānāmādi
2. sthira
3. sarvamitya^ ityetadanantaraṃ samasta^
ityetasmātpūrvaṃ kānicinākṣarāṇyaspaṣṭāni
4. paramakaraṇa
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: dvārāṇi (yasya) taṃ1 viśvatomukham / yad evālambanatvenopādīyate
vakṣyamāṇaṃ tad eva tatprāptyupāyatāṃ pratipadyate // 15 //
children.translated_text: that very thing that is about to be described becomes a means for attaining Him. (15)
i.e. doorways, are everywhere—Him who faces everywhere. Whatever is taken as a support [for meditation],

children.text: tad idānīṃ prapañcayati ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now He elaborates on that—

children.text:
(ahaṃ kratur ahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣadham /
mantro 'ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṃ hutam // BhG_9.16 //)
children.translated_text: (I am the <s>kratu</s> (Vedic ritual), I am the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), I am the <s>svadhā</s> (offering to ancestors), I am the <s>auṣadha</s> (plant/herb), I am the <s>mantra</s>, I alone am the clarified butter, I am the fire, I am the oblation.) (BhG 9.16)

children.text:
ahaṃ kratur iti / ahaṃ kratuḥ paśusomeṣṭilakṣaṇo yajñaḥ smārtaḥ
pañcamahāyajñādiḥ2 / svadhā yat tu pitṝn uddiśya kriyate /
aham auṣadhaṃ vrīhyādīnām / idaṃ kim / tad annam /
mantro yājyāpuro'nuvākādiḥ3 / aham evājyaṃ homasādhanam / aham agnir
āhavanīyo yatra hūyate / hutaṃ ca havanakriyāham eva // 16 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'I am the <s>kratu</s>'—I am the <s>kratu</s>—the ritual characterized by animal and <s>soma</s> sacrifices. The <s>yajña</s> is the <s>smārta</s> (traditional) [rite]—the five great sacrifices (<s>pañcamahāyajña</s>) and the like. <s>Svadhā</s>—that which is offered to the ancestors. I am the <s>auṣadha</s>—rice and other [grains]. What is this? That is food. The <s>mantra</s>—the sacrificial formulae (<s>yājyā</s>), invocations (<s>puro'nuvākya</s>), and the like. I alone am the <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter)—the means of oblation. I am the fire—the <s>āhavanīya</s> [fire] in which oblations are offered. And the <s>huta</s> (oblation)—the act of offering—is also I alone. (16)

children.text:
(pitāham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ /
vedyaṃ pavitram oṅkāra ṛk sāma yajur eva ca // BhG_9.17 //)
children.translated_text: (I am the father of this world, the mother, the sustainer, the grandfather. I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, and the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Yajur</s> [<s>Vedas</s>].) (BhG 9.17)

children.text:
piteti / pitotpādayitā pālayitā vā / mātā dhātrī dhātā vidhātā
/
karmaphalānām / pitāmahaḥ pituḥ pitā cāham eva /
yad vedyaṃ jñeyaṃ vastu tad aham / yac ca pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ
prāyaścittādi / oṅkāraḥ praṇavaḥ / vedatrayaṃ cāham eva // 17 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Father'—the father is the begetter or the protector. The mother is the nurse. The sustainer (<s>dhātā</s>) is the ordainer—of the fruits of <s>karma</s>. The grandfather—the father's father—that too is I alone. Whatever is to be known (<s>vedya</s>)—the object worthy of knowledge—that am I. And the purifier—the means of purification such as <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) and the like. <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the <s>praṇava</s>. And the three <s>Vedas</s> too are I alone. (17)

children.text:
(gatir bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt /
prabhavaḥ pralayasthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījam avyayam // BhG_9.18 //)
children.translated_text: (The goal, the sustainer, the lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the friend, the origin, the dissolution, the ground, the treasure, and the imperishable seed.) (BhG 9.18)

children.text:
gatir iti / gamyata iti gatir gantavyo 'ham / bhartā poṣṭā /
prabhuḥ svāmī / draṣṭā pratyakṣaparokṣakṛtānāṃ karmaṇām /
nivāsaḥ prāṇinām / nivasanty asminn iti nivāsaḥ / śaraṇam ārtānām
/
suhṛd upakārī pratyupakārānapekṣayā / prabhavo jagataḥ pralayaḥ
sthānaṃ
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Goal'—that which is to be reached is the goal (<s>gati</s>)—I am the one to be reached. The sustainer (<s>bhartā</s>) is the nourisher. The lord (<s>prabhu</s>) is the master. The witness (<s>sākṣin</s>)—the seer of actions done in public and in secret. The abode (<s>nivāsa</s>)—of living beings; they dwell in this, hence the abode. The refuge (<s>śaraṇa</s>)—of the afflicted. The friend (<s>suhṛd</s>)—one who does good without expectation of reciprocation. The origin of the world; the dissolution; the ground—

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. taṃ taṃ
2. yajñādi
3. puronuvākyādiḥ
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
sthitihetuḥ / nidhīyate 'smiñ chreya iti nidhānam /
bījam utpattikāraṇam /
avyayaṃ vyayarahitam / vrīhyādibījaṃ vyayi // 18 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] meaning the cause of sustenance. The treasure (<s>nidhāna</s>)—that in which the highest good is deposited. The seed—the cause of origination. Imperishable—free from decay. For the seed of rice and the like is perishable. (18)

children.text: kiṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover—

children.text:
(tapāmy ahaṃ ahaṃ varṣa nigṛhṇāmy utsṛjāmi ca /
amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuś ca sad asac cāham arjuna // BhG_9.19 //)
children.translated_text: (I give heat; I release and withhold rain. I am immortality and death; I am being and non-being, O <s>Arjuna</s>.) (BhG 9.19)

children.text:
tapāmīti / ādityātmanā sthitvā nidāghasamaye tapāmi
kaiścid raśmibhiḥ / prāvṛṭkāle varṣam utsṛjāmi / kaiścit
kiraṇair nigṛhṇāmy anyartāv aham evāmṛtaṃ jīvanam /
mṛtyuś ca vināśaḥ sad asac cāham arjuna / sad iti sthūlaṃ
vyavahārayogyaṃ vastu vyapadiśyate / asad iti sūkṣmam avyaktam
a(vyavahārya)m / evaṃ madvyati(riktaṃ kim api nāsti) /
santaḥ1 samyagdarśina ekatvenākāmā (viśva)tomukham
avasthitaṃ2 (mā)m (upāsate /
apare akāmāḥ) ... kratvādyekaikapratipattyā bahudhā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Others, without desire, through the apprehension of each individual [form] such as <s>kratu</s> and the rest, in various ways,

children.text: pṛthaktvenopāsata
children.translated_text: worship as different—

children.text: iti saṅkṣepārthaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: this is the summary meaning. (19)

[Commentary:] 'I give heat'—abiding in the form of the sun, in the hot season I give heat with certain rays. In the rainy season, I release rain; with other rays I withhold [rain] in other seasons. I alone am immortality—life—and death—destruction. I am being (<s>sat</s>) and non-being (<s>asat</s>), O <s>Arjuna</s>. '<s>Sat</s>' refers to the gross entity fit for conventional usage. '<s>Asat</s>' refers to the subtle, unmanifest, [which is] beyond conventional usage. Thus, there is nothing whatsoever apart from Me. The wise (<s>santaḥ</s>), those of right vision, without desire, contemplate Me who abides facing everywhere, as one.

children.text:
ye punar jñānayajñenopāsate pṛthaktvenaikatvena (vā) kevalakarmiṇaḥ
phalalubdhāḥ ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But those who worship through the sacrifice of knowledge, whether as different or as one—the mere performers of ritual actions, greedy for fruits—

children.text:
(traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā yajñair iṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante /
te puṇyam āsādya surendralokam aśnanti divyān divi devabhogān // BhG_9.20 //)
children.translated_text: (Those who know the three <s>Vedas</s>, who drink the <s>soma</s>, purified of sin, who worship Me through sacrifices and pray for the way to heaven—they, having reached the holy world of the lord of the gods, enjoy divine pleasures in heaven.) (BhG 9.20)

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. kacyantaḥ
2. `avasthitaṃ' etadantaram ekam akṣaram aspaṣṭam / tad anantaraṃ
maparaṃ iti vartate / tataḥ param ekam akṣaram aspaṣṭhaṃ mūlakoṣe
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
traividyeti / tisro vidyā yeṣāṃ te traividyāḥ / svārthe taddhitaḥ /
vedatrayavihitakarmāṇa ity arthaḥ / somapās tata eva pūtapāpāḥ
saṃśodhitakalmaṣā yajñair iṣṭvā mām evendrādirūpeṇāvasthitaṃ
vastuto na punas te jānanti svargatiṃ svargagamanam / te puṇyaṃ
puṇyakarmasādhyaṃ śatakratoḥ sthānaṃ bhuñjanti divyān anubhavanti
bhogān // 20 //
children.translated_text: divine pleasures. (20)

[Commentary:] 'Those of the three <s>Vedas</s>'—those whose [qualification is] the three <s>Vedas</s>; the <s>taddhita</s> suffix is used in the reflexive sense; the meaning is: those whose actions are prescribed by the three <s>Vedas</s>. Soma-drinkers; thereby purified of sin—their impurities are cleansed. Having worshipped Me—who abide in the form of <s>Indra</s> and other [deities]—by means of sacrifices, they pray for the way to heaven, the going to heaven. But in reality they do not know [Me]. They, having attained the holy abode of <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>)—attainable through meritorious <s>karma</s>—enjoy and experience

children.text: te ca ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And they—

children.text:
(te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti /
evaṃ trayīdharmam anuprapannā gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante // BhG_9.21 //)
children.translated_text: (Having enjoyed the vast world of heaven, when their merit is exhausted, they enter the mortal world. Thus, those who follow the <s>dharma</s> of the three [<s>Vedas</s>], desiring objects of desire, obtain going and coming.) (BhG 9.21)

children.text: te tam iti /2 bhukteṣu bhogeṣu punaḥ kṣīṇapuṇyāḥ puṇyakṣaye
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'They that'—when their enjoyments have been enjoyed, again, their merit being exhausted, upon the exhaustion of merit,

children.text: martyalokaṃ praviśanti / evam ity uktaparāmarśaḥ / hiśabdo hetau /
trayīdharmaṃ3 vedatrayavihitaṃ karma prapannā jāyante mriyante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Those who have followed the <s>dharma</s> prescribed by the three <s>Vedas</s>—those actions—are born and die.

children.text: kāmān bhogān kāmayamānāḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: Desiring pleasurable objects of desire. (21)
they enter the mortal world. 'Thus' refers back to what was said. The word '<s>hi</s>' indicates reason.

children.text: ye tu ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But those who—

children.text:
(ananyāṃś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate /
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmy aham // BhG_9.22 //)
children.translated_text: (Those people who, thinking of no other, worship Me—for those who are ever united [with Me], I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.) (BhG 9.22)

children.text:
ananyāṃś cintayanto mām iti / na vidyate 'nya upāsyo yeṣāṃ te
ananyāḥ / teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānām aham eva yogakṣemaṃ vahāmi /
aprāptaprāptir yogaḥ / kṣemaḥ prāptasya parirakṣaṇam /
tad ubhayam // 22 //
children.translated_text: That is both [aspects]. (22)

[Commentary:] 'Thinking of no other and [thinking of] Me'—those for whom there is no other object of worship—they are '<s>ananya</s>' (without another). For those who are ever united [with Me], I Myself carry their <s>yogakṣema</s> (acquisition and preservation). <s>Yoga</s> is the attainment of what has not been attained; <s>kṣema</s> is the preservation of what has been attained.

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. gamanam
2. bhukteṣv iti mukteṣu bhogeṣu vaḥ kṣīṇapuṇyāḥ karmasādhyaṃ
śatakratoḥ puṇyakṣaye / atra rma ityārabhya etadantaḥ pāṭhaḥ
kaṇḍhita iti pratibhāti
3. traidharnya
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: kiṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover—

children.text:
(ye 'py anyadevatābhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ /
te 'py mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhipūrvakam // BhG_9.23 //)
children.translated_text: (Even those who are devotees of other deities, who worship with faith—they too worship Me alone, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, though not in the proper manner.) (BhG 9.23)

children.text:
ye 'pīti / ye 'py anyadevatābhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ /
yajante pūjayanti ca / te 'pi mām eva vastuto yajanti / kiṃ tv
avidhipūrvakam / muktimārgavidhirahitam ity arthaḥ /
na punaḥ kalpasūtroktaṃ1 (vidhipūrvakam) / vidhiṃ te na jānanti // 23
//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even those'—even those who are devotees of other deities, who worship with faith—they worship and honor. They too, in reality, worship Me alone. But how? Not in the proper manner—meaning, without the method [leading to] the path of liberation. They do not know the [proper] method. (23)

children.text: kutaḥ punar evam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Why is that so?

children.text:
(ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca /
na tu mām abhijānanti tattvenātaś cyavanti te // BhG_9.24 //)
children.translated_text: (For I am the enjoyer and the lord of all sacrifices. But they do not know Me in truth; hence they fall.) (BhG 9.24)

children.text: ahaṃ hīti / ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānām tena tenendrādyātmanāvasthito2
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'For I'—for I, of all sacrifices, abiding in the form of this or that deity such as <s>Indra</s> and others,

children.text:
bhoktā ca prabhur eva (ca) / te punar na tu mām abhijānanti
(tattvena ta)thāvasthitam3 / ataś cyavanti te /
punarāvṛttiṃ bhajanta ity arthaḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: meaning they undergo return [to <s>saṃsāra</s>]. (24)
am the enjoyer and the lord as well. But they do not know Me in truth—as I truly abide. Therefore they fall—

children.text: etad eva darśayati ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He demonstrates this very point—

children.text:
(yānti devavratā devān pitṝn yānti pitṛvratāḥ /
bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti madyājino 'pi mām // BhG_9.25 //)
children.translated_text: (Worshippers of the gods go to the gods; worshippers of the ancestors go to the ancestors; worshippers of spirits go to the spirits; and My worshippers come to Me.) (BhG 9.25)

children.text:
yāntīti / yānti devavratāḥ / devānāṃ karma vratam (yeṣāṃ
te) / yathā kratur asmiṃl loke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'They go'—worshippers of the gods go [to them]. Those whose vow consists of the rituals for the gods are 'god-devoted.' 'As is one's will in this world, so does one become after departing from here'—

children.text:
iti śruteḥ / taṃ yathā yaś copāsate --- iti ca brāhmaṇam /
nigadavyākhyā / ata e(va) /
sarve māṃ yāji(naḥ) vāsudevā bhavanti // 25 //
children.translated_text: all who worship Me become [one with] <s>Vāsudeva</s>. (25)
so says the <s>śruti</s>. 'According to how and whom one worships'—thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text]. This is a plain explanation. Therefore,

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text:
1. kalpasūtroktaṃ vidhiṃ te na jānanti
2. tena tenaindrādyātmanāvasthito
3. tathāvāsthitam
children.translated_text: [Editorial notes with variant manuscript readings.]

children.text: (sā)phalyam anena ..... paṭha ... sādhyatvāt ... ārādhanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The fruitfulness [of devotion is shown] by this [...] because of being easily accomplished [...] He is to be worshipped.

children.text: katham ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How?

children.text:
(patraṃ puṇyaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati /
tad ahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ // BhG_9.26 //)
children.translated_text: (Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water—that offering of love from one of pure heart, I accept.) (BhG 9.26)

children.text:
patraṃ puṣpam iti / vilvādipatram / puṣpaṃ karavīrādi /
badarāmrādi phalam / kṛtārthaṃ me janmeti snehārdrahṛdayo yo me
prayacchati tad aham upahṛtaṃ gṛhītvāśnāmi tṛpyāmi
śraddhābuddheḥ // 26 //
children.translated_text: by [the offering of] one of faithful mind. (26)

[Commentary:] 'A leaf, a flower'—a leaf of <s>bilva</s> and the like; a flower of <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) and the like; a fruit of jujube, mango, and the like. One who, with a heart moistened by affection [thinking] 'my birth is fulfilled,' offers to Me—that, having received what is offered, I eat, I am satisfied,

children.text: yata evam ataḥ ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since this is so, therefore—

children.text:
(yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi yaj juhoṣi dadāsi yat /
yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva madarpaṇam // BhG_9.27 //)
children.translated_text: (Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practice, O <s>Kaunteya</s>—do that as an offering to Me.) (BhG 9.27)

children.text:
yad iti / yat karoṣi snānādi / yad aśnāsi bhojanakāle /
prāṇāhutiḥ homo nirdiśyate / yaj juhoṣi bāhye 'gnau dadāsi
hiraṇyādi / yat tapasyasy upavāsādi (karoṣi) / tat sarvaṃ
madarpaṇaṃ kuru // 27 //
children.translated_text: do as an offering to Me. (27)

[Commentary:] 'Whatever'—whatever you do, such as bathing and the like; whatever you eat at mealtime; the oblation to the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is indicated as sacrifice; whatever you offer in the external fire; whatever you give—gold and the like; whatever austerity you practice—fasting and the like—all that,

children.text: śruṇu tataḥ phalam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Hear then the fruit—

children.text:
(śubhāśubhaphalair evaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ /
sannyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto mām upaiṣyasi // BhG_9.28 //)
children.translated_text: (Thus you shall be freed from the bonds of action, which bear good and evil fruits. With your self united through the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation, liberated, you shall come to Me.) (BhG 9.28)

children.text:
śubheti / śubhāśubhāni phalāni yeṣāṃ karmabandhanānām /
karmāṇy eva bandhanāni / tair vimucyase /
vimuktaś ca sannyāsayogayuktātmā / sannyāsaḥ kṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ
brahmaṇi samarpaṇam / tad eva
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Good and evil'—good and evil are the fruits of the bonds of action. Actions themselves are the bonds. From these you shall be freed. And having been freed, with your self united through the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation. <s>Sannyāsa</s> (renunciation) is the offering of performed actions to <s>Brahman</s>. That very

children.text: kartṛkarmaphalaṃ cety abhedabhāvanā yogaḥ / tābhyāṃ yukta ātmā
yasyāsau sannyāsayoga(yukt)ātmā mām upeṣyasi // 28 //

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [thinking] 'the doer, the action, and the fruit [are all <s>Brahman</s>]'—this contemplation of non-difference is <s>yoga</s>. One whose self is united by these two is one of 'a self united through the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation'—you shall come to Me. (28)

children.text:
nanu yas tvayi samarpaṇaṃ karoti sa eva cet tvām upaiti
rāgādimāṃs tarhi bhavān yathā loke rājā bhajamānasyopakaroti
netarasyety āśaṅkyāha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, if one who offers to You alone attains You, then You would be partial — just as in the world a king helps only one who serves him and not another — anticipating this objection, he says:

children.text:
(samohaṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo 'sti na priyaḥ /
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpy aham // BhG_9.29 //)
children.translated_text: I am equal to all beings; none is hateful or dear to Me. But those who worship Me with devotion — they are in Me, and I too am in them. // BhG 9.29 //

children.text:
samoham iti / samohaṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me rāgadveṣau / yo bhaktyā
māṃ bhajate tasyānugrahaṃ kartuṃ mama svabhāvaḥ yathāgniḥ
samyag bhajamānasya śītādyapanodaṃ karoti netarasya / ato ye
bhajanti tu bhaktyā sevante (mām) āśrayante teṣv ahaṃ varte /
nātra rāgadveṣau kāraṇam / api tu
prāṇikarmānurūpaphalapradarśanenāgnivadanugṛhṇāmīty
abhiprāyaḥ // 29 //

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'I am equal' — I am equal to all beings; I have neither attachment nor aversion. One who worships Me with devotion — it is My nature to bestow grace upon him, just as fire removes cold and the like for one who properly tends it, but not for another. Therefore, those who worship Me with devotion — who serve and take refuge in Me — I abide in them. Attachment and aversion are not the cause here. Rather, just as fire, I show fruits corresponding to the actions of beings — this is the intent. // 29 //

children.text:
idānīṃ vṛttādinirākaraṇenāpi bhagavadāśrayaṇastutyartham
arthavādakathanaṃ kriyate / vṛttam apy atra tantram ity āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement) is made for the purpose of praising taking refuge in the Lord, even by setting aside [considerations of] conduct and the like. What constitutes the essential teaching (<s>tantra</s>) here is stated:

children.text:
(api cet sudurācāro bhajate mām ananyabhāk /
sādhur eva sa mantavyaḥ samyag vyavasito hi saḥ // BhG_9.30 //)
children.translated_text: Even if a person of extremely wicked conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, he is to be regarded as righteous, for he has rightly resolved. // BhG 9.30 //

children.text: apīti / suṣṭhu bhṛśaṃ1 ced durācāraḥ so 'pi sādhur eva
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even if' — even if one is of exceedingly wicked conduct, he is to be regarded as righteous.

children.text:
mantavyaḥ / kasmāt / samyag vyavasitaḥ suniścitabuddhiḥ sanmārgam
āsthito yataḥ / hiśabdo hetau // 30 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because he has rightly resolved — he is of firmly established intellect, having taken the righteous path. The word 'hi' indicates a reason. // 30 //

children.text: NOTES:
children.translated_text: [NOTES — variant readings]

children.text: 1. dṛśaṃ
children.translated_text: [Variant readings for preceding text.]

children.text: ayaṃ (pu)naḥ ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, this [person] —

children.text:
(kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvac chāntiṃ nigacchati /
kaunteya pratijānīhi na madbhaktaḥ praṇaśyati // BhG_9.31 //)
children.translated_text: He quickly becomes a righteous soul and attains eternal peace. O <s>Kaunteya</s>, declare that My devotee never perishes. // BhG 9.31 //

children.text:
kṣipram iti / .... ṭi .... pāpakṣayāt / śaśvad iti kriyāvi(śeṣaṇam)
ni(rga)cchatīty arthaḥ / tad etad vastu pratijānīhi / na me
(bhaktaḥ praṇaśya)tīti // 31 //
children.translated_text: perish.' // 31 //
[Commentary:] 'Quickly' — ... due to the destruction of sins. 'Eternally' is an adverb modifying 'attains' — that is the meaning. Declare this truth: 'My devotee does not

children.text:
idānīṃ ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā --- iti yad bhagavatsevanaṃ
prakrāntaṃ tatra śraddhābhaktibhyāṃ
bhagavadvyapāśrayaṇaprarovanārtham
apy arthavādam āha ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, regarding what was stated — 'those who worship Me with devotion' — in order to encourage taking refuge in the Lord through faith and devotion, he states another <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement):

children.text:
(māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye 'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ /
striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās te 'pi yānti parāṃ gatim // BhG_9.32 //)
children.translated_text: For those who take refuge in Me, O <s>Pārtha</s>, even those of sinful birth — women, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> — they too attain the supreme goal. // BhG 9.32 //

children.text:
mām iti / he pārtha māṃ vyapāśritya viśeṣeṇa śaraṇatvenāśritya
ye 'pi pāpayonayo bhavanti / pāpād yonir janma yeṣāṃ te pāpayonayaḥ
kutsitajanmānaḥ stryādayo ye 'tyantam apavarge 'nadhikṛtās te 'pi
svakarmānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇena madājñāsampādanena pāpakṣayāt
paramāṃ
prakṛṣṭām uttamāṃ svargalakṣaṇāṃ gatiṃ yānti prāpnuvantīti
sambhāvyate / matsamparko hi śu(ddhikāraṇam analasamparka iva lauhasya /
svakarmaṇā (māṃ) sevasveti1 / svakarmaṇaivārādhanasya vidhānāt
pratyutthānātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam iti pratyutthānena
children.translated_text: the duty of a <s>Śūdra</s> too, which is innate — consisting of rising in respect and attendance — through such service with one's own duty,

children.text: paricaryātmakena svakarmaṇā tam evārthasiddhiṃ vindati mānava iti /
children.translated_text: 'a person attains that very fulfillment of purpose' — thus,

children.text: tadanuṣṭhānenaiva puruṣārthasiddher vidhāsyamānatvāt // 32 //
children.translated_text: because the fulfillment of the human goal will be enjoined through the performance of that very [duty]. // 32 //

[Commentary:] 'Me' — O <s>Pārtha</s>, having taken special refuge in Me — having resorted to Me as shelter — those who are of sinful birth — those whose birth arises from sin, i.e., those of lowly birth — women and others who are absolutely unqualified for <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) — they too, through the performance of their own prescribed duties, which constitutes the fulfillment of My command, and through the destruction of sins thereby, attain the supreme, excellent, highest goal characterized by heaven — this is to be understood. For contact with Me is the cause of purification, just as contact with fire [purifies] iron. 'Worship Me through your own duty' — since worship through one's own duty alone is enjoined,
