children.text: arthavādatātparyam upasaṃharann āha1 ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Summing up the purport of the <s>arthavāda</s>, he says:

children.text:
(kiṃ punar brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayas tathā /
anityam asukhaṃ lokam imaṃ prapya bhajasva mām // BhG_9.33 //)
children.translated_text: How much more then holy <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and devoted royal sages! Having obtained this impermanent and joyless world, worship Me. // BhG 9.33 //

children.text:
kim iti / bhagavaccharaṇagatā anadhikṛtāḥ stryādayo 'py utkṛṣṭāṃ
gatiṃ gacchanti / kiṃ punar ye śuddhayonayo 'dhikṛtā
brāhmaṇarājarṣayaś
ca te na yāsyantīti / apiśabdena sambhāvanārthenātiśayoktyā
brāhmaṇādīnāṃ jñānaprarocanānena kriyate na tu yathāśruto 'rtho
vidhīyate / yathā --- api parvataṃ śirasā bhindyāt api droṇapākaṃ
bhuñjīta --- ity anena vākyena puruṣaśaktiśraddhānaṃ kriyate na tu
(pa)rvatabhe(daḥ) pratipādyata aśakyatvāt / na hi parvataṃ bhindyād
ity asyānyaparatvāt svārthātātparyāt tatra pravṛttiḥ / na hi
vidhivihitasyārthasya stutyā droṇapākasya pratiṣiddhasya
duṣṭasya nindayā nivṛttiḥ /
na tu viṣabhakṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ svārthaṃ pratipādyate / ataś ca
jaiminir arthavādalakṣaṇasūtraṃ2 praṇītavān --- vidhinā tv
ekavākyatvāt stutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syur iti / arthavādāḥ
kila vidhyekavākyatayā vidhiśeṣatvena niṣedhaśeṣatvena ca
tatstutyarthās tannindārthā vā bhaveyur ity arthaḥ /
arthavādavākyānāṃ padārthatvāt svārthe ca tātparyā(bhāvā)d
anyaparatvāc ceti / tathā ca bhaṭṭapādair evoktam ---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'How much more' — if even unqualified persons such as women and others, who have taken refuge in the Lord, attain an exalted destination, how much more so those of pure birth who are qualified — <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and royal sages — will they not attain it? By the particle 'api' in the sense of possibility, an <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is employed to encourage the knowledge of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and others. The meaning is not to be taken literally. Just as — 'one might even split a mountain with one's head; one might even consume a <s>droṇa</s>-measure of food' — by this statement, confidence in a person's power is generated, not that the splitting of a mountain is actually taught, since it is impossible. For the statement 'one might split a mountain' does not have that as its real purport, since its intent is something else. Neither does praise of what is enjoined cause engagement, nor does blame of a prohibited and sinful act like consuming a <s>droṇa</s>-measure cause cessation. Nor is the literal meaning of consuming poison being taught. Therefore <s>Jaimini</s> composed the aphorism defining <s>arthavāda</s>: 'But since they form a single sentence with the injunction, they serve the purpose of praising the injunctions.' <s>Arthavādas</s>, being part of the same sentence as injunctions, serve as supplements to injunctions and prohibitions — their purpose is either to praise or to blame — this is the meaning. Since <s>arthavāda</s> sentences are [merely] words, and since there is no independent purport in their literal meaning, and since their intent points to something else. And so <s>Bhaṭṭapāda</s> (<s>Kumārila</s>) himself has said:

children.text:
vyākhyeyād guṇavādena yo 'rthavādād atatparāt /
arthe 'dhigantum iṣyeta kathaṃ syāt tasya satyatā // iti /
children.translated_text: 'One who seeks to ascertain meaning from an <s>arthavāda</s> that is not independently authoritative, by interpreting it as a <s>guṇavāda</s> (subsidiary statement) — how can there be truth in that?'

children.text:
tathā ca śrutau --- paśuyāge3 vapāhomaḥ kartavya iti /
asya vidher avaśyānuṣṭhānāyārthavādavākyam ---
prajāpatir vapām udakhidata
children.translated_text: And likewise in <s>śruti</s>: 'In the animal sacrifice, the <s>vapā</s> (omental offering) must be offered' — this is the injunction. For the purpose of its obligatory performance, the <s>arthavāda</s> statement is: '<s>Prajāpati</s> extracted the <s>vapā</s>.'

eva vāpam utkhidya vapāhomo 'nuṣṭhita iti paśuyāgavidher
avaśyakartavyatve
vapotkhananam adhyāropitaṃ prarocanārtham /
loke 'py anabhipretaduṣṭapuruṣagṛhabhojananivṛttyarthaṃ
kaścid bravīti --- varaṃ viṣaṃ bhakṣya mā cāsya gṛhe bhuṅkthā iti
anenāpi laukikenārthavādavākyena na viṣabhakṣaṇalakṣaṇaḥ2 svārtho
vidhīyata api tu atiśayoktyā (ta)d gehabhojananivṛttiḥ kriyate /
... niṣiddha ...... /
children.translated_text: and performed the <s>vapā</s> offering — this is superimposed on the obligatory nature of the animal-sacrifice injunction for the purpose of encouragement. Even in the world, in order to prevent someone from eating at the house of a disreputable, wicked person, someone says: 'Better to eat poison than to eat at his house!' By this worldly <s>arthavāda</s> statement too, the literal meaning of eating poison is not being enjoined; rather, through hyperbole, cessation from eating at that house is being effected. ... prohibited ...
The meaning of that is: thus indeed the sacrificer must necessarily perform the <s>vapā</s> offering.
